This role defines compensation strategy for large, complex employee populations while ensuring programs are competitive, scalable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. 

As the organization's subject matter expert for manufacturing and operations compensation, the Director partners closely with business leaders, Px Business Partners, Finance, and Legal to design compensation programs that enable business growth, talent attraction, workforce scalability, and operational excellence. 

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in manufacturing compensation strategy, non-exempt workforce design, market intelligence, and executive consulting, with a demonstrated ability to influence enterprise decisions and build compensation frameworks that support rapidly growing operations.

lists.content:
Compensation Strategy & Enterprise Leadership 
  • Develop and lead the compensation strategy supporting Aircraft manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades populations.  
  • Serve as the SME on manufacturing and operations compensation, shaping long-term compensation philosophy and governance.  
  • Partner with business leadership to align compensation strategy with business growth, workforce planning, organizational design, and operational priorities.  
  • Drive compensation initiatives supporting facility expansions, new business models, geographic growth, and workforce transformation.  
    • Manufacturing & Operations Compensation 
  • Lead the design and evolution of compensation structures supporting large non-exempt employee populations.  
  • Establish wage structures, geographic differentials, shift premium strategies, progression frameworks, and other compensation programs that balance external competitiveness with internal equity.  
  • Oversee market pricing methodologies utilizing Radford, Mercer, WTW, and specialized manufacturing compensation surveys alongside complementary market intelligence.  
  • Develop innovative compensation approaches to attract and retain highly competitive manufacturing, technical, and operational talent. 
    • Executive Partnership & Business Consulting 
  • Serve as the trusted compensation advisor to Aircraft executives and business leaders.  
  • Consult on organization design, workforce investments, location strategy, and talent acquisition decisions with significant financial and organizational impact in partnership with the Px Business Partner.  
  • Provide strategic guidance on compensation implications of organizational changes, acquisitions, new facilities, and business expansion.  
  • Present compensation recommendations and analyses to executive leadership with clear business rationale and risk assessments.  
    • Compensation Analytics & Insights 
  • Lead enterprise compensation analyses including market competitiveness, pay equity, workforce cost modeling, and incentive effectiveness.  
  • Translate complex compensation data into actionable insights for executive stakeholders.  
  • Anticipate market trends and proactively recommend compensation strategies that strengthen organizational competitiveness.  
    • Governance, Compliance & Program Excellence 
  • Establish governance frameworks, policies, and administration standards for manufacturing compensation programs.  
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local wage and hour regulations while mitigating organizational risk.  
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, and People Operations on complex compensation matters and regulatory changes.  
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives to simplify compensation processes, improve scalability, and enhance operational efficiency. 
    • Leadership 
  • Champion best practices in compensation design, analytics, governance, and operational excellence.  
  • Build organizational capability through knowledge sharing, coaching, and development of compensation expertise across the People function.

• Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Finance, Business, Economics, or a related field.  
  • 15+ years of progressive compensation experience, including significant leadership supporting manufacturing, production, operations, or supply chain organizations.  
  • Deep expertise designing enterprise compensation strategies for large non-exempt employee populations.  
  • Extensive knowledge of wage and hour regulations, compensation governance, and manufacturing compensation practices.
  • Demonstrated experience designing wage structures, progression frameworks, geographic differentials, and premium pay programs.  
  • Advanced analytical, financial modeling, and executive presentation skills.  
  • Proven ability to influence senior executives and drive enterprise-wide compensation decisions.  
  • Experience leading large, cross-functional compensation initiatives with significant organizational impact.

• Certified Compensation Professional (CCP).  
  • Experience supporting both union and non-union manufacturing environments.  
  • Experience within global manufacturing or advanced technology organizations.  
  • Expertise utilizing Radford, Mercer, WTW, and specialized manufacturing compensation surveys.  
  • Experience with Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, or enterprise compensation planning systems.  
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement experience. 
  • Experience leading or mentoring compensation professionals.

lists.content:
• Design and implement novel computer vision algorithms from scratch, optimised for real-time performance.

  • Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Previous Defence experience is highly desirable.

• Build mission-critical vision and autonomy systems that make a real-world impact.
  • Collaborate with some of the best minds in AI, autonomy, and defence technology.

Job Description:

Job Description:

The Configuration and Change Control Manager is a senior individual contributor responsible for owning configuration discipline for the fielded V-BAT fleet, including aircraft, payloads, software, ground equipment, support equipment, and customer-specific configurations.This role ensures Shield AI maintains an accurate, traceable, and controlled understanding of what hardware, software, payload, and ground system configurations are deployed, which changes apply to which aircraft or customers, and how approved fixes, retrofits, releases, and service actions are controlled through execution.This position is critical to preventing configuration confusion across aircraft serial numbers, hardware revisions, software versions, payload variants, ground equipment configurations, fielded modifications, maintenance releases, and customer-specific baselines. The Configuration and Change Control Manager partners closely with Fleet Support, Sustainment Engineering, Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Success, Operations, and Configuration Management to ensure changes are documented, approved, communicated, traceable, and deployed to the correct assets.The role requires strong process discipline, technical fluency, attention to detail, and the ability to drive cross-functional accountability without direct authority.

lists.content:
• Own and maintain the V-BAT fielded and as-maintained configuration baseline for aircraft, payloads, software, ground equipment, support equipment, and related sustainment assets.
  • Track aircraft serial numbers, hardware revisions, software versions, payload configurations, ground system configurations, fielded modifications, retrofit status, and customer-specific baselines.
  • Manage the change control process for fielded V-BAT systems, ensuring approved changes are controlled, traceable, and applied to the correct aircraft, customers, and configurations.
  • Support Engineering Change Requests, Engineering Change Orders, change impact assessments, release readiness reviews, retrofit plans, and service action planning.
  • Ensure fielded fixes, retrofits, software updates, hardware changes, payload changes, and service actions are tied to the correct serial numbers, configurations, customers, and effectivity ranges.
  • Maintain configuration records for deployed aircraft, spares, payloads, ground equipment, support equipment, and field-modified assets.
  • Partner with Fleet Support, Sustainment Engineering, Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Success, Operations, and Configuration Management to control changes across the V-BAT fleet.
  • Support release readiness reviews for software, hardware, payload, ground system, maintenance, and support equipment updates.
  • Ensure changes are documented, approved, communicated, implemented, and traceable from engineering approval through field deployment.
  • Maintain a clear view of which customers, aircraft, payloads, ground systems, spares, and support equipment are affected by each change.
  • Define and maintain change effectivity logic, including serial number applicability, build applicability, customer applicability, configuration applicability, and retrofit applicability.
  • Coordinate with Product Engineering and Sustainment Engineering to understand technical change intent, required implementation steps, and field impact.
  • Coordinate with Fleet Support and Customer Success to ensure field teams understand which updates, inspections, retrofits, or service actions apply to each customer asset.
  • Coordinate with Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain to ensure production records, nonconformance records, part revisions, supplier changes, and field configurations remain aligned.
  • Identify configuration gaps, data inconsistencies, undocumented modifications, incomplete retrofit records, and risks to fielded fleet traceability.
  • Escalate configuration risks that could affect fleet readiness, customer support, release execution, repair decisions, or technical troubleshooting.
  • Support audits, reviews, and investigations requiring accurate configuration history, change history, serial number traceability, or fielded asset applicability.
  • Improve configuration management processes, change control mechanisms, release tracking, field modification tracking, and reporting tools as the sustainment function scales.
  • Provide leadership updates on configuration health, change control status, open risks, affected assets, and field deployment progress.

• 4+ years of experience in configuration management, change control, aviation sustainment, hardware/software product support, manufacturing operations, product lifecycle management, engineering operations, or complex hardware sustainment.
  • Demonstrated experience managing configuration baselines, revision control, change effectivity, fielded asset records, engineering change processes, or product release control in a complex technical environment.
  • Strong understanding of configuration baselines, as-built records, as-maintained records, revision control, serial number traceability, effectivity management, and engineering change control.
  • Experience supporting Engineering Change Requests, Engineering Change Orders, release readiness reviews, retrofit planning, service actions, or fielded product updates.
  • Experience tracking or managing hardware revisions, software versions, payload configurations, ground equipment configurations, customer-specific configurations, or deployed asset baselines.
  • Ability to determine which aircraft, systems, customers, configurations, or serial numbers are affected by a given change, issue, release, retrofit, or service action.
  • Experience working across Product Engineering, Sustainment Engineering, Fleet Support, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, Customer Success, and Configuration Management teams.
  • Strong technical fluency with bills of material, part revisions, drawings, software releases, hardware changes, configuration records, product structures, or fielded system documentation.
  • Strong process discipline and attention to detail, with the ability to maintain accurate records across multiple systems, stakeholders, and changing priorities.
  • Ability to identify configuration risks, traceability gaps, undocumented changes, incomplete records, and process breakdowns before they affect fleet readiness or customer support.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly communicate change applicability, implementation status, configuration risks, and decision needs.
  • Ability to operate independently as a senior IC and drive cross-functional accountability without direct authority.
  • Ability to balance configuration rigor with field support urgency, release timelines, customer needs, and operational realities.
  • Ability to possess a Secret DoD security clearance as required by customers.

• Experience with aviation, defense, unmanned systems, robotics, aerospace manufacturing, complex hardware/software products, or deployed technical systems.
  • Familiarity with PLM, ERP, MES, CMMS, service management systems, requirements systems, software release systems, or configuration management databases.
  • Experience with aircraft serial number tracking, software release management, payload configuration management, ground system configuration, depot repair records, or field modification tracking.
  • Experience with ECO/ECR processes, MRB, FRACAS, RCCA, service bulletins, maintenance releases, retrofit campaigns, or fleet-wide service actions.
  • Familiarity with configuration audits, physical configuration audits, functional configuration audits, controlled baselines, product structures, or digital thread concepts.
  • Experience supporting military, defense, aviation, or high-reliability customer environments where configuration accuracy affects safety, readiness, supportability, or contractual commitments.
  • Experience working in a startup, high-growth, defense technology, aerospace, robotics, or advanced manufacturing environment.
  • CM2, CMII, PMP, Lean Six Sigma, APICS, aviation maintenance, systems engineering, or related certification preferred but not required.

Job Description:
This role will serve as the owner's representative responsible for leading facility planning, programming, design development, and project delivery for manufacturing, engineering, laboratory, office, and secure facility projects.
This position is heavily focused on design management and will be responsible for directing external architecture and engineering (A&E) firms throughout the entire project lifecycle. The successful candidate will lead stakeholder engagement, requirements development, programming, consultant management, design reviews, constructability reviews, and technical decision-making while ensuring designs align with operational objectives, budget constraints, schedule requirements, security requirements, and long-term facility strategies.
The ideal candidate thrives in environments where requirements are evolving and can effectively guide design teams through ambiguity to produce practical, constructible, and scalable solutions. Construction oversight is expected, but the primary focus of this role is ensuring design quality, design coordination, and successful project definition before construction begins.

  • Support permitting, entitlement, and regulatory approval efforts.
  • Provide technical leadership during procurement, contractor selection, and project execution activities.

  • Utilize AutoCAD to review, coordinate, and comment on design documentation.

  • Experience leading multidisciplinary design teams through all phases of project development.
  • Ability to review and interpret architectural and engineering drawings, specifications, calculations, and technical documentation.
  • Working knowledge of building systems, construction methods, codes, and industry best practices.
  • Proficiency with AutoCAD.
  • Experience supporting projects in active operational environments, including aviation or airfield facilities.

  • Ability to lift 50 pounds or greater and perform site visits in active construction environments.

  • Experience with SCIF planning, design, and accreditation processes.
  • Experience delivering projects using design-build, progressive design-build, or fast-track delivery methods.
  • Professional registration or certification such as PE, RA, PMP, CCM, LEED, or similar.

Job Description: 

We are seeking a Director, Legal to provide hands-on legal leadership across four core areas: (i) product counseling; (ii) marketing, AI governance and privacy; (iii) public-company readiness, including building the technology and software development compliance processes and policies, such as open source software, AI and other authorized usage policies; and (iv) general corporate project work, including helping manage employment matters and litigation. The goal is to help the business move at the speed of the mission while managing risk in a highly regulated environment. 
 
This is a builder’s role in one of the fastest-moving defense technology companies in the world. You will be a primary legal partner to the teams that build, ship and sell Hivemind and Shield AI’s other software, and to People Experience (PX), Marketing and IT. You will stand up the programs, policies and playbooks that let those teams launch products, run campaigns, adopt AI, and you will be accountable for making Legal an enabler of rapid development and growth. 
 
Three qualities are non-negotiable: 
Executive and external credibility. You must have the presence, judgment and technical fluency to advise C-suite and executive leaders directly, and to represent Shield AI with confidence to partners, customers and outside counsel on AI, software, data and product questions.
Action orientation under shifting priorities. You must be able to run many projects and workflows at once, move quickly on urgent requests, re-prioritize without losing track of anything, and see matters through from intake to completion. In Shield AI’s words: be rigorous and go fast.
Practical, needs-driven program building. You must understand what product, engineering, marketing and PX teams actually need, and then proactively build scalable processes, policies and self-serve guidance that meet those needs, while doing what honor dictates when the answer is hard. 
The role is on-site at one of the Shield AI offices listed above. You will report to the Senior Director, Legal, who leads legal support for PX, Marketing, IT and many aspects of the Hivemind software business, including partnerships. You will work closely with the Chief Legal Officer and the broader Legal and Security teams, with opportunities to mentor attorneys and legal professionals, and manage outside counsel as the business expands.

  • Translate evolving AI frameworks into practical requirements, including the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, U.S. federal and state AI laws, and U.S. Department of Defense policy on responsible AI and autonomy in weapon systems.
  • Advise IT, Security and enterprise teams on AI vendor and model-provider agreements, AI tool procurement, data processing terms and agentic AI use cases.
  • Develop and run key parts of the privacy program, including privacy-by-design reviews, privacy notices, data processing agreements, cross-border data transfers, data mapping and data subject requests, under GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA and the laws of other countries where Shield AI operates. 
  • Partner with PX and IT on employee and candidate data, data sensitivity labeling and data governance across enterprise systems, and develop standard responses to recurring customer AI, privacy and security questionnaires. 
    Technology and company compliance programs
  • Help prepare the Legal team and the business for larger company maturity and scrutiny by designing, documenting and putting into practice the technology and software development policies, processes and controls a public company is expected to have.
  • Build and scale Shield AI’s open source software compliance program, including policy, intake and approval workflows, license review (e.g., GPL, LGPL, AGPL, Apache, MIT), software bill of materials (SBOM) and software composition analysis tooling with Engineering and Security, remediation, and an outbound contribution policy.
  • Develop, roll out and maintain AI policies and authorized and acceptable use policies, including internal AI use, IT and data use, and customer-facing acceptable use terms for Hivemind and other software products, including terms governing customers’ AI and agentic systems.
  • Partner with Finance, Internal Audit, IT and Security to provide legal input on controls and certifications that support public-company and customer requirements (e.g., SOX IT general controls, ISO 27001, CMMC), and set up policy governance, including owners, review cadence, attestations and training.
  • Get IP and technology records ready for diligence, including IP chain of title, inventories of inbound licenses and third-party software and data, contract repository hygiene, and input on disclosures about AI, privacy, cybersecurity and IP risk.
  • Train teammates on new policies and processes so that compliance is built into how engineering, product and business teams work every day. 
    • General corporate, employment and litigation 
  • Partner with PX and employment counsel on employment matters, including workplace investigations, separations and releases, restrictive covenants, contractor classification, handbook and policy updates, and multi-state and international employment questions as Shield AI expands globally.
  • Help manage litigation, arbitration and pre-litigation disputes with outside counsel, including case strategy, budgets, legal holds, demand letters, and IP and commercial disputes, at the direction of the Senior Director, Legal and the Chief Legal Officer.
  • Support corporate projects, including M&A due diligence and post-close integration, strategic partnerships and investments, Board and executive materials on topics within this role’s scope, and special initiatives as assigned.
  • Be a good steward of resources: manage outside counsel and legal spend efficiently, holding firms to clear scopes, budgets and outcomes. 
    • Collaboration, execution and leadership 
  • Work confidently and collaboratively with C-suite and executive leaders, business unit leaders, engineers and operators, as well as external partners, customers, government stakeholders and outside counsel, adjusting communication style to the audience.
  • Manage multiple concurrent projects and workflows, often with urgency, and quickly re-prioritize as business needs, deal timelines and urgent requests shift.
  • Take ownership of matters from intake to completion, anticipate next steps, escalate issues early with clear options, trade-offs and recommendations, and follow through.
  • Mentor and develop attorneys and legal professionals, and help build and scale the team that supports PX, Marketing, IT/AI and the Hivemind business.
  • Build and improve templates, playbooks and trackers, and use legal technology and AI-enabled tools to increase speed, consistency and quality.
  • Handle highly confidential, sensitive and export-controlled information with discretion and professionalism.

• Experience supporting a large, fast-growing private company through multiple phases of late venture to public company or larger private company maturity.
  • Experience in AI/ML, autonomy, robotics, aerospace/aviation or dual-use technologies, and familiarity with defense and government contracting requirements such as ITAR/EAR, DFARS data rights, FedRAMP and CMMC.
  • Privacy or AI governance certification, such as CIPP/US, CIPP/E or AIGP.
  • Experience with M&A due diligence and post-close integration, including integrating acquired products and teams.
  • Experience with international operations across Europe, the Middle East or Asia-Pacific.
  • Experience building and mentoring legal teams and deploying AI-enabled legal tools and processes.

• J.D. from an accredited law school; active membership in at least one U.S. state bar.
  • 12+ years of legal experience, including substantial in-house experience as product counsel at a high-growth technology, software, AI, aerospace or defense company; experience at a leading law firm is a plus.
  • Deep experience in product counseling and technology transactions, including software licensing and distribution across on-premises, SaaS, embedded, OEM and channel models, and strategic technology partnerships.
  • Demonstrated experience building or running privacy and AI governance programs, with working knowledge of GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, the EU AI Act and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
  • Hands-on experience building or running an open source software compliance program and drafting technology policies, such as acceptable use and AI use policies.
  • Experience advising marketing and communications teams on advertising, promotions and public claims.
  • Working knowledge of employment law and experience managing litigation and disputes with outside counsel.
  • Executive presence and communication skills to advise C-suite executives and senior leaders and to represent the company credibly with external partners and customers.
  • Highly action-oriented, with a track record of managing many projects and workflows at once and delivering quickly on urgent and frequently shifting priorities.
  • Comfort operating at both strategic and tactical levels in a lean, high-tempo environment, with a practical, risk-based approach that enables the business.

Job Description: 

We are seeking a Director, Legal to provide hands-on legal leadership across four core areas: (i) product counseling; (ii) marketing, AI governance and privacy; (iii) public-company readiness, including building the technology and software development compliance processes and policies, such as open source software, AI and other authorized usage policies; and (iv) general corporate project work, including helping manage employment matters and litigation. The goal is to help the business move at the speed of the mission while managing risk in a highly regulated environment. 
 
This is a builder’s role in one of the fastest-moving defense technology companies in the world. You will be a primary legal partner to the teams that build, ship and sell Hivemind and Shield AI’s other software, and to People Experience (PX), Marketing and IT. You will stand up the programs, policies and playbooks that let those teams launch products, run campaigns, adopt AI, and you will be accountable for making Legal an enabler of rapid development and growth. 
 
Three qualities are non-negotiable: 
  • Executive and external credibility. You must have the presence, judgment and technical fluency to advise C-suite and executive leaders directly, and to represent Shield AI with confidence to partners, customers and outside counsel on AI, software, data and product questions.
  • Action orientation under shifting priorities. You must be able to run many projects and workflows at once, move quickly on urgent requests, re-prioritize without losing track of anything, and see matters through from intake to completion. In Shield AI’s words: be rigorous and go fast.
  • Practical, needs-driven program building. You must understand what product, engineering, marketing and PX teams actually need, and then proactively build scalable processes, policies and self-serve guidance that meet those needs, while doing what honor dictates when the answer is hard. 
The role is on-site at one of the Shield AI offices listed above. You will report to the Senior Director, Legal, who leads legal support for PX, Marketing, IT and many aspects of the Hivemind software business, including partnerships. You will work closely with the Chief Legal Officer and the broader Legal and Security teams, with opportunities to mentor attorneys and legal professionals, and manage outside counsel as the business expands.

Job Description:
Shield AI builds intelligent systems that protect service members and civilians. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software and V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and our teams support customers and operations across the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. 
Shield AI is hiring a Senior Customer Sustainment Engineer to support Hivemind systems after they reach customers and operational teams. This role sits at the intersection of customer support, systems troubleshooting, and engineering. 
Customers and forward deployed employees bring valuable operational context when they report a mission interruption, update concern, or unexpected system behavior. You will work with them to translate that context into a clear technical problem by gathering the right evidence, understanding the operating environment, narrowing the likely causes, and identifying the best path to resolution. 
Some issues will be resolved through configuration changes, deployment corrections, known workarounds, or better guidance. Others will require a product or engineering change. In either case, you will stay with the issue through resolution, keep the customer informed, and make sure the outcome is captured for future use. 
The role is the primary owner for Tier 1 support, handles a meaningful portion of Tier 2 troubleshooting, and can contribute to limited Tier 3 investigation when deeper technical experience is useful. Using DoD sustainment language, this is roughly the software equivalent of intermediate-level maintenance: resolve what can be addressed at that level, identify what needs depot-level repair, and provide engineering with a complete technical handoff. Product Support and core engineering teams provide the depot-level repair capability, while this role stays engaged to validate the result and close the loop with the customer. 
You will work closely with Forward Deployment Engineering, Product Support Engineering, Operations & Sustainment, Product, Program, Licensing, and the core Hivemind engineering teams. The goal is straightforward: help customers return to mission-ready operation while making Hivemind easier to support over time.

lists.content:
• Own Tier 1 customer support and incident coordination from initial report through confirmed resolution. 

  • Gather the information needed to understand an issue, including mission impact, software version, configuration, deployment state, logs, telemetry, screenshots, network context, and reproduction steps. 

  • Troubleshoot Hivemind software, APIs, licensing and provisioning, deployments, configurations, networks, operator workflows, and partner or OEM integrations. 

  • Separate product defects from configuration problems, environmental differences, integration issues, training needs, and feature requests. 

  • Resolve common technical problems, handle appropriate Tier 2 investigations, and reproduce more complex failures in lab, simulation, or representative test environments. 

  • Recognize issues that require Tier 3 or depot-level product repair and give engineering teams concise escalation packages that explain the impact, evidence, likely causes, work already attempted, and expected result. 

  • Provide customers with clear updates, practical next steps, and technically sound workarounds while investigations are in progress. 

  • Support software releases, upgrades, onboarding, licensing and provisioning workflows, and the transition from deployment into ongoing sustainment. 

  • Turn recurring issues into troubleshooting guides, known-issue records, diagnostic tools, training material, and product feedback. 

  • Use incident patterns to identify improvements to product reliability, diagnostics, documentation, and release readiness.

• Investigate a mission failure after a software update by comparing logs, configurations, versions, network behavior, telemetry, and release notes. 

  • Reproduce an autonomy, API, or integration issue and provide engineering with the evidence needed to correct it. 

  • Restore an offline customer environment affected by licensing, provisioning, time synchronization, or version compatibility. 

  • Coordinate the technical response to a high-impact customer issue and validate the workaround or fix before closure. 

  • Build a diagnostic playbook for recurring deployment, configuration, networking, or operator-workflow problems.

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical, military, field-engineering, or technical experience. 

  • 7+ years of hands-on experience supporting fielded, software-enabled systems in customer, operational, test, deployment, or sustainment environments. 

  • Experience with cyber-physical, edge, mission, robotics, autonomy, aviation, defense, industrial-control, or similarly complex deployed systems. 

  • Strong troubleshooting skills across software, Linux, configuration, networking, logs, telemetry, software versions, and hardware-adjacent interfaces. 

  • A record of owning technical issues from an incomplete initial report through diagnosis and resolution. 

  • Ability to read and reason about modern C++ and use existing Python, Bash, or similar scripts during troubleshooting and log analysis. 

  • Clear written and verbal communication with customers, operators, and engineering teams, including during time-sensitive situations. 

  • Ability to write useful incident records, troubleshooting guidance, engineering escalations, and customer-facing updates. 

  • Sound judgment when working within security, export-control, safety, customer-site, contractual, and data-handling requirements. 

  • Ability to possess a Secret DoD security clearance when required by customers.

• Experience with autonomy software, robotics, unmanned systems, aviation, defense or mission software, ground-control software, SDKs, APIs, or edge-deployed systems.
  • Experience supporting fleet operations, operational-readiness events, flight or ground test campaigns, or customer-site deployments.
  • Familiarity with DoD sustainment, intermediate- and depot-level maintenance concepts, or comparable field-to-engineering support models.
  • Hands-on software engineering experience writing and debugging C++ and developing Python scripts or tools for diagnostics, automation, or data analysis.
  • Familiarity with software releases, configuration baselines, upgrade validation, rollback, and version compatibility.
  • Experience with licensing, provisioning, offline or air-gapped environments, edge compute, time synchronization, networking, or telemetry analysis.
  • Experience with Jira, Azure DevOps, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, Confluence, or similar engineering and support tools.
  • Military, operator, maintainer, field-service, mission-support, or customer-engineering experience.
  • Active or prior security clearance. 
    •

After 90 days,
  • You can independently manage Tier 1 Hivemind support, resolve appropriate Tier 2 problems, and bring well-supported Tier 3 or depot-level cases to the appropriate engineering team. 
  • Customers and internal teams receive clear updates, practical next steps, and consistent follow-through. 
  • Your escalation packages allow engineering teams to begin useful work without repeating basic discovery. 
  • After 6 months 
  • Common field issues have repeatable diagnostics, workarounds, and support guidance. 
  • Forward Deployment Engineers and core engineers spend less time reconstructing customer problems because the evidence and technical qualification are already in place. 
  • Incident trends are leading to improvements in Hivemind reliability, supportability, documentation, and release readiness.

lists.content:
• Decompose, allocate and implement cyber security requirements into system architecture. 
  • Enforce network security architecture, ensuring compliance with cybersecurity standards and best practices.  
  • Develop documentation for installations and configurations required to obtain Authorizations to Operate (ATOs). 
  • Optimize secure network topologies, including segmentation, firewalls, VPNs, and zero-trust models. 
  • Collaborate with cybersecurity engineering to implement STIGs and develop Base Media solutions that enable execution of Plans of Actions and Milestones (POAMs) to mitigate cyber risks. 
  • Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to implement threat detection, mitigation, and incident response strategies. 
  • Provide technical insight on X-BAT GCS cybersecurity stack to cross-functional teams. 
  • Ensure system scalability, reliability, and performance through proactive design and monitoring strategies  
  • Support troubleshooting and resolution of complex network and infrastructure issues. 
  • Work with Network Engineering teams on implementing Voice Over IP Capabilities.

• This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD government clearance at the Secret level 
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related IT field 
  • 5+ years of experience in platform engineering, cybersecurity or network engineering roles  
  • Knowledge of network protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, etc.)  
  • Strong expertise in cybersecurity frameworks and protocols (Zero Trust, NIST SP 800-53 & 800-63B, ISO 27001, firewalls, IDS/IPS, encryption standards)  
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise networking hardware (routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers)  
  • Experience with cloud networking (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and hybrid environments  
  • Experience implementing Voice Over IP solutions.

• Industry certifications such as CCIE, CCNP, CISSP, or equivalent

descriptionPlain:
Job Description
Are you an experienced aircraft-development leader looking to help build a new class of autonomous combat aircraft? Are you energized by technically difficult problems, rapid execution, and the opportunity to redefine airpower? Shield AI may be the place for you.
The Deputy Chief Engineer for X-BAT will report to the Air Vehicle Lead / Chief Engineer X-BAT and serve as their primary technical deputy across the design, development, integration, test, and maturation of the X-BAT air vehicle.
This individual will help maintain the technical integrity of the aircraft while driving day-to-day engineering execution across structures, aerodynamics, propulsion, mechanical systems, avionics, electrical systems, flight controls, software, autonomy integration, manufacturing, and flight test.
The ideal candidate combines broad aircraft technical depth with strong systems thinking, sound engineering judgment, and a demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams through ambiguity. They must be comfortable moving between system-level decisions and detailed technical problem-solving while balancing performance, safety, cost, schedule, manufacturability, and mission requirements.
What You’ll Do
Serve as the primary technical deputy to the X-BAT Air Vehicle Lead, acting on their behalf when necessary and helping translate program objectives into clear engineering priorities.
Maintain the integrity of the air vehicle’s technical baseline, including system requirements, architecture, interfaces, configuration, performance, verification, and airworthiness evidence.
Lead the day-to-day integration of engineering activities across aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, mechanical systems, avionics, electrical systems, flight controls, software, autonomy, manufacturing, and test.
Drive aircraft-level technical decisions and trade studies, ensuring decisions are grounded in first-principles analysis and consider downstream effects on performance, safety, cost, schedule, producibility, maintainability, and operations.
Establish and maintain a disciplined technical-risk process, ensuring risks are identified early, assigned accountable owners, supported by mitigation plans, and retired through analysis or test.
Lead major technical and design reviews, ensuring the aircraft is sufficiently mature to progress through fabrication, ground test, flight test, qualification, and production.
Partner with Program Management to align technical scope with schedule, budget, staffing, supplier, and customer commitments.
Work closely with Manufacturing and Supply Chain to ensure designs are producible, scalable, and supported by a resilient supplier base.
Partner with Test and Flight Operations to define verification strategies, ground- and flight-test objectives, instrumentation requirements, test readiness criteria, and issue-resolution plans.
Lead rapid root-cause investigations and corrective actions for complex aircraft-level problems identified during integration, ground test, flight test, production, or operations.
Ensure technical decisions and engineering changes are documented, communicated, and reflected in the controlled product baseline.
Develop the technical leadership capabilities of engineering managers, functional leads, integrated product team leads, and senior individual contributors.
Communicate aircraft status, technical risks, decision recommendations, and recovery plans clearly to program leadership, executives, customers, and external partners.
Foster a culture of technical excellence, urgency, ownership, intellectual honesty, and constructive challenge.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
12+ years of progressive experience developing complex aircraft, military aerospace systems, autonomous aircraft, or similarly integrated aerospace products.
Demonstrated technical leadership on an aircraft-development program, preferably as a Chief Engineer, Deputy Chief Engineer, Air Vehicle Lead, Systems Engineering Lead, Integrated Product Team Lead, or equivalent.
Broad understanding of aircraft design and integration across multiple engineering disciplines, with the technical judgment to identify critical interfaces and system-level consequences.
Experience taking an aircraft or similarly complex aerospace system through multiple lifecycle stages, such as requirements development, preliminary and critical design, fabrication, integration, ground test, flight test, qualification, or production.
Experience establishing and managing system requirements, technical baselines, interface definitions, design reviews, verification plans, and engineering risks.
Demonstrated ability to make high-quality technical decisions with incomplete information and under aggressive program timelines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues and recommendations to executive and customer audiences.
Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced development environment.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, Engineering Management, or a related discipline.
Experience developing clean-sheet military aircraft, fighter aircraft, collaborative combat aircraft, unmanned aircraft systems, or advanced VTOL platforms.
Experience with propulsion integration, flight controls, vehicle management systems, autonomy integration, low-observable aircraft, or weapons and mission-systems integration.
Experience supporting aircraft ground test, envelope expansion, developmental flight test, airworthiness, and mishap-risk reduction.
Familiarity with military airworthiness frameworks, verification and validation processes, configuration management, and model-based systems engineering.
Experience transitioning an aircraft from rapid prototype development into qualification, rate production, and operational deployment.
Experience working directly with the Department of Defense, military service customers, external suppliers, and strategic industry partners.
Background in a high-growth aerospace organization where speed, individual ownership, and first-principles thinking were essential to program success.

They must be comfortable moving between system-level decisions and detailed technical problem-solving while balancing performance, safety, cost, schedule, manufacturability, and mission requirements.
What You’ll Do
Serve as the primary technical deputy to the X-BAT Air Vehicle Lead, acting on their behalf when necessary and helping translate program objectives into clear engineering priorities.
Maintain the integrity of the air vehicle’s technical baseline, including system requirements, architecture, interfaces, configuration, performance, verification, and airworthiness evidence.
Lead the day-to-day integration of engineering activities across aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, mechanical systems, avionics, electrical systems, flight controls, software, autonomy, manufacturing, and test.
Drive aircraft-level technical decisions and trade studies, ensuring decisions are grounded in first-principles analysis and consider downstream effects on performance, safety, cost, schedule, producibility, maintainability, and operations.
Establish and maintain a disciplined technical-risk process, ensuring risks are identified early, assigned accountable owners, supported by mitigation plans, and retired through analysis or test.
Lead major technical and design reviews, ensuring the aircraft is sufficiently mature to progress through fabrication, ground test, flight test, qualification, and production.
Partner with Program Management to align technical scope with schedule, budget, staffing, supplier, and customer commitments.
Work closely with Manufacturing and Supply Chain to ensure designs are producible, scalable, and supported by a resilient supplier base.
Partner with Test and Flight Operations to define verification strategies, ground- and flight-test objectives, instrumentation requirements, test readiness criteria, and issue-resolution plans.
Lead rapid root-cause investigations and corrective actions for complex aircraft-level problems identified during integration, ground test, flight test, production, or operations.
Ensure technical decisions and engineering changes are documented, communicated, and reflected in the controlled product baseline.
Develop the technical leadership capabilities of engineering managers, functional leads, integrated product team leads, and senior individual contributors.
Communicate aircraft status, technical risks, decision recommendations, and recovery plans clearly to program leadership, executives, customers, and external partners.
Foster a culture of technical excellence, urgency, ownership, intellectual honesty, and constructive challenge.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
12+ years of progressive experience developing complex aircraft, military aerospace systems, autonomous aircraft, or similarly integrated aerospace products.
Demonstrated technical leadership on an aircraft-development program, preferably as a Chief Engineer, Deputy Chief Engineer, Air Vehicle Lead, Systems Engineering Lead, Integrated Product Team Lead, or equivalent.
Broad understanding of aircraft design and integration across multiple engineering disciplines, with the technical judgment to identify critical interfaces and system-level consequences.
Experience taking an aircraft or similarly complex aerospace system through multiple lifecycle stages, such as requirements development, preliminary and critical design, fabrication, integration, ground test, flight test, qualification, or production.
Experience establishing and managing system requirements, technical baselines, interface definitions, design reviews, verification plans, and engineering risks.
Demonstrated ability to make high-quality technical decisions with incomplete information and under aggressive program timelines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues and recommendations to executive and customer audiences.
Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced development environment.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, Engineering Management, or a related discipline.
Experience developing clean-sheet military aircraft, fighter aircraft, collaborative combat aircraft, unmanned aircraft systems, or advanced VTOL platforms.
Experience with propulsion integration, flight controls, vehicle management systems, autonomy integration, low-observable aircraft, or weapons and mission-systems integration.
Experience supporting aircraft ground test, envelope expansion, developmental flight test, airworthiness, and mishap-risk reduction.
Familiarity with military airworthiness frameworks, verification and validation processes, configuration management, and model-based systems engineering.
Experience transitioning an aircraft from rapid prototype development into qualification, rate production, and operational deployment.
Experience working directly with the Department of Defense, military service customers, external suppliers, and strategic industry partners.
Background in a high-growth aerospace organization where speed, individual ownership, and first-principles thinking were essential to program success.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Founded in 2015, Shield AI is building intelligent, autonomous aircraft that protect service members and civilians around the world. As we scale production, we're building more than a factory—we're building an AI-native manufacturing ecosystem that will define the future of aerospace production. 
Build the AI Factory of the Future 
We're looking for a Digital Factory Lead to help create one of the world's most advanced manufacturing environments. 
This role sits at the intersection of manufacturing, software, data, automation, and artificial intelligence. You will define and deploy the digital systems, connected infrastructure, and AI-enabled tools that power aircraft production—transforming factory operations through technology. 
From implementing our Manufacturing Execution System (MES) to deploying AI-powered manufacturing solutions, you'll help define how autonomous aircraft are built for years to come.

lists.content:
AI-Enabled Manufacturing 
  • Develop and execute Shield AI's AI Manufacturing roadmap. 
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI across production, quality, maintenance, supply chain, training, and operational decision-making. 
  • Deploy AI-powered solutions including intelligent work instructions, manufacturing copilots, predictive maintenance, automated root-cause analysis, and advanced analytics. 
  • Partner with software and data teams to turn operational challenges into scalable technical solutions. 
  • Capture and digitize manufacturing knowledge to improve workforce productivity, training, and consistency. 
    • Digital Factory Systems 
  • Lead the deployment, configuration, and continuous improvement of Shield AI's Manufacturing Execution System (MES). 
  • Establish the digital thread connecting engineering, production, quality, maintenance, and supply chain operations. 
  • Drive integration between MES, ERP, PLM, QMS, factory automation systems, and manufacturing equipment. 
    • Connected Factory Infrastructure 
  • Define and deploy the digital architecture supporting production equipment, tooling, test systems, PLCs, sensors, and industrial controls. 
  • Establish factory-wide connectivity and real-time operational visibility. 
  • Develop the data ecosystem required to support AI, automation, analytics, and future autonomous manufacturing capabilities. 
    • Factory Transformation 
  • Develop and execute Shield AI's Digital Factory roadmap. 
  • Lead automation initiatives across manufacturing, inspection, testing, and material flow. 
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including machine vision, digital twins, autonomous inspection, and next-generation manufacturing systems. 
  • Help define what aircraft manufacturing should look like over the next decade.

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, Automation, or a related technical discipline. 
  • 8+ years of experience in digital manufacturing, manufacturing systems, industrial automation, software-enabled operations, or Industry 4.0 environments. 
  • Experience implementing manufacturing software systems such as MES, QMS, maintenance, analytics, or automation platforms. 
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, industrial controls, factory automation, and manufacturing data systems. 
  • Experience working directly with software developers, system integrators, automation engineers, or data teams to deliver production-ready solutions. 
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex cross-functional initiatives from concept through deployment.

• Aerospace, defense, automotive, robotics, electronics, or other high-complexity manufacturing experience. 
  • Experience supporting greenfield factory launches or large-scale factory transformations. 
  • Experience applying AI, machine learning, advanced analytics, or digital twin technologies in an operational environment. 
  • Knowledge of AS9100, or other highly controlled manufacturing systems.

Most companies are still trying to digitize their factories. 

At Shield AI, we're building an AI-native manufacturing environment from the ground up. 

The systems, technologies, and AI-enabled capabilities you deploy will directly influence how autonomous aircraft are manufactured for years to come, enabling Shield AI to scale production while maintaining the quality, speed, and operational excellence required for mission-critical aerospace systems.

Job Description:
At Shield AI, we’re redefining the battlespace with autonomy-enabled airpower. As part of our global expansion, we’re looking for a bold and visionary Director – CCAs, Northeast Asia to lead strategic sales, customer engagement, and capture efforts for our Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) initiatives across the region. This is a high-impact role at the cutting edge of aerospace and defense innovation. You’ll be on the front lines, driving adoption and revenue for Shield AI’s CCA technologies by engaging directly with top-tier defense stakeholders—military customers, industry primes, and government decision-makers. Your mission: position Shield AI as the go-to partner for next-generation air combat solutions in Northeast Asia. 
You’ll bring a rare mix of defense sales expertise, technical credibility, and a deep understanding of air domain CONOPS and acquisition frameworks. From identifying new opportunities to closing complex deals and launching early-stage programs, you’ll own the entire business development lifecycle.

  • Strong track record of capturing and closing defense programs or tech insertions with relevant ministries of Defense or multinational frameworks.

Shield AI is seeking a Director of Contingent Workforce Programs to lead the strategy, governance, operations, and continuous improvement of our contingent workforce program, supporting agency workers, independent contractors, and statement-of-work (SOW) engagements. In this role, you will independently assess business needs, establish program priorities, recommend decisions, and drive execution across functions. You will build and improve the processes, controls, and partnerships that enable an effective, scalable program. You will partner closely with business leaders, People Experience (PX), EOR vendors, Legal, Finance, IT, and Security to strengthen program performance, manage risk, improve supplier accountability, and deliver a consistent stakeholder experience. This is a hands-on role for someone who can set direction and follow through on the operational details that make a program successful. The role may supervise one employee responsible for program coordination and administration.

lists.content:
Program Strategy & Governance
• Own the contingent workforce program strategy, operating model, and roadmap; independently assess gaps, recommend solutions, and drive improvements.
• Establish policies, processes, decision rights, approval requirements, and service expectations with cross-functional partners.
• Lead program changes from planning through implementation, communications, training, and adoption.
 
Program Operations
• Oversee the engagement lifecycle, from intake and review through onboarding, extensions, and offboarding.
 • Monitor service performance, resolve bottlenecks, and lead resolution of complex or sensitive issues.  
• Address recurring problems and develop practical guidance that improves execution and the manager experience.
• Partner with business leaders and Finance on workforce needs, engagement options, and budget considerations.
• Serve as the program's subject-matter expert and coordinate classification reviews with Legal, PX, and Procurement.
• Align stakeholders, drive accountability, and present program performance, risks, and recommendations to leadership.
 
Vendors, Data, & Systems Management
• Own supplier relationships and performance, including scorecards, reviews, and corrective actions.
• Partner with business leaders and other stakeholders on supplier strategy, selection, contracts, rates, and cost optimization.
• Maintain program controls with Legal, PX, Procurement, and Security, ensuring required reviews, approvals, documentation, and exceptions are managed.
• Define metrics and reporting to monitor workforce population, spend, supplier performance, service levels, and risk.
• Use data to guide improvements and partner with vendors to strengthen workflows, data quality, and supporting systems.

• 12+ years of relevant experience in contingent workforce management, workforce programs, HR/PX operations, procurement, or supplier management, including direct ownership of a contingent workforce program.
• Demonstrated experience building, scaling, or transforming an enterprise contingent workforce program, with measurable improvements in operations, governance, supplier performance, or cost.
• Experience independently leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through implementation and ongoing improvement.
• Strong working knowledge of agency worker, independent contractor, and SOW engagement models.
• Experience establishing program governance, processes, controls, service standards, and performance measures.
• Experience managing suppliers and resolving complex operational or stakeholder issues.
• Ability to analyze workforce, supplier, or spend data and turn findings into actionable recommendations. 
• Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to advise leaders and drive accountability across teams.
• Ability to work independently with broad direction, navigate ambiguity, and balance strategic priorities with hands-on execution.

• Experience supporting contingent workforce programs across multiple countries or business units.
• Previous people-management or team-leadership experience.
• Experience with vendor management systems (VMS), managed service provider (MSP) models, and HR, procurement, or workforce analytics platforms.
• Experience with supplier negotiations, rate management, and workforce cost optimization.
• Experience in a high-growth, technical, engineering, aerospace, defense, or manufacturing environment.

Shield AI is expanding rapidly across global defense markets, working with governments, militaries, defense organizations, and strategic partners to deliver next-generation autonomous capabilities. Based in Singapore and reporting to the VP, Global Field Marketing Units, this leader will develop the strategy, team, programs, and operating discipline required to support Shield AI’s growth across a diverse and rapidly evolving set of aerospace and defense markets.
 
This role will partner closely with Sales, Business Development, Capture, Growth, Product Marketing, and executive leadership to translate regional business priorities into high-impact field marketing programs that strengthen strategic relationships, accelerate opportunities, support capture efforts, and generate measurable pipeline impact.

The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of international defense and aerospace markets and is comfortable navigating complex government, military, acquisition, and industry stakeholder environments. lists.content:
• Lead and scale Field Marketing across the Middle East, India, and Asia Pacific, establishing a unified regional strategy aligned with Shield AI’s global Go-to-Market priorities.
  • Lead the company’s largest regional field marketing team, developing organizational structure, talent, processes, and operating rhythms that enable the team to scale effectively across multiple markets.
  • Build and institutionalize field marketing as a disciplined, revenue-aligned function within a fast-growing aerospace and defense organization.
  • Develop and execute account-based marketing strategies for priority government, military, defense, aerospace, and strategic industry accounts, mapping stakeholders and orchestrating multi-touch engagement across events, executive briefings, targeted campaigns, and other high-value experiences.
  • Develop a deep understanding of the defense and aerospace ecosystems across the Middle East, India, Japan, Korea, Australia, Southeast Asia, and other priority APAC markets, including key military, government, acquisition, industry, and technology stakeholders.
  • Partner with Sales, Business Development, and Capture teams to identify strategic accounts and opportunities and develop marketing programs that support relationship development, pipeline creation, opportunity progression, and capture objectives.
  • Own strategy and execution for major aerospace and defense events across the region, prioritizing strategic account engagement, executive meetings, customer relationships, and opportunity acceleration over brand presence alone.
  • Create and execute high-impact ABM programs, executive engagements, customer experiences, roundtables, and regional campaigns designed to generate new pipeline and accelerate existing opportunities.
  • Develop regional marketing strategies that account for differences in defense procurement processes, government structures, military organizations, acquisition timelines, budgets, and business cultures across individual markets.
  • Build strong relationships with regional Sales, Business Development, Capture, and Growth leaders to ensure field marketing investments are directly connected to business priorities and revenue opportunities.
  • Establish KPIs that reflect international defense sales realities, including strategic account penetration, stakeholder engagement depth, executive engagement, opportunity creation, pipeline contribution, and deal acceleration.
  • Lead regional agencies, vendors, event partners, and other external resources, ensuring high-quality execution and disciplined management of marketing investments.
  • Bring creativity, structure, cultural awareness, and adaptability to a rapidly evolving environment where new markets, capabilities, and customer opportunities are developing in real time.
  • Represent Shield AI and Field Marketing with senior internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating the credibility, judgment, and executive presence required to operate in complex aerospace and defense environments.

• 10 to 15+ years of experience in field marketing, demand generation, integrated marketing, or related marketing leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated experience marketing into international government, military, aerospace, defense, or other highly complex B2G environments.
  • Strong understanding of aerospace and defense markets across the Middle East and/or Asia Pacific, with the ability to operate effectively across multiple countries and cultures.
  • Experience working with defense ministries, military services, government agencies, acquisition organizations, defense primes, or other strategic aerospace and defense stakeholders.
  • Proven experience building and executing account-based marketing strategies within complex, multi-stakeholder organizations.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop marketing strategies that support long-cycle sales, government procurement, defense acquisition, capture, and strategic account development.
  • Experience leading and scaling regional teams across multiple countries or geographies.
  • Strong executive presence and credibility engaging senior military, government, defense industry, and business leaders.
  • Experience operating as a hands-on builder and operator in a high-growth or rapidly evolving organization.
  • Strong cross-functional partnership skills with Sales, Business Development, Capture, Growth, Product Marketing, and executive leadership.
  • Ability to travel internationally 25-50% of the time.

Job Description:

We are seeking a hands-on engineering leader to direct multiple teams spanning electrical design engineering, avionics root cause analysis, and avionics build/test operations. In this role, you will own the technical health and reliability of the avionics systems powering the V-BAT platform — leading the people, processes, and designs that take issues from field observation through root cause resolution and durable design improvement. You will operate at the intersection of design, manufacturing, quality, and fleet support, and you will be measured by the reliability, performance, and manufacturability of what your teams deliver.

lists.content:
• Lead and grow the team. Mentor and develop a multidisciplinary organization of electrical design engineers, root cause analysis engineers, and avionics build/test technicians, building career paths and technical depth across all three disciplines.
  • Set direction and drive execution. Establish team priorities, allocate resources against competing demands, and drive execution while fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and continuous improvement.
  • Stay technical. Actively contribute to design development and reviews, hands-on root cause analysis, and the definition and validation of corrective actions — leading by technical example, not just management.
  • Own investigations end to end. Lead cross-functional failure investigations, establish and verify corrective and preventive actions, and build tooling and infrastructure that accelerate debugging, test, and issue resolution.
  • Improve system reliability. Drive coordination across Supply Chain, Reliability, Manufacturing, Quality, and Fleet Support to implement the processes and design changes that measurably increase the reliability and availability of the V-BAT system.
  • Build the standard. Establish the standards, review cadences, and metrics (e.g., reliability growth, escape rates, time-to-resolution) that make technical quality repeatable and scalable as the program grows.

• B.S. in Electrical Engineering or an equivalent technical field.
  • 10+ years of experience, including demonstrated success leading and growing teams of electrical engineers.
  • Proven track record of building and scaling high-performing technical teams.
  • Experience working cross-functionally across design, supply chain, manufacturing, quality, and fleet/field support.
  • Proven ability to plan and execute complex electronic and electrical designs in a high-consequence industry (defense, aerospace, automotive, or medical device).
  • Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership development environment with rapidly evolving priorities.

• M.S. or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering.
  • Experience with structured problem-solving and failure analysis methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone/Ishikawa diagrams, FMEA/FMECA, 8D, or similar.
  • Ownership of full product development lifecycles — from concept through release, production ramp, customer sustainment, and product retirement.
  • Experience in UAV/UAS design or other autonomous or unmanned systems.
  • Familiarity with reliability engineering practices (reliability growth modeling, MTBF/MTBUR analysis, accelerated life testing).

Shield AI is looking for a Director of Avionics Mechanical Engineering to build and lead the organization responsible for all mechanical, thermal, and harnessing (EWIS) design for the X-BAT aircraft and ground equipment. You'll set the technical strategy and organizational structure, develop managers and technical leads, and be accountable for delivering flight-critical electro-mechanical hardware from concept through production. As a senior member of the avionics leadership team, you'll partner with engineering, program, and operations leaders to shape architecture, schedule, and resourcing decisions. Leaders at Shield are expected to have strong technical fundamentals and a real history of hands-on design.

lists.content:
• Own the technical vision, strategy, and roadmap for mechanical, thermal, and EWIS engineering across X-BAT flight and ground avionics
  • Build and scale a multi-team organization: hire and develop managers and technical leads, define org structure, and plan headcount to meet near- and long-term program goals
  • Be accountable for your organization's delivery of complex electro-mechanical hardware that survives harsh environments, from architecture through qualification and production
  • Set engineering standards, design review practices, and processes for thermal, mechanical, and harness design of flight-critical avionics
  • Serve as the final technical authority on key mechanical and thermal architecture tradeoffs, and escalate risk to program leadership with clear recommendations
  • Partner with electrical engineering, RF, PCB design, reliability, structures, supply chain, and manufacturing leaders to drive full-scope product delivery
  • Own organizational planning inputs, including resourcing, schedule commitments, supplier and contract manufacturer strategy, and make-vs-buy decisions
  • Build a culture of extreme ownership, technical rigor, and accountability
  • You won't design as an individual contributor. You must have done that work earlier in your career so you can establish what "right" looks like across the organization.

• B.S. in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering
  • 15+ years of experience in mechanical design around electronics and electrical systems, including significant early-career, hands-on design of enclosures, thermal solutions, and harness integration
  • 5+ years of people leadership, including managing managers or leading multiple engineering teams
  • Proven record of building and scaling engineering teams through rapid growth
  • Record of delivering complex avionics or electro-mechanical hardware from concept through production
  • Deep technical fluency in avionics packaging, FEA, thermal analysis, and fatigue and lifecycle testing
  • Experience setting engineering strategy, standards, and processes across an organization
  • Experience managing relationships with fabrication shops, contract manufacturers, and key suppliers
  • Ability to operate in a fast-paced, agile environment with shifting priorities
  • A demonstrated record of working hard, being trustworthy, holding yourself to high standards, and being kind to others
  • Ability to obtain a Secret security clearance

• Experience leading hardware teams on aircraft, spacecraft, launch vehicles, or defense platforms
  • Background in high-rate hardware production, such as satellites, EV power electronics, or autonomous vehicles
  • Experience with DO-160, MIL-STD-810, or similar environmental qualification standards
  • Degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or equivalent Engineering

Job Description:
The Director, DoN Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating rhythm that enables Shield AI’s UAS pursuits with the Department of the Navy, including the U.S. Navy and U.S. Marine Corps. Opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders retain ownership of their customers, capture strategies, account plans, and individual pursuits. This role serves as the connective tissue across those leaders, integrating information across the DoN portfolio and providing the VP, Mission Solutions with a clear, decision-ready view of campaign health, priorities, dependencies, risks, mitigations, and resource requirements. 
The Director connects DoN pursuits with relevant activity across other Services, allied and partner nations, product and engineering, U.S. Government approvals, aircraft availability, ship and at-sea test windows, airworthiness and shipboard-suitability sequencing, internal investment, and industrial strategy. The role identifies shared dependencies and resource conflicts early, helps sequence competing demands, and coordinates the cross-functional support required for GTM leads to execute their captures effectively. 
The role maintains the authoritative DoN campaign picture and runs the operating cadence that turns portfolio insight into action.
