Job Description:

The Director, DoN Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating rhythm that enables Shield AI’s UAS pursuits with the Department of the Navy, including the U.S. Navy and U.S. Marine Corps. Opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders retain ownership of their customers, capture strategies, account plans, and individual pursuits. This role serves as the connective tissue across those leaders, integrating information across the DoN portfolio and providing the VP, Mission Solutions with a clear, decision-ready view of campaign health, priorities, dependencies, risks, mitigations, and resource requirements. 

The Director connects DoN pursuits with relevant activity across other Services, allied and partner nations, product and engineering, U.S. Government approvals, aircraft availability, ship and at-sea test windows, airworthiness and shipboard-suitability sequencing, internal investment, and industrial strategy. The role identifies shared dependencies and resource conflicts early, helps sequence competing demands, and coordinates the cross-functional support required for GTM leads to execute their captures effectively. 

The role maintains the authoritative DoN campaign picture and runs the operating cadence that turns portfolio insight into action. This includes campaign reviews, risk and dependency management, executive dashboards, action tracking, investment recommendations, and escalation of decisions requiring VP or executive attention. The Director ensures that information flows efficiently from the GTM organization to the VP, Mission Solutions and that leadership receives clear recommendations, tradeoffs, and required decisions. 

GTM leads remain accountable for customer engagement, account planning, capture strategy, win strategy, price-to-win, proposal content, and pursuit outcomes. The Director enables their success by improving coordination, reducing friction around shared resources, and ensuring that the broader organization is aligned behind the highest-priority Department of the Navy opportunities.

lists.content:
This is a senior, high-visibility seat with authority, not a reporting function: 
  • Portfolio: Multiple concurrent Navy and Marine Corps pursuits across the X-BAT FoS, representing a multi-billion-dollar addressable opportunity. 
  • Team: Leadership by influence role, leveraging dedicated capture-operations and analyst support, with the expectation to build the team as the portfolio scales. 
  • Investment: Develops and co-stewards annual campaign and indirect investment against prioritized campaign returns. 
  • Governance: holds a standing seat in DoN bid/no-bid and investment-prioritization reviews, and sets the agenda for the executive campaign review. 
  • Growth path: a pipeline role toward senior Department of the Navy growth or general-management leadership at Shield AI.

• Own the DoN view. Build and maintain the integrated DoN campaign picture across all X-BAT FoS DoN pursuits: strategy status, critical path, milestones, dependencies, decision points, and campaign health in one authoritative view. 
  • Enable GTM leads. Give each GTM lead the templates, playbooks, data, competitive inputs, cost and schedule inputs, and cross-functional access they need to build and execute their own capture plan. Success is measured by their outcomes, not by your visibility. 
  • Synchronize functions. Coordinate engineering, product, export, legal, contracts, finance, government relations, and business operations against a single prioritized campaign plan so GTM leads are not individually negotiating for the same scarce resources. 
  • Surface conflicts between campaigns. Identify where two or more campaigns compete for the same aircraft, test window, ship or range availability, engineering effort, approval bandwidth, or indirect dollar, and bring executive leadership a clear tradeoff and a recommendation. 
  • Drive executive decision quality. Run the operating cadence — campaign reviews, gate reviews, risk registers, action tracking, and executive dashboards — so leadership receives timely, accurate, decision-ready information on bid/no-bid, investment, and prioritization. 
  • Steward indirect investment. Work with Finance and Business Operations to track campaign investment, indirect spend, and resource planning against campaign priorities and expected return. 
  • Scale discipline. Capture what worked and what did not across captures, and convert it into repeatable tools, templates, metrics, and playbooks so each new campaign starts further ahead than the last. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
  • Roll up your sleeves. Personally drive the execution of critical customer responses (RFI, RFP, CSO, and other solicitation vehicles) — assembling cross-functional inputs, holding the response schedule, and driving on-time submission, while the GTM lead retains ownership of win strategy, price-to-win, and proposal content.

• This role is accountable for: the integrated campaign plan and DoN view; the operating cadence and campaign-health reporting; identification and escalation of cross-campaign dependencies, conflicts, and risks; path-to-win roadmap; and recommendations on investment prioritization and sequencing. 
  • Opportunity GTM leads are accountable for: customer relationships and engagement, capture strategy, win strategy and price-to-win for their pursuit, proposal content, and the bid/no-bid recommendation for their opportunity. 
  • Government Relations, Export, Legal, and Contracts are accountable for: data-rights, political and legislative engagements and outcomes, disclosure determinations, legal positions, and contracting terms. 
  • Engineering and Product are accountable for: technical solution definition, configuration decisions, performance commitments, and coordination with relevant DoN technical authorities on airworthiness and shipboard-suitability requirements. 
  • Program Management is accountable for: execution of customer-funded programs after award. 
  • External customer engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead.

• U.S. person as defined by ITAR (22 CFR 120.62), with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. 
  • 12–20+ years in capture management, program management, strategic operations, business operations, technical program management, or a comparable cross-functional leadership role. 
  • Demonstrated success leading highly complex initiatives with multiple interdependent workstreams across engineering, business development, operations, finance, and executive leadership. 
  • Working knowledge of how Department of the Navy programs actually get funded and fielded — ASN(RD&A) and NAVAIR program-office dynamics (particularly PAE(A)) and the unmanned aviation portfolio), Navy and Marine Corps resource sponsorship and requirements staffing (N9/N98) and the Marine Corps aviation requirements process, the PPBE/POM cycle and Navy budget submission rhythm, and rapid-acquisition pathways such as OTAs, CSOs, Middle Tier of Acquisition, SBIR/STRATFI, DIU, ONR, and NavalX, including the transition from prototype to program of record. 
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to drive accountability across functions and geographies. 
  • Strong executive communication: leadership briefings, dashboards, metrics, and decision-support materials that lead to decisions rather than discussion. 
  • Deep operational rigor in integrated schedules, critical path, milestones, action tracking, dependency management, and risk mitigation. 
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments with competing priorities across multiple time zones. 
  • Working understanding of the dependencies unique to naval aviation — NAVAIR airworthiness and flight-clearance processes, shipboard integration and suitability, environmental and marinization requirements, ship and at-sea test window availability, and DT/OT execution at Patuxent River and associated ranges. 
  • A service orientation toward the GTM leads this role supports, and the judgment to know when to escalate versus resolve quietly.

• Active DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and current Special Access Program accesses. 
  • Experience supporting Department of Defense, aerospace, autonomy, robotics, aviation, or defense-technology organizations. 
  • Naval aviation background — U.S. Navy or Marine Corps operational, test, staff, or acquisition experience, or equivalent industry experience delivering aircraft to the Department of the Navy. 
  • Experience within business development, capture, proposal operations, strategic planning, or growth organizations running multiple concurrent U.S. Government pursuits. 
  • Familiarity with the export and international mechanisms that shape Department of the Navy pursuits — foreign disclosure determinations, FMS/DCS pathways, and security cooperation planning — where allied demand affects the Navy business case. 
  • Experience building executive dashboards, KPIs, operational scorecards, or portfolio health metrics. 
  • Experience supporting executive staff, chief-of-staff organizations, Strategy and Operations teams, or enterprise PMOs. 
  • Fluency with integrated schedule and work-management tooling (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira), and an advanced degree or relevant certification (MBA, PMP, Lean Six Sigma) is a plus but not required.

• GTM leads report that the role makes their campaign easier to run, not heavier to report on. 
  • DoN path-to-win is in place and running on a predictable, repeatable cadence that the whole organization can plan against. 
  • Cross-campaign resource and timing conflicts reach leadership as a decision with a recommendation, not as a surprise. 
  • Executive leadership can see, at any time, an accurate health picture of the DoN X-BAT FoS portfolio and make investment calls with confidence. 
  • Campaign mechanisms are reused across opportunities, and each new pursuit stands up measurably faster than the previous one.

Shield AI’s core values — Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, and Pursue Excellence — are how we hire, promote, and make hard calls. This role in particular demands servant leadership: success is measured by the outcomes of the GTM leads it supports. 

Veterans and transitioning service members: we actively seek candidates with U.S. Navy or U.S. Marine Corps operational, staff, or acquisition experience, and we support military-to-civilian transitions. 

Compensation and benefits: competitive base salary, meaningful equity in a growing defense-technology company, annual bonus, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and relocation support where applicable. Final compensation depends on experience, clearance, and location.

lists.content:
• Establish and own engineering design standards across programs, including XBAT and VBAT

  • Manufacturing & supply chain handoff including EBOM and MBOM creation along with driving part demand
  • Build and mature an engineering excellence framework that scales with the company  
  • Partner with engineering leadership to align teams on consistent ways of working  
  • Ensure standards are practical, accessible, and consistently applied across teams  
  • Influence design decisions and engineering processes across disciplines without becoming a bottleneck  
  • Support both near-term program execution and long-term scalability of engineering processes  
  • Drive improvements in configuration management, documentation quality, and design consistency  
  • Ability to obtain a S//SAR level security clearance desired.

• 10+ years of experience in aerospace or high-performance hardware design environments 
  • Deep experience working within organizations that maintain strong engineering standards and design rigor 
  • Broad technical background across multiple engineering domains (mechanical, aerospace, systems, etc.)  
  • Experience defining or applying design standards, documentation practices, and configuration management systems  
  • Familiarity with industry standards such as MIL-STD-810, DO-160, and ASME Y14.5 (GD&T)

  • Establish engineering effectiveness metrics and dashboards that provide visibility into organizational health, delivery performance, and engineering productivity.

Job Description:
The Director, International Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating system behind Shield AI international X-BAT pursuits. Regional, country and opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders own their customers, their regional and in-country strategies, and their individual captures. This role owns the layer above them: the single, integrated view across regions, and the mechanisms that turn that view into faster decisions, earlier risk mitigation, and better-supported GTM leads. 
Each GTM lead sees their own campaign clearly. No one else sees the whole international board. This role does. It connects individual pursuits to shared dependencies — U.S. Government approvals, foreign disclosure and export sequencing, engineering and product capacity, aircraft and test availability, indirect investment, partner and industrial strategy — and makes sure competing regional timelines and strategies are sequenced deliberately rather than reactively. 
This is a pre-award enablement and integration role. It is explicitly not the primary customer interface, and it does not extend to the execution of customer-funded programs after award, though it may involve developing projections to better inform execution-supporting decision making. The GTM lead remains the face to the customer, the owner of the account plan, and the accountable capture lead for their country. This role makes those leads faster, better armed, and better supported.

Job Description:

The Director, International Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating system behind Shield AI international X-BAT pursuits. Regional, country and opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders own their customers, their regional and in-country strategies, and their individual captures. This role owns the layer above them: the single, integrated view across regions, and the mechanisms that turn that view into faster decisions, earlier risk mitigation, and better-supported GTM leads. 

Each GTM lead sees their own campaign clearly. No one else sees the whole international board. This role does. It connects individual pursuits to shared dependencies — U.S. Government approvals, foreign disclosure and export sequencing, engineering and product capacity, aircraft and test availability, indirect investment, partner and industrial strategy — and makes sure competing regional timelines and strategies are sequenced deliberately rather than reactively. 

This is a pre-award enablement and integration role. It is explicitly not the primary customer interface, and it does not extend to the execution of customer-funded programs after award, though it may involve developing projections to better inform execution-supporting decision making. The GTM lead remains the face to the customer, the owner of the account plan, and the accountable capture lead for their country. This role makes those leads faster, better armed, and better supported.

lists.content:
• Own the global view. Build and maintain the integrated international campaign picture across all X-BAT regional and country pursuits: strategy status, critical path, milestones, dependencies, decision points, and campaign health in one authoritative picture. 
  • Enable the GTM leads. Give regional and country GTM leads the templates, playbooks, data, competitive inputs, cost and schedule inputs, and cross-functional access they need to build and execute their capture plan. Your success is measured by their outcomes. 
  • Synchronize across company functions. Ensure engineering, product, export, legal, contracts, finance, government relations, and business operations have common understanding of a single prioritized international campaign plan, so GTM leads are not individually negotiating for the same scarce resources. 
  • Map the U.S. Government and approval critical path. Maintain the enterprise view of FMS, DCS, and hybrid pathway dependencies — foreign disclosure, exportability, releasability, technology security, and interagency approval sequencing — and translate them into country-level timeline implications the GTM leads can act on. Government Relations and the relevant functional owners lead those engagements; this role ensures they are planned early, sequenced correctly, and never discovered late. Understand and communicate the global GTM projections in ways that support enabling functions’ ability to anticipate and properly resource for future demand. 
  • Surface conflicts between campaigns. Identify where two or more regional campaigns compete for the same aircraft, test window, engineering effort, approval bandwidth, or indirect dollar, and bring executive leadership a clear tradeoff and a recommendation. 
  • Drive executive decision quality. Run the operating cadence — campaign reviews, gate reviews, risk registers, action tracking, and executive dashboards — so leadership receives timely, accurate, decision-ready information on overall international capture health in support of resource allocation. Steward indirect investment. Work with Finance and Business Operations to track campaign investment, indirect spend, and resource planning against campaign priorities and expected return. 
  • Scale the discipline. Capture lessons learned across international efforts and convert them into repeatable tools, templates, metrics, and playbooks so each new campaign starts further ahead than the last. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

This role is accountable for: the integrated international campaign plan; the operating cadence and campaign-health reporting; identification and escalation of cross-campaign dependencies, conflicts, and risks; the consolidated U.S. Government approval and disclosure roadmap; and recommendations on investment prioritization and sequencing. 

Regional, country and opportunity GTM leads are accountable for: customer relationships and engagement, in-country strategy, partner and industrial development, win strategy and price-to-win for their pursuit, proposal content, and the bid/no-bid recommendation for their opportunity. 

Government Relations, Export, Legal, and Contracts are accountable for: interagency and embassy engagement, export authorizations, disclosure determinations, legal positions, and contracting terms. 

Engineering and Product are accountable for: technical solution definition, configuration decisions, and performance commitments. 

Strategy and Operations is responsible for enterprise, cross-product strategy, of which the products this role directly supports would be a part. Program Management is accountable for: execution of customer-funded programs after award. 
 
This role will be complemented by a parallel position whose focus will be on integration across all U.S. customers, and with whom close collaboration will be required.  

External customer engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead.

• 12+ years in international B2G capture management, program management, strategic operations, business operations, technical program management, or a comparable cross-functional leadership role.  
  • Demonstrated success leading highly complex initiatives with multiple interdependent workstreams across engineering, business development, operations, finance, and executive leadership. 
  • Working knowledge of international defense pursuit dependencies, including FMS, DCS, or hybrid acquisition pathways and the approval, disclosure, and exportability sequencing that governs them. 
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to drive accountability across functions and geographies. 
  • Strong executive communication: leadership briefings, dashboards, metrics, and decision-support materials that lead to decisions rather than discussion. 
  • Deep operational rigor in integrated schedules, critical path, milestones, action tracking, dependency management, and risk mitigation. 
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments with competing priorities across multiple time zones. 
  • A service orientation toward the functional roles this position supports, and the judgment to know when to escalate versus resolve quietly. 
  • Demonstrated alignment with Shield AI core values: Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, Pursue Excellence. 
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required, and to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

• Experience supporting Department of War, aerospace, autonomy, robotics, aviation, or defense-technology organizations.  
  • Experience within B2G business development, capture, proposal operations, strategic planning, or growth organizations running multiple concurrent international pursuits. 
  • Familiarity with U.S. Government international engagement mechanisms such as foreign disclosure processes, security cooperation planning, embassy and country team coordination, or interagency advocacy. 
  • Experience building executive dashboards, KPIs, operational scorecards, or portfolio health metrics. 
  • Experience supporting executive staff, chief-of-staff organizations, Strategy and Operations teams, or enterprise PMOs. 
  • Experience with tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira, Confluence, or The AI Work Platform for People & Agents | monday.com . 
  • MBA or advanced degree; PMP, Agile, or Lean Six Sigma certification.

• Every regional campaign has an approved strategy, a critical-path schedule, and a mapped approval pathway that the GTM lead owns and uses. 
  • GTM leads report that the role makes their campaigns easier to run, not heavier to report on. 
  • U.S. Government, export, and disclosure dependencies are identified early enough to change the outcome rather than explain it. 
  • Cross-campaign resource and timing conflicts reach leadership early enough for meaningful action, and as a decision with a recommendation. 
  • Executive leadership can see, at any time, an accurate health picture of the international X-BAT portfolio and make investment calls with confidence. 
  • Campaign mechanisms are reused across countries, and each new pursuit stands up measurably faster than the previous one.

Shield AI’s mission is to protect service members and civilians with intelligent systems. We develop autonomy software and advanced aircraft to help U.S. and allied forces accomplish their missions in challenging environments.
Are you an experienced engineering leader passionate about developing advanced autonomous aircraft? Do you want to build exceptional teams and deliver the mechanical systems that turn aircraft ambition into flight capability? Shield AI may be the place for you.
Shield AI is seeking a Director of X-BAT Mechanical Systems to lead engineering managers and senior technical leaders responsible for mechanical systems and mechanical test on X-BAT, while overseeing Mechanical Engineering and Air Vehicle Systems across our Group 5 aircraft programs. This leader will establish technical strategy, build organizational capability, and oversee execution from architecture and design through integration, qualification, ground test, and flight readiness.
The scope includes landing gear, wing fold, doors, flight control actuation, hydraulics, environmental control, and thermal management. Shield AI’s mission is to protect service members and civilians with intelligent systems. We develop autonomy software and advanced aircraft to help U.S. and allied forces accomplish their missions in challenging environments.

Are you an experienced engineering leader passionate about developing advanced autonomous aircraft? Do you want to build exceptional teams and deliver the mechanical systems that turn aircraft ambition into flight capability? Shield AI may be the place for you.

Shield AI is seeking a Director of X-BAT Mechanical Systems to lead engineering managers and senior technical leaders responsible for mechanical systems and mechanical test on X-BAT, while overseeing Mechanical Engineering and Air Vehicle Systems across our Group 5 aircraft programs. This leader will establish technical strategy, build organizational capability, and oversee execution from architecture and design through integration, qualification, ground test, and flight readiness.

The scope includes landing gear, wing fold, doors, flight control actuation, hydraulics, environmental control, and thermal management. The ideal candidate combines broad aircraft mechanical systems expertise with a demonstrated ability to lead through managers, develop technical leaders, and balance engineering rigor with development speed. They bring the judgment to empower teams, challenge critical decisions, and engage directly when needed to advance aircraft capability.

lists.content:
• Lead and develop the mechanical systems and mechanical test organization for X-BAT, while providing leadership across Mechanical Engineering and Air Vehicle Systems for our Group 5 aircraft portfolio.

  • Define organizational structure, establish clear ownership and decision authority, and align talent and resources with aircraft and program priorities.

  • Recruit, coach, and develop engineering managers and senior technical leaders, building leadership capacity, technical depth, and succession capability.

  • Establish technical strategy, capability roadmaps, and development priorities for landing gear, wing fold, doors, flight control actuation, hydraulics, environmental control, and thermal management.

  • Lead aircraft-level architecture and trade studies that balance performance, reliability, safety, mass, power, volume, maintainability, cost, and schedule.

  • Partner with adjacent engineering organizations to resolve interfaces, reconcile competing requirements, manage dependencies, and retire critical technical risks.

  • Oversee execution from requirements definition and design through hardware development, systems integration, qualification, ground test, and flight readiness.

  • Establish practical expectations for design reviews, verification, risk management, and configuration control that produce clear evidence of design maturity and readiness.

  • Build mechanical test capability encompassing test strategy, facilities, fixtures, instrumentation, procedures, and data analysis to accelerate learning and verify system performance.

  • Guide hardware development and supplier strategy, establish technical expectations, and hold suppliers and manufacturing partners accountable for quality and execution.

  • Work closely with manufacturing, ground test, and flight test leadership to align resources, resolve hardware issues, and deliver integrated systems for aircraft evaluation.

  • Communicate technical direction, progress, risks, decisions, and resource needs to executive leadership, program stakeholders, and customers.

• Bachelor’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • 15+ years of relevant experience in aerospace mechanical systems, air vehicle systems, or comparable complex hardware development.

  • Substantial experience managing engineering managers and senior technical leaders within a multidisciplinary engineering organization.

  • Broad technical credibility across aircraft mechanical systems, with significant expertise in landing gear, actuation, mechanisms, environmental control, or thermal management.

  • Demonstrated success building engineering organizations, hiring and developing leaders, allocating resources, and maintaining high technical standards.

  • Experience guiding teams through hardware development, systems integration, verification, supplier execution, manufacturing, and flight test.

  • Proven ability to make aircraft-level tradeoffs, manage dependencies across programs, and focus teams on work that advances program objectives.

  • Sound engineering and business judgment, including the ability to make decisions with incomplete information while balancing technical risk, cost, schedule, and program maturity.

  • Clear, decisive communication skills and demonstrated success creating alignment across engineering, program leadership, and external stakeholders.

  • U.S. citizenship.

• Leadership experience spanning multiple mechanical engineering departments or a broad air vehicle systems portfolio.

  • Development experience on UAVs, autonomous aircraft, fighters, tactical aircraft, or other high-performance aerospace programs.

  • Experience scaling engineering organizations, mechanical test facilities, and development processes in a rapid research and development or production environment.

  • Familiarity with aircraft airworthiness, qualification, and verification practices, including MIL-HDBK-516 and MIL-STD-810.

  • Demonstrated success taking aircraft hardware through prototype build, integration, ground test, flight test, and transition to production.

  • Advanced degree in a relevant engineering discipline.

  • Active Secret or higher security clearance.

Job Description
Are you a mission-driven engineering leader passionate about developing advanced autonomous aircraft? Do you want to help deliver capabilities that provide decisive advantage in contested environments? Shield AI may be the place for you.
 
Shield AI is seeking a Director of Mission Systems to lead multidisciplinary teams spanning communications, and integrated mission systems for our next-generation autonomous aircraft. This leader will establish the organization’s technical and business strategy, align investments and priorities with product and program objectives, and oversee execution from early concept development through integration, flight test, and fielding.
 
The ideal candidate has led a multidisciplinary organization supporting complex military aircraft or autonomous systems and brings strong business acumen alongside sound technical judgment. This individual need not be a subject-matter expert in every discipline but must understand how operational analysis, survivability, communications, payloads, avionics, autonomy, and weapons integration combine to drive mission effectiveness.
 
What You’ll Do
Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization spanning communications, and integrated mission systems.
Establish clear priorities, accountability, organizational objectives, and operating rhythms that enable teams to execute effectively.
Define technical strategy, capability roadmaps, and investment priorities aligned with aircraft program objectives, customer requirements, and broader business goals.
Oversee the development of integrated mission-system architectures encompassing sensors, payloads, avionics, weapons, secure communications, autonomy, and aircraft survivability.
Direct modeling, simulation, wargaming, and system-of-systems analysis to evaluate mission effectiveness, operational performance, emerging threats, and aircraft design alternatives.
Lead cross-functional trade studies that balance mission capability, survivability, technical risk, cost, schedule, manufacturability, and program maturity.
Ensure disciplined execution from requirements definition and architecture development through hardware-in-the-loop testing, signature validation, flight test, certification, and fielding.
Partner with engineering, product, program management, business development, and aircraft leadership to deliver integrated and mission-relevant capabilities.
Engage DoD customers, operators, suppliers, and government stakeholders to shape requirements, refine concepts of operations, support key decisions, and communicate the operational value of Shield AI’s solutions.
Recruit, coach, and develop people managers and senior technical leaders while building organizational depth and succession capability.
Ensure compliance with applicable system-safety, airworthiness, cybersecurity, security, and certification requirements.
 
Required Qualifications
 
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, mathematics, or another relevant technical discipline.
10+ years of experience supporting complex military aircraft, autonomous systems, or other aerospace and defense programs.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing a multidisciplinary engineering organization that includes people managers and senior technical leaders.
Broad working knowledge across multiple relevant disciplines, including mission systems, operational analysis, modeling and simulation, survivability, secure communications, avionics, sensors, payloads, or weapons integration.
Experience establishing organizational and technical strategies while managing technical, programmatic, and organizational risk.
Proven ability to balance mission performance and engineering requirements with cost, schedule, product maturity, and business priorities.
Experience overseeing complex aircraft capabilities across the product lifecycle—from requirements and architecture through integration, test, certification, fielding, and sustainment.
Executive-level communication skills with demonstrated success influencing customers, operators, business leaders, engineering teams, and government stakeholders.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Job Description:
Shield AI is building intelligent autonomy systems for the defense of service members and civilians. The Hivemind Solutions organization applies Shield AI’s autonomy stack to mission-critical systems across air, maritime, strike, weapons, space, and collaborative autonomy domains.
We are seeking a Director, Operations Analysis to lead a team responsible for turning operational problems into quantitative insights that shape product strategy, engineering priorities, customer engagement, and mission outcomes. This leader will manage and grow a high-performing Operations Analysis team that uses modeling, simulation, wargaming, campaign analysis, and mission-level trade studies to help determine what Hivemind should build, why it matters, and how it performs in realistic operational contexts.
This is a leadership role for someone who can operate at the intersection of autonomy, military operations, mission engineering, modeling and simulation, product strategy, and customer-facing analysis. The right candidate will be technically credible, analytically rigorous, comfortable with ambiguity, and able to translate complex operational questions into clear recommendations for executives, engineers, business development leaders, and government customers.

Job Description:

Shield AI is building intelligent autonomy systems for the defense of service members and civilians. The Hivemind Solutions organization applies Shield AI’s autonomy stack to mission-critical systems across air, maritime, strike, weapons, space, and collaborative autonomy domains.

We are seeking a Director, Operations Analysis to lead a team responsible for turning operational problems into quantitative insights that shape product strategy, engineering priorities, customer engagement, and mission outcomes. This leader will manage and grow a high-performing Operations Analysis team that uses modeling, simulation, wargaming, campaign analysis, and mission-level trade studies to help determine what Hivemind should build, why it matters, and how it performs in realistic operational contexts.

This is a leadership role for someone who can operate at the intersection of autonomy, military operations, mission engineering, modeling and simulation, product strategy, and customer-facing analysis. The right candidate will be technically credible, analytically rigorous, comfortable with ambiguity, and able to translate complex operational questions into clear recommendations for executives, engineers, business development leaders, and government customers.

lists.content:
• Lead and manage the Hivemind Solutions Operations Analysis team, including hiring, mentoring, prioritization, performance management, and technical direction.
  • Build an operations analysis capability that directly informs Hivemind product strategy, autonomy roadmap decisions, customer pursuits, and program execution.
  • Define and execute mission analysis, campaign analysis, force-on-force studies, CONOPS evaluations, and operational trade studies across multiple Hivemind product domains.
  • Partner with Product, Architecture, Systems Engineering, Business Development, Strategy, and Program teams to translate operational problems into analytical studies and actionable product recommendations.
  • Develop analysis plans that connect mission objectives, operational assumptions, threat environments, system performance, autonomy behaviors, and measurable mission outcomes.
  • Guide the use of tools such as AFSIM, NGTS, STK, MATLAB, Python, custom simulations, and other modeling environments to evaluate mission effectiveness and operational value.
  • Establish standards for analytical rigor, model credibility, assumption tracking, sensitivity analysis, uncertainty characterization, and communication of results.
  • Create clear, executive-ready briefings that explain what was analyzed, what assumptions were made, what the results mean, and what decisions should follow.
  • Support customer engagements by developing compelling, technically grounded analysis that demonstrates the operational value of Hivemind-enabled systems.
  • Work with engineering teams to identify the autonomy behaviors, system capabilities, interfaces, performance parameters, and test data needed to improve model fidelity.
  • Help shape product requirements by connecting operational outcomes to measurable system and autonomy performance needs.
  • Build reusable analysis frameworks, scenarios, vignettes, and metrics that can scale across programs and domains.
  • Represent the Operations Analysis function in internal technical reviews, roadmap discussions, capture strategy sessions, and customer-facing meetings.

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations research, applied mathematics, computer science, physics, aerospace, systems engineering, data science, or a related technical field.
  • 10+ years of relevant experience in operations analysis, mission analysis, modeling and simulation, systems analysis, military analysis, campaign analysis, or related technical domains.
  • 5+ years of experience leading teams, projects, or technical analysis efforts.
  • Experience using modeling and simulation to inform real product, system, program, or operational decisions.
  • Strong understanding of military operations, mission planning, force employment, kill chains, sensing, communications, autonomy, aircraft systems, weapons systems, or related defense concepts.
  • Ability to translate ambiguous operational questions into structured analysis plans, quantitative methods, and decision-quality outputs.
  • Experience working with engineering, product, business development, strategy, or customer-facing teams.
  • Strong technical communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders and customers with clarity, confidence, and analytical discipline.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment where priorities evolve quickly and analysis must support real business and technical decisions.
  • U.S. citizenship and eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

• Master’s degree or PhD in operations research, engineering, applied mathematics, data science, aerospace, systems engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Experience with AFSIM, NGTS, STK, MATLAB, Python, Cameo, custom simulation environments, or other mission and campaign analysis tools.
  • Experience analyzing autonomous systems, collaborative autonomy, uncrewed aircraft, crewed-uncrewed teaming, electronic warfare, space systems, missile systems, maritime systems, or air combat operations.
  • Experience supporting defense product development, advanced concepts, government capture efforts, experimentation, test planning, or mission engineering.
  • Familiarity with model validation, verification, credibility assessment, sensitivity analysis, design of experiments, and uncertainty quantification.
  • Experience building analysis teams, establishing technical standards, and scaling analytical capabilities across multiple stakeholders or product lines.
  • Prior military, government laboratory, FFRDC/UARC, defense contractor, or aerospace experience.
  • Active U.S. security clearance.

In this role, success means the Operations Analysis team becomes a trusted decision engine for Hivemind Solutions. The team’s work should not sit on a shelf. It should shape what we build, how we prioritize, how we explain operational value to customers, and how we make hard trade decisions across product lines.

A successful manager will build a team that is technically rigorous, operationally grounded, fast-moving, and deeply connected to the business. They will ensure that analysis is not treated as an after-the-fact briefing function, but as a core part of product development, strategy, and customer engagement.

Autonomy changes what is operationally possible, but only if we understand where it creates real mission advantage. The Operations Analysis team helps answer that question. This team connects Hivemind’s technical capabilities to measurable operational outcomes, helping Shield AI make better product decisions and helping customers understand the mission impact of intelligent autonomous systems.

If you want to lead a team that sits at the center of autonomy, strategy, engineering, and operational decision-making, this role is for you.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Director of Proposals to lead our Business Proposals organization and turn complex deal strategies into compelling, compliant, and timely customer submissions. Reporting to the Sr. Director of Deal Strategy and Execution, you will build the team, standards of excellence, and execution discipline that help Shield AI win domestic and international business. 

You will lead proposal Sr. Managers and proposal professionals supporting the Americas, international markets, and emerging products. Working closely with account teams, Regional Deal Strategists, and functional leaders, you will translate customer mission needs, technical capabilities, and approved commercial approaches into clear, persuasive proposals that earn customer confidence. 

You will develop strong methodologies, processes and systems that raise the quality of written persuasion, allocate resources across competing opportunities, and establish repeatable practices that increase speed and consistency as proposal volume and complexity grow.

lists.content:
Proposal Organization and Talent 
  • Lead, coach, and develop proposal managers and their teams, establishing clear expectations for quality, accountability, collaboration, and professional growth. 
  • Build workforce and capacity plans aligned with the opportunity pipeline, regional demand, pursuit complexity, and emerging product requirements. 
  • Assign proposal leadership and resources across concurrent pursuits, making prioritization recommendations to the Sr. Director of Deal Strategy and Execution when demand exceeds capacity. 
  • Establish a team culture grounded in candid feedback, excellent writing, sound judgment, and shared ownership of results. 
    • Proposal Strategy and Customer Persuasion 
  • Partner with account teams and Regional Deal Strategists early in pursuits to shape proposal strategy, win themes, discriminators, and supporting evidence around customer priorities and evaluation criteria. 
  • Translate complex offerings spanning autonomous platforms, software, payloads, integration, training, services, and sustainment into clear customer value narratives. 
  • Set the standard for executive summaries, technical and management narratives, graphics, and integrated proposal storytelling. Personally write, edit, and challenge critical content on priority pursuits. 
  • Ensure proposal claims are accurate, substantiated, and consistent with approved capabilities, configurations, scope, and delivery assumptions. 
    • Proposal Execution and Compliance 
  • Own the proposal lifecycle from intake and solicitation analysis through planning, development, reviews, production, and submission, including customer clarifications and revisions. 
  • Establish proposal schedules, compliance matrices, content plans, contributor assignments, and review milestones tailored to the size and complexity of each pursuit. 
  • Lead disciplined color team reviews that test compliance, persuasiveness, technical accuracy, and alignment with the approved deal strategy. Ensure findings are resolved before release. 
  • Hold teams accountable for complete, accurate, and timely submissions, with rigorous version control, production checks, and confirmation of delivery. 
  • Support both strategic pursuits and the broader portfolio of written responses, including requests for information, requests for proposals, and other customer submissions. 
    • Functional Alignment and Risk Management 
  • Coordinate contributions from Sales, Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, Contracts, Delivery, Partnerships, and other subject matter experts, with clear owners and deadlines. 
  • Ensure proposed scope, pricing, terms, partner responsibilities, and delivery commitments reflect decisions approved by the appropriate functional owners. 
  • Surface missing inputs, unsupported claims, unresolved decisions, and submission risks early. Escalate with clear recommendations, required decisions, and schedule implications. 
  • Integrate proposal milestones with established Opportunity Review and Management Review processes while reducing duplicate work and unnecessary meetings. 
  • Maintain an accurate record of submitted commitments, assumptions, exclusions, and approved revisions to support contracting and delivery handoffs. 
    • Scalable Processes and Continuous Improvement 
  • Build and maintain a searchable library of approved proposal content, templates, proof points, graphics, and reusable response modules, with named owners and review cadences. 
  • Connect proposal content to approved capability definitions and deal frameworks so teams can reuse validated material with confidence. 
  • Partner with GTM systems and tools leaders to improve proposal workflows, collaboration, content retrieval, and reporting. 
  • Lead proposal retrospectives and incorporate customer feedback, evaluation results, and lessons from wins and losses into team practices and reusable content. 
  • Measure submission timeliness, compliance, response cycle time, rework, content reuse, and win rate on submitted proposals. Use results to improve execution and inform resource decisions.

The Director of Proposals owns the proposal organization, proposal strategy and execution plans, contributor coordination, written quality, compliance, and submission readiness. Regional Deal Strategists lead deal strategy and commercial construction on assigned pursuits, partnering with proposal teams to keep the submission aligned with the agreed approach. 

Account teams retain ownership of customer relationships and the close. Functional leaders retain authority over their respective technical, financial, contractual, export, and delivery decisions. You will ensure those decisions are accurately reflected in the proposal and escalate unresolved issues through the Sr. Director of Deal Strategy and Execution.

• Significant progressive experience leading proposals for complex defense, aerospace, national security, or government technology opportunities, with a demonstrated record of delivering competitive, compliant submissions. 
  • Experience leading proposal managers and multidisciplinary proposal teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and resource allocation across concurrent pursuits. 
  • Demonstrated ability to develop winning proposal strategies and translate technical capabilities into clear, credible customer value. 
  • Strong command of solicitation analysis, compliance matrices, proposal planning, color team reviews, content development, and submission production. 
  • Detailed oriented with exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to improve executive narratives and technical content under demanding deadlines. 
  • Experience coordinating contributions and securing decisions across Sales, Engineering, Product, Finance, Legal, Contracts, and delivery organizations. 
  • Familiarity with government acquisition and contracting requirements, including the ability to identify proposal obligations and engage the appropriate experts. 
  • Sound judgment in handling sensitive information, managing competing priorities, and escalating risks with clear recommendations. 
  • A record of building practical processes and reusable content that improve quality and speed in a growing organization.

• Experience supporting both U.S. government and international defense proposals, including partner contributions and coordination of export and contracting reviews. 
  • Experience with offerings that combine hardware, software, integration, training, field services, and sustainment. 
  • Experience supporting autonomous systems, aviation, defense software, or emerging technology pursuits. 
  • Experience establishing or scaling a centralized proposals function while preserving responsiveness to regional account teams. 
  • Familiarity with Shipley methods, APMP certification, or comparable proposal management training. 
  • Experience applying approved automation and AI tools to proposal workflows with appropriate information protection and human review.

• Repeatable onboarding and performance standards established that challenge and uplevel the Deal Strategy & Execution org. 
  • Proposals are compelling, compliant, delivered on time, and aligned with approved deal strategy and executable commitments. 
  • Proposal managers and contributors operate with clear ownership, realistic plans, and earlier visibility into decisions and risks. 
  • Account teams receive responsive proposal support across strategic opportunities and the broader submission portfolio. 
  • Reusable content and consistent practices reduce avoidable rework and improve response speed. 
  • Proposal quality, team capability, and pursuit outcomes improve through measurable feedback and continuous learning.

Job Description:

As the Director of SOX Compliance, you will build, lead, and continuously improve the company's Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance program in support of a high-growth, public-company environment. Reporting to the Corporate Controller (or Chief Accounting Officer), you will partner closely with Finance, Internal Audit, IT, Engineering, HR, Legal, and business leaders to ensure an effective internal control environment while enabling business growth.

This is initially an individual contributor leadership role (Radford P6) with significant cross-functional influence and executive visibility. As the organization grows, this role is expected to evolve into a people management position with responsibility for building and leading a SOX compliance team.

lists.content:
• Own and lead the company's end-to-end SOX 404 compliance program, including business process, entity-level, and IT general controls (ITGCs).
  • Develop and maintain the annual SOX strategy, risk assessment, scoping, testing plan, and compliance calendar.
  • Partner with control owners to document, assess, and improve key business processes and internal controls.
  • Coordinate management's annual SOX assessment and support external audit requirements to ensure timely completion.
  • Evaluate control deficiencies, facilitate root cause analysis, and drive remediation efforts through successful closure.
  • Monitor regulatory developments and evolving best practices to continuously enhance the SOX program.
  • Collaborate with Finance Transformation, ERP, and business system implementation teams to ensure appropriate controls are designed into new processes and technologies.
  • Drive automation and continuous monitoring opportunities to improve efficiency and control effectiveness.
  • Develop executive-level reporting and present SOX program status, risks, and remediation progress to senior leadership and Audit Committee stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to business leaders on internal controls, governance, and risk management.
  • Establish and maintain SOX policies, methodologies, documentation standards, and training programs.
  • Support broader internal control, governance, and enterprise risk initiatives as needed.
  • Help define the future organizational structure of the SOX function, including recruiting, mentoring, and developing team members as the program expands.

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
  • CPA, CIA, or equivalent professional certification.
  • 15+ years of progressive experience in SOX compliance, internal audit, external audit, accounting, or internal controls.
  • Experience leading SOX programs for publicly traded companies or organizations preparing for public company readiness.
  • Strong knowledge of SOX 404 requirements, COSO Internal Control Framework, and SEC reporting environment.
  • Experience with business process controls, entity-level controls, and IT general controls.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Experience managing external auditors and coordinating complex compliance activities across multiple functions.
  • Excellent project management, analytical, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to executive leadership.
  • Proven ability to identify process improvement opportunities while maintaining a strong control environment.

• Experience in aerospace, defense, manufacturing, hardware, or other complex operational environments.
  • Experience supporting ERP implementations or major systems transformations (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Workday, etc.).
  • Experience with GRC platforms such as AuditBoard, Workiva, Archer, ServiceNow GRC, or similar technologies.
  • Experience leading SOX readiness for IPOs or scaling public-company compliance programs.
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity controls, automated controls, and emerging technologies supporting compliance.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement experience.
  • Demonstrated success building or scaling compliance organizations.
  • Passion for mentoring and developing talent, with an interest in growing into a formal people leadership role as the organization expands.

We are seeking a Director of Systems Engineering & Architecture (SE&A) for Shield AI’s Hivemind Enterprise organization, supporting development of our autonomy platform and development ecosystem for AI Pilots. This leader will oversee Systems Engineering, System Architecture, Cybersecurity Engineering, and Safety/Airworthiness Engineering, building the teams and technical practices needed to deliver dependable, software-intensive autonomous systems.
 
You will connect operational product needs to measurable requirements, coherent architectures, and credible verification and assurance evidence. Partnering with Product, Software Engineering, Program Management, and Integration and Test teams, you will embed practical engineering rigor throughout the development lifecycle.

lists.content:
• Lead the team: Hire, develop, and lead the SE&A engineering disciplines, establishing clear responsibilities, technical standards, and effective cross-functional partnerships.
  • Establish the operating model: Define how SE&A engages with product and engineering teams, prioritizes competing demands, and allocates resources. Establish clear decision rights, escalation paths, and risk-proportionate engineering practices that improve delivery without unnecessary process overhead.
  • Own requirements and architecture: Guide requirements development and management, system modeling, architectural trade studies, interface definition, traceability, and change impact analysis.
  • Drive verification and validation planning: Establish system-level verification and validation strategies, measurable acceptance criteria, and evidence expectations. Partner with integration and test teams to demonstrate end-to-end capability.
  • Support software development: Integrate systems engineering and architecture into iterative planning, design, implementation, testing, release readiness, and sustainment.
  • Lead integrated assurance: Ensure cybersecurity, safety, and airworthiness considerations shape requirements, architecture, development, and verification from the outset.
  • Guide technical decisions: Lead risk-based design reviews, resolve cross-team technical issues, and provide evidence-based readiness recommendations while preserving designated approval and risk-acceptance authorities.
  • Improve engineering effectiveness: Establish and continuously improve practical methods, models, and workflows that connect requirements, architecture, implementation, and evidence. Measure success through earlier risk discovery, reduced rework, improved integration and release predictability, and timely closure of verification and assurance gaps.

• At least 15 years of applied systems engineering experience with complex, multidisciplinary systems, including direct involvement in development, integration, verification, and delivery.
  • Leadership: Demonstrated success leading engineering teams and senior technical talent, setting technical direction, and driving execution across organizational boundaries.
  • Requirements engineering: Deep experience with requirements development and management, including decomposition, allocation, traceability, interface requirements, baselining, and change control.
  • Architecture and modeling: Demonstrated ability to develop system architectures and use system models to analyze structure, behavior, interfaces, constraints, and design tradeoffs.
  • Verification and validation: Experience defining verification methods, measurable acceptance criteria, representative validation scenarios, and the evidence needed to assess system readiness.
  • Software lifecycle support: Experience applying systems engineering within software development lifecycles, including iterative development, continuous integration, testing, configuration management, and release processes.
  • Engineering effectiveness: Demonstrated ability to improve engineering maturity in an iterative development environment, tailoring rigor to technical risk and achieving measurable delivery benefits rather than process adoption alone.
  • Technical judgment: Ability to lead specialists across cybersecurity, safety, and airworthiness disciplines and communicate technical decisions and risks clearly to engineering, executive, and customer stakeholders.
  • Autonomous systems: Experience with autonomy software, AI-enabled systems, robotics, mission systems, or autonomy development platforms and tools.
  • A Degree in a relevant engineering or computer science discipline, or equivalent practical experience; an advanced technical degree is a plus

lists.text: Experience That Will Help You Stand Out:
lists.content:
• Engineering methods: Experience applying model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and scaling engineering practices without unnecessary process overhead. Familiarity with SysML and Cameo or similar system modeling tools.
  • Aerospace and defense: Experience delivering aerospace or defense systems with government customers, platform integrators, or operational users.
  • Safety and airworthiness: Practical experience with safety-critical development, hazard analysis, airworthiness planning, and compliance or certification evidence.
  • Applied cybersecurity: Experience translating threat assessments and security obligations into requirements, architectural controls, and verification activities.

You will own the strategy, planning and execution of complex, multi-phase test campaigns supporting the transition of autonomy capabilities from simulation and lab environments to full-scale flight test and operationally relevant mission scenarios, including multi-vehicle coordination. Using a disciplined fly–fix–fly methodology, you will drive rapid capability maturation while maintaining rigorous safety, configuration control, and mission assurance standards. 

This role will serve as the single technical authority for test execution across the portfolio of ACP efforts, responsible for managing risk, test readiness and driving test execution  Here, you will serve as primary focal to facilitate coordination across OEM partners, government customers and internal functional teams rs to deliver high-impact autonomy capabilities at scale.

lists.content:
• Act as Test Leader and technical lead for integration and flight test of Hivemind autonomy on group 5 ACP systems, including multi-aircraft coordination scenarios in LVC and empirical flight test scenarios.
  • Own test strategy and execution across the full development lifecycle, including system-level verification & validation, test phasing, and prioritization across SIL, HIL, simulation, ground, and flight test environments
  • Plan and execute large-scale flight test campaigns, including complex mission scenarios involving cooperative autonomy, human-machine teaming, and distributed systems
  • Serve as the final authority during mission autonomy test operations, directing test conduct and approving test plans, procedures, and execution flow
  • Coordinate cross-functional execution across software, hardware, systems engineering, flight operations, safety, and program leadership teams
  • Define mission-level performance metrics and success criteria, ensuring traceability from requirements to test outcomes and operational effectiveness
  • Own test infrastructure strategy, including large-scale simulation environments, SIL/HIL systems, aircraft integration labs, and flight test assets
  • Lead on-aircraft integration and flight test operations with platform OEM partners, including system configuration, software deployment, real-time troubleshooting, and post-flight data analysis
  • Serve as primary coordinator working with platform OEMs to define and enforce test readiness criteria (entry/exit), define safety-of-flight and mission risk management, airspace coordination and test hazard identification, analysis, and mitigation to ultimately make go/no-go decisions for progression into ground and flight test events
  • Establish and scale test processes, standards, and best practices aligned with DoD DT&E/OT&E expectations and operational test rigor

• Typically requires 12+ years of experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 10+ years with a Master’s; or 10+ years with a PhD; or equivalent experience
  • Demonstrated experience leading flight test or large-scale system integration efforts, including authority over test readiness, execution, and risk decisions
  • Strong background in full-scale aviation test environments, including aircraft integration, ground test, and flight operations
  • Experience with system-level verification & validation across multiple test environments (SIL, HIL, simulation, and flight)
  • Proven ability to plan and execute complex, multi-phase flight test campaigns involving multiple stakeholders and dependencies
  • Experience working cross-functionally across software, hardware, avionics, systems engineering, safety, and program teams
  • Strong understanding of safety-of-flight principles, risk management, and disciplined test execution in aviation environments
  • Proficiency in Python or similar tools for test automation, data analysis, or system validation
  • Excellent technical leadership and communication skills, including briefing to senior leadership and external customers
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a SECRET clearance; U.S. citizenship required

• Experience supporting Autonomous Collaborative Platforms (ACP), loyal wingman concepts, or multi-vehicle autonomous systems
  • Prior role as Flight Test Director, Test Conductor, or Lead Flight Test Engineer on full-scale aircraft programs
  • Familiarity with military aviation test processes, including DT&E and OT&E frameworks
  • Experience operating in or supporting government flight test ranges and operational environments
  • Background in autonomy, AI/ML-enabled systems, or human-machine teaming in aviation contexts
  • Experience with airworthiness processes, flight clearance, and configuration control for aircraft systems
  • Familiarity with tools such as Git, Jira/Azure DevOps, and CI/CD pipelines
  • Active SECRET clearance

Job Description:
The Director, USAF Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating rhythm that enables Shield AI’s UAS pursuits with the United States Air Force. Opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders retain ownership of their customers, capture strategies, account plans, and individual pursuits. This role serves as the connective tissue across those leaders, integrating information across the USAF portfolio and providing the VP, Mission Solutions for the X-BAT FoS with a clear, decision-ready view of campaign health, priorities, dependencies, risks, mitigations, and resource requirements. 
The Director connects USAF pursuits with relevant activity across other Services, allied and partner nations, product and engineering, government approvals, aircraft and test availability, internal investment, and industrial strategy. The role identifies shared dependencies and resource conflicts early, helps sequence competing demands, and coordinates the cross-functional support required for GTM leads to execute their captures effectively. 
The role maintains the authoritative USAF campaign picture and runs the operating cadence that turns portfolio insight into action. This includes campaign reviews, risk and dependency management, executive dashboards, action tracking, investment recommendations, and escalation of decisions requiring VP or executive attention. The Director ensures that information flows efficiently from the GTM organization to the VP, Mission Solutions and that leadership receives clear recommendations rather than unstructured reporting. 
GTM leads remain accountable for customer engagement, account planning, capture strategy, win strategy, price-to-win, proposal content, and pursuit outcomes. The Director enables their success by improving coordination, reducing friction around shared resources, and ensuring that the broader organization is aligned behind the highest-priority USAF opportunities.

Job Description:

The Director, USAF Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating rhythm that enables Shield AI’s UAS pursuits with the United States Air Force. Opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders retain ownership of their customers, capture strategies, account plans, and individual pursuits. This role serves as the connective tissue across those leaders, integrating information across the USAF portfolio and providing the VP, Mission Solutions for the X-BAT FoS with a clear, decision-ready view of campaign health, priorities, dependencies, risks, mitigations, and resource requirements. 

The Director connects USAF pursuits with relevant activity across other Services, allied and partner nations, product and engineering, government approvals, aircraft and test availability, internal investment, and industrial strategy. The role identifies shared dependencies and resource conflicts early, helps sequence competing demands, and coordinates the cross-functional support required for GTM leads to execute their captures effectively. 

The role maintains the authoritative USAF campaign picture and runs the operating cadence that turns portfolio insight into action. This includes campaign reviews, risk and dependency management, executive dashboards, action tracking, investment recommendations, and escalation of decisions requiring VP or executive attention. The Director ensures that information flows efficiently from the GTM organization to the VP, Mission Solutions and that leadership receives clear recommendations rather than unstructured reporting. 

GTM leads remain accountable for customer engagement, account planning, capture strategy, win strategy, price-to-win, proposal content, and pursuit outcomes. The Director enables their success by improving coordination, reducing friction around shared resources, and ensuring that the broader organization is aligned behind the highest-priority USAF opportunities.

lists.content:
This is a senior, high-visibility seat with authority, not a reporting function: 
  • Portfolio: Concurrent USAF pursuits across the X-BAT FoS, representing a multi-billion-dollar addressable opportunity. 
  • Team: Leadership by influence role, leveraging dedicated capture-operations and analyst support, with the expectation to build the team as the portfolio scales. 
  • Investment: Develops and co-stewards annual campaign and indirect investment against prioritized campaign returns. 
  • Governance: holds a standing seat in USAF bid/no-bid and investment-prioritization reviews and sets the agenda for the executive campaign review. 
  • Growth path: a pipeline role toward senior Department of the Navy growth or general-management leadership at Shield AI.

• Own the USAF view. Build and maintain the integrated USAF campaign picture across all X-BAT FoS USAF pursuits: strategy status, critical path, milestones, dependencies, decision points, and campaign health in one authoritative view. 
  • Enable GTM leads. Give each GTM lead the templates, playbooks, data, competitive inputs, cost and schedule inputs, and cross-functional access they need to build and execute their own capture plan. Success is measured by their outcomes, not by your visibility. 
  • Synchronize functions. Coordinate engineering, product, export, legal, contracts, finance, government relations, and business operations against a single prioritized campaign plan so GTM leads are not individually negotiating for the same scarce resources. 
  • Surface conflicts between campaigns. Identify where two or more campaigns compete for the same aircraft, test window, engineering effort, approval bandwidth, or indirect dollar, and bring executive leadership a clear tradeoff and a recommendation. 
  • Drive executive decision quality. Run the operating cadence — campaign reviews, gate reviews, risk registers, action tracking, and executive dashboards — so leadership receives timely, accurate, decision-ready information on bid/no-bid, investment, and prioritization. 
  • Steward indirect investment. Work with Finance and Business Operations to track campaign investment, indirect spend, and resource planning against campaign priorities and expected return. 
  • Scale discipline. Systematically capture lessons learned across capture efforts—both what worked and what did not, and translate them into repeatable tools, templates, metrics, and playbooks so every new campaign begins with a stronger foundation than the last. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
  • Roll up your sleeves. Personally drive the execution of critical customer responses (RFI, RFP, CSO, and other solicitation vehicles) — assembling cross-functional inputs, holding the response schedule, and driving on-time submission, while the GTM lead retains ownership of win strategy, price-to-win, and proposal content.

• This role is accountable for: the integrated USAF campaign plan; the operating cadence and campaign-health reporting; identification and escalation of cross-campaign dependencies, conflicts, and risks; path-to-win roadmap; and recommendations on investment prioritization and sequencing. 
  • Opportunity GTM leads are accountable for: customer relationships and engagement, capture strategy, win strategy and price-to-win for their pursuit, proposal content, and the bid/no-bid recommendation for their opportunity. 
  • Government Relations, Export, Legal, and Contracts are accountable for: data-rights, political and legislative engagements and outcomes, disclosure determinations, legal positions, and contracting terms. 
  • Engineering and Product are accountable for: technical solution definition, configuration decisions, and performance commitments. 
  • Program Management is accountable for: execution of customer-funded programs after award. 
  • External customer engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead.

• U.S. person as defined by ITAR (22 CFR 120.62), with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. 
  • 12–20+ years in capture management, program management, strategic operations, business operations, technical program management, or a comparable cross-functional leadership role. 
  • Demonstrated success leading highly complex initiatives with multiple interdependent workstreams across engineering, business development, operations, finance, and executive leadership. 
  • Working knowledge of how USAF programs actually get funded and fielded — SAF/AQ and HAF staffing processes, PEO and program-office dynamics, the PPBE/POM cycle, and rapid-acquisition pathways such as OTAs, CSOs, SBIR/STRATFI, AFWERX, and the transition from prototype to program of record. 
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to drive accountability across functions and geographies. 
  • Strong executive communication: leadership briefings, dashboards, metrics, and decision-support materials that lead to decisions rather than discussion. 
  • Deep operational rigor in integrated schedules, critical path, milestones, action tracking, dependency management, and risk mitigation. 
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments with competing priorities across multiple time zones. 
  • A service orientation toward the GTM leads this role supports, and the judgment to know when to escalate versus resolve quietly.

• Active DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and current Special Access Program accesses. 
  • Experience supporting DoW, aerospace, autonomy, robotics, aviation, or defense-technology organizations. 
  • Experience within business development, capture, proposal operations, strategic planning, or growth organizations running multiple concurrent U.S. Government pursuits. 
  • Familiarity with the export and international mechanisms that shape USAF pursuits — foreign disclosure determinations, FMS/DCS pathways, and security cooperation planning — where allied demand affects the USAF business case. 
  • Experience building executive dashboards, KPIs, operational scorecards, or portfolio health metrics. 
  • Experience supporting executive staff, chief-of-staff organizations, Strategy and Operations teams, or enterprise PMOs. 
  • Fluency with integrated schedule and work-management tooling (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira), and an advanced degree or relevant certification (MBA, PMP, Lean Six Sigma) is a plus but not required.

• GTM leads report that the role makes their campaign easier to run, not heavier to report on. 
  • USAF path-to-win is in place and running on a predictable, repeatable cadence that the organization can plan against. 
  • Cross-campaign resource and timing conflicts reach leadership as a decision with a recommendation. 
  • Executive leadership have an accurate health picture of the USAF X-BAT FoS portfolio and make investment calls with confidence. 
  • Campaign mechanisms are reused across opportunities, and each new pursuit stands up measurably faster than the previous one.

Shield AI’s core values — Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, and Pursue Excellence — are how we hire, promote, and make hard calls. This role in particular demands servant leadership: success is measured by the outcomes of the GTM leads it supports. 

Veterans and transitioning service members: we actively seek candidates with U.S. Air Force operational, staff, or acquisition experience, and we support military-to-civilian transitions.

• Lead a team to sustain and grow the Company’s Middle East & Asia-Pacific Direct Commercial Sales Programs
  • Manage the portfolio of programs to meet or exceed company Annual Operating Plan objectives
  • Deliver proven, exceptional, and reliable performance in support of customer/end-user’s mission through flawless execution of Program Management and team leadership.
  • Shape/codify processes and procedures to effectively collaborate, motivate, and manage relevant stakeholders required to successfully deliver programs early, under budget, and with exceptional technical performance.
  • Constantly drive a healthy tension between all functions to ensure a holistic approach to delivering on Shield AI’s commitments.
  • Astutely balance and rebalance shifting customer priories related to cost, schedule, and technical parameters of programs. 
  • Guide the initiation and sustainment of DCS contracts for Shield AI’s V-BAT systems.
  • Lead the identification, development, and implementation of process improvements for DCS program management processes and tools 
  • Provide hands-on management of projects/programs as needed while the program grows
  • Oversee customer relationships and act as the key escalation point for programs, projects, and operational performance issues 
  • Drive efforts to attain budget, schedule, and scope requirements
  • Drive the accurate and timely tracking and reporting of budget, resource, and project management standard metrics 
  • Complete critical path analyses including the evaluation of potential means to accelerate the pace or mitigate identified risks
  • Identify potential bottlenecks or delays in programs and drive efforts to ensure projects stay on schedule
  • Partner with leadership to guide prioritization of projects and utilization of resources 
  • Hire and supervise a team of project and program managers as needed to support Shield AI’s rapid growth in the international sector

  • Establish and lead a consistent cadence of well-organized, well-facilitated, and effective meetings, including driving all preparation and follow up activities
