description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

You will build and lead the Guidance & Control (G&C) team for Ranger, a fully autonomous aircraft designed for conventional runway takeoff and landing. You will own the team’s technical direction, development roadmap, and project execution, delivering flight control and flight-autonomy capabilities from requirements and architecture through flight verification.

lists.content:
• Build and lead the Ranger G&C team. Define staffing needs, establish clear technical ownership, and develop the team through mentorship, design reviews, and hands-on problem solving.
  • Own the G&C development roadmap. Translate program objectives into a phased plan for requirements development, algorithm maturation, simulation capabilities, software integration, verification, and flight testing. Establish measurable milestones and align priorities with program leadership and partner teams.
  • Own project execution and delivery. Scope and estimate work, allocate resources, manage schedules and cross-team dependencies, and track progress against deliverables. Identify technical and schedule risks early, drive mitigation plans, and communicate trade-offs and resource needs.
  • Define and deliver the G&C architecture, including Auto-Taxi and ATOL algorithms, inner- and outer-loop control laws, guidance, trajectory validation, flight-mode logic, and control allocation. Maintain stable, predictable aircraft performance through actuator constraints, disturbances, uncertainty, and defined degraded conditions.
  • Lead integration between flight autonomy and mission autonomy through A-GRA-aligned interfaces. Establish clear responsibilities for mission-level decision-making and vehicle-level execution, including command validation, flight-mode transitions, status reporting, and contingency coordination.
  • Lead development and validation of high-fidelity 6DOF simulation capabilities. Establish model fidelity requirements, validation plans, and uncertainty bounds to support control development, vehicle-level trades, and credible pre-flight performance predictions.
  • Own the G&C verification strategy and supporting compliance evidence. Define requirements-based acceptance criteria and verification coverage across linear and nonlinear analysis, Monte Carlo campaigns, sensitivity and failure studies, and software- and hardware-in-the-loop testing.
  • Drive cross-disciplinary trades with propulsion, aerodynamics, actuation, state estimation, embedded software, and autonomy teams. Translate G&C performance needs into subsystem requirements and resolve interface, timing, and integration issues.
  • Lead G&C preparation and analysis for ground and flight testing, including test-point selection, envelope-expansion planning, pre-flight predictions, and post-flight reconstruction. Provide evidence-based flight-readiness recommendations, resolve simulation-to-test discrepancies, and drive verified corrective changes.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in flight controls, GNC, or autonomous aircraft development, with demonstrated technical ownership of flight-vehicle systems from requirements and design through integration and flight test.
  • Experience building or leading engineering teams, including establishing technical direction, assigning ownership, mentoring engineers, and delivering complex development efforts through coordinated team execution.
  • Demonstrated ownership of technical roadmaps and project execution, including work scoping, effort estimation, staffing plans, milestone definition, dependency management, and technical risk reduction.
  • Deep expertise in aircraft flight dynamics, classical and modern control theory, nonlinear systems, and fixed-wing control law design, including stability, performance, and robustness across the operating envelope.
  • Strong experience developing or validating high-fidelity 6DOF simulations and using ground- and flight-test data to identify modeling limitations, characterize uncertainty, and improve predictive capability.
  • Experience defining and executing requirements-based verification strategies, including linear and nonlinear analysis, Monte Carlo studies, integrated testing, and flight-test analysis.
  • Experience integrating guidance, control, and flight-mode logic, with a clear understanding of the division between flight autonomy and mission autonomy and the interfaces needed to support feasible vehicle-level execution.
  • Proficiency in C++, with experience implementing, reviewing, and debugging G&C or simulation software and addressing real-time execution constraints. Experience using MATLAB and/or Python for engineering analysis and verification.
  • Strong technical judgment and communication skills, with the ability to resolve ambiguous, cross-disciplinary problems and clearly communicate decisions, assumptions, risks, and limitations to engineers and program leadership.

    • Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading development, integration, or flight verification of autonomous fixed-wing aircraft.
  • Direct experience defining, implementing, or verifying A-GRA-aligned interfaces, or integrating flight autonomy with a separate mission-autonomy provider.
  • Experience building a G&C team or development capability for a new aircraft program, including establishing technical practices, simulation infrastructure, verification workflows, and development plans.
  • Experience applying flight safety and airworthiness processes, deriving flight control requirements, and producing supporting artifacts such as simulation descriptions, verification reports, and flying-qualities analyses.
  • Experience evaluating navigation errors, air data uncertainty, altitude-sensing limitations, latency, and data validity against flight control and ATOL performance requirements.
  • Experience establishing software- and hardware-in-the-loop capabilities, automated regression testing, and CI/CD workflows using Linux, Git, and modern C++ development practices.
  • Experience integrating steady-state or transient NPSS propulsion models or model outputs into a 6DOF simulation environment.
  • Experience leading G&C execution in developmental flight-test programs, balancing rapid iteration with configuration control, verification rigor, and disciplined flight-readiness assessments.

Job Description:

In this role, you will design, implement, and flight-test autonomous shipboard recovery guidance for XBAT, with an emphasis on precision recovery to a moving ship in GPS-degraded and GPS-denied environments. Working within an established G&C team, you will own recovery guidance algorithms and their integration with relative navigation, flight controls, and recovery hardware. 

We are seeking someone with direct experience taking shipboard recovery guidance from algorithm development through implementation and flight testing.

lists.content:
• Design and implement ship-relative guidance for approach, station keeping, alignment, and terminal recovery. 

    • Develop deck-motion compensation and landing-timing strategies that account for navigation uncertainty, aircraft response, control authority, and touchdown or capture constraints. 

    • Work closely with state estimation and sensing teams to define relative-navigation requirements and ensure recovery guidance remains robust to measurement errors, latency, and intermittent sensor availability. 

    • Implement recovery sequencing and contingency logic, including hold, wave-off, go-around, retry, and responses to degraded or lost navigation. 

    • Develop and integrate real-time guidance software in C++, working with flight controls, autonomy, embedded software, and recovery-system teams. 

    • Define recovery performance requirements and verify them through 6DOF simulation, Monte Carlo analysis, software-in-the-loop testing, and hardware-in-the-loop testing. 

    • Support test planning, flight readiness assessments, and flight operations. Analyze test data, diagnose performance shortfalls, and drive improvements between tests. 

    • Provide technical direction within the recovery-guidance effort, mentor engineers, and communicate design decisions, limitations, and test results across teams.

• Demonstrated hands-on experience designing, implementing, and flight-testing guidance laws for autonomous shipboard recovery, including recovery using relative navigation without GPS/GNSS. 

    • Strong understanding of moving-platform guidance, ship-relative reference frames, deck motion, and terminal position, velocity, and attitude constraints. 

    • Experience integrating guidance with relative-navigation systems and assessing the closed-loop effects of navigation bias, noise, latency, and dropouts. 

    • Strong background in flight dynamics and guidance and control, including the relationship between guidance demands, aircraft tracking bandwidth, and available control authority. 

    • Proficiency in C++ for real-time algorithm implementation and MATLAB/Simulink or Python for algorithm development and analysis. 

    • Experience executing verification and validation through simulation, hardware integration, flight testing, and post-flight analysis. 

    • Demonstrated ability to own a technical capability, resolve problems across subsystem boundaries, and work effectively with navigation, controls, software, and test engineers. 

    • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

• Full-scale, at-sea flight-test experience with autonomous shipboard recovery. 

  • VTOL or rotorcraft experience involving precision recovery to constrained or significantly moving landing platforms. 

  • Experience characterizing recovery performance across ship motion, wind over deck, ship airwake, turbulence, and degraded visibility. 

  • Experience integrating vision, infrared, lidar, radar, or cooperative RF sensing into a relative-navigation and recovery system. 

  • Experience supporting ship–aircraft dynamic-interface testing, recovery-envelope development, flight safety, or airworthiness. 

  • Familiarity with Linux-based development, Git, automated testing, and CI/CD workflows. 

  • Ability to obtain S//SAR access.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to work in a team-oriented, cross-functional environment
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills

You will lead prototype build execution and the manufacturing setup of our new Seattle-area facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll build the production team, establish the factory’s operating system and deliver the readiness needed to scale aircraft production safely, reliably and efficiently. 

This role carries accountability across the full journey: turning lessons from development builds into a repeatable production system, then leading that operation against safety, quality, delivery and cost commitments. lists.content:
Lead prototype builds and new product introduction 

  • Own the day-to-day execution of X-BAT prototype and development aircraft builds, including assembly, integration, rework and build support for testing. 
  • Partner with Program Management to establish achievable build schedules, resource plans and milestones, making constraints and trade-offs visible early. 
  • Work with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering through build-test-learn cycles, ensuring build issues are captured, resolved and reflected in future designs and production processes. 
  • Plan and execute pre-series builds to prove tooling, work instructions, material flow, process controls and workforce readiness before production ramp. 
  • Maintain configuration discipline and aircraft traceability throughout development builds in partnership with Engineering and Quality. 

    • Establish the Seattle production operation 

  • Lead manufacturing setup and operational readiness for X-Forge 3, working with Facilities and Manufacturing Engineering on factory layout, equipment installation, commissioning and production flow. 
  • Recruit, develop and lead the production organization, building capable frontline leadership and a skilled aircraft assembly team. 
  • Own production staffing, training and capacity plans, aligning investment and workforce growth with program demand. 
  • Drive launch readiness across people, tooling, materials, processes and quality, with clear owners and closure plans for gaps. 
  • Lead the transition from prototype operations into Seattle production, ensuring build knowledge and lessons learned transfer with the work. 

    • Deliver and scale aircraft production 

  • Own production execution against safety, quality, delivery and cost targets as X-BAT moves through initial production and into sustained rate. 
  • Establish daily operating routines, visual management and escalation processes that surface problems early and drive timely resolution. 
  • Improve throughput, labor productivity, first-pass quality and schedule adherence through practical Lean methods and structured problem-solving. 
  • Partner with Supply Chain and Planning to align material availability, supplier readiness and outsourced manufacturing with the production plan. 
  • Work with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to eliminate recurring build issues and embed permanent corrective actions. 
  • Deploy digital manufacturing tools and appropriate automation to improve execution, traceability and scalability. 
  • Give leadership a clear view of production performance, launch readiness, risks and the decisions needed to maintain progress.

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing or a related technical field. 
  • 10+ years of experience in aerospace or comparable advanced manufacturing, including at least 5 years leading production teams. 
  • Demonstrated experience leading prototype or new product introduction builds and carrying a product into sustained production. 
  • Proven ability to build and scale manufacturing operations, including workforce development, capacity planning and production systems. 
  • Experience leading complex assembly and integration operations with demanding quality, configuration and traceability requirements. 
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing readiness, tooling validation, material coordination and production launch. 
  • Track record of improving safety, quality, delivery and cost through Lean manufacturing and structured problem-solving. 
  • Ability to lead across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Program Management, resolving competing priorities and driving clear accountability. 
  • A hands-on leadership style, with the ability to move between long-term factory planning and detailed problem-solving on the floor.

• Direct experience taking a new aircraft program from prototype through initial and rate production. 
  • Experience establishing a new manufacturing facility or transferring production between sites. 
  • Experience in aircraft final assembly, systems integration and production test. 
  • Familiarity with aerospace quality systems, including AS9100, and digital manufacturing and traceability tools. 
  • Experience managing production interfaces with outsourced manufacturing partners and complex supplier networks. 
  • Advanced degree or relevant training in manufacturing leadership, program management or production launch.

You will build the aircraft quality organization and establish the quality capability for our new Seattle-area production facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll own product and process quality across prototype, pre-series and production builds, ensuring that lessons from development become effective controls as the program scales. 

This role owns the Quality Management System, quality engineering, inspection, nonconformance management and audit readiness for the X-BAT manufacturing operation. You’ll partner with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Production and Supply Chain to prevent defects, resolve recurring problems and deliver aircraft that meet technical, customer and applicable regulatory requirements. 

We need a technically credible leader who can build practical, scalable systems, make sound decisions under schedule pressure and challenge senior stakeholders constructively while keeping execution moving.

lists.content:
Build quality into prototype and launch 

  • Lead quality planning and execution for X-BAT prototype and development builds, establishing appropriate inspection, test evidence and build records as designs evolve. 
  • Partner with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering to identify product and process risks, define critical controls and build quality requirements into tooling, work instructions and test plans. 
  • Establish configuration and traceability controls with Engineering and Production, ensuring each aircraft’s build status, deviations and nonconformances are understood and documented. 
  • Capture lessons from build, integration and test issues, and drive their incorporation into design changes, manufacturing processes and future builds. 
  • Define quality readiness criteria for pre-series builds and production launch, validating inspection methods, process controls, workforce competence and closure of significant risks. 

    • Establish the Seattle quality operation 

  • Recruit, develop and lead the quality team, building the technical capability and frontline support needed as aircraft production grows. 
  • Establish and maintain a lean, effective QMS for X-Forge 3, aligned with Shield AI’s wider quality framework, AS9100, ISO 9001 and applicable customer requirements. 
  • Lead certification readiness and internal, customer and external audits, driving timely closure and sustained effectiveness of corrective actions. 
  • Set up receiving, in-process and final inspection capability, including measurement equipment, calibration, training and quality records, in partnership with relevant functions. 

    • Deliver quality at rate 

  • Own production quality performance, using first-pass yield, defects, rework and escapes to focus action where it improves aircraft quality and production flow. 
  • Lead containment, root cause analysis and corrective action for manufacturing quality issues, with clear functional ownership and verification that fixes prevent recurrence. 
  • Own the nonconformance and MRB process, ensuring disposition decisions follow approved technical authority and that affected hardware remains controlled. 
  • Partner with Supply Chain and supplier quality teams to resolve incoming quality issues and improve supplier performance before defects disrupt aircraft builds. 
  • Work with Engineering and Production to define acceptance evidence and ensure aircraft meet approved requirements before release. 
  • Use digital quality tools and manufacturing data to strengthen traceability, expose trends and reduce manual administration as production scales. 
  • Give leadership a clear view of quality performance, product risks and readiness; escalate or stop affected work when requirements or product integrity cannot be assured.

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality or a related technical field. 
  • 10+ years of leadership experience in quality, product assurance or reliability within aerospace, defense technology or high-reliability manufacturing.

Job Description 

The Head of Operational Excellence will lead operational excellence across Shield AI’s Group 3 UAV manufacturing in Frisco, TX (V-BAT) and Group 5 UAV manufacturing in Seattle, WA (X-BAT). Based in Frisco, this leader will create, deploy, and actively manage manufacturing KPIs and performance systems across both sites, embedding operating rhythms that improve accountability, visibility, and results. 
 
You will be responsible for instilling a culture of execution excellence, embedding structured problem-solving practices, and delivering measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery, and productivity. This includes leading the development and governance of operational standards—such as visual management, 5S, and root cause analysis—while owning the manufacturing budget cycle, business rhythm, and executive reporting interface across both locations. This role partners with engineering, production, quality, and business functions to execute high-priority improvement initiatives, support V-BAT production, and establish operational excellence as X-BAT progresses through prototype and into rate production. 

Do you have the expertise and leadership to embed excellence into the fabric of autonomous defense manufacturing?

lists.content:
• Create, deploy, and actively manage consistent manufacturing KPIs and performance dashboards across both sites to drive visibility and accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity. 

    • Define, train, deploy, and continually improve operational standards across V-BAT manufacturing in Frisco and X-BAT manufacturing in Seattle, including 5S, root cause analysis, and visual management. 

      • Develop and institutionalize the manufacturing budget process across both sites, including forecasting, controls, and performance tracking. 

        • Set financial targets in collaboration with operations and finance teams and drive adherence to budget and cost goals. 

          • Lead high-impact cross-functional improvement initiatives across both sites to improve quality, delivery, efficiency, productivity, and cost performance. 

            • Prepare and coordinate senior and executive-level reporting packages for Manufacturing leadership reviews. 

              • Partner with production, quality, and engineering teams to deploy Lean and continuous improvement practices, adapting execution to the needs of established production and prototype-to-rate manufacturing. 

                • Own business office functions for Manufacturing across both sites, including goal tracking, KPI dashboards, and process governance. 

                  • Coach and train teams and leaders across both sites to elevate operational discipline, share effective practices, and sustain improvements.

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, or related field. 

    • Experience leading operational excellence, Lean, or business office programs within a manufacturing environment, with the ability to lead improvement across multiple sites. 

      • Demonstrated ability to design, roll out, and sustain structured operational standards and improvement systems. 

        • Strong background in budgeting, reporting, and performance management at a senior level. 

          • Excellent communication skills and experience preparing executive-level summaries and presentations.

• Master’s degree or formal Lean Six Sigma certification. 

    • Experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware manufacturing environments. 

      • Proficiency with digital tools for KPI visualization, reporting automation, and business process tracking. 

        • Track record of influencing change across large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations and multiple sites.

lists.content:
User Research & Product Discovery 

  • Lead customer research efforts across product development, customer engagement, and solutions teams to identify pain points, workflows, unmet needs, and product opportunities. 
  • Establish scalable mechanisms for gathering, synthesizing, and communicating user insights throughout the product development lifecycle. 
  • Translate customer and operational feedback into actionable product recommendations, requirements, and design initiatives. 

    • Product Design & User Experience 

  • Design end-to-end workflows across autonomy development, simulation, testing, analysis, deployment, and operations. 
  • Create intuitive experiences for highly technical users including autonomy engineers, software developers, operators, and mission planners. 
  • Simplify complex system architectures, data flows, infrastructure tooling, and AI workflows into understandable user experiences. 
  • Own the end-to-end experience of the product including training, documentation, tutorials, and overall workflows – help our users get the most of the product. 

    • Strategic Product Leadership 

  • Partner closely with Product Managers to shape product vision, roadmap priorities, and go-to-market strategies. 
  • Drive alignment across Product, Engineering, Design, and Executive Leadership through compelling narratives, prototypes, and visual storytelling. 
  • Advocate for user-centered decision making in a highly technical and engineering-driven environment. 

    • Design Practice, Systems & Organizational Scale 

  • Establish and evolve design standards, design systems, UX principles, and product design best practices across Shield AI. 
  • Raise the quality bar for product design, usability, consistency, and customer experience. 
  • Grow the product design function by mentoring a small team of designers, shaping design culture, and staying actively involved in critical design work. 
  • Champion design wins and impact across the organization, highlighting the important role design plays in delivering successful products. 

    • AI-Native Product Design & Agentic Workflows 

  • Define the future user experience for AI-assisted autonomy development, simulation, testing, deployment, and operational workflows. 
  • Design human-AI collaboration models that enable users to effectively leverage AI agents, copilots, and foundation-model-powered systems. 
  • Partner with Product, AI Research, and Engineering teams to create new interaction patterns for agent orchestration, autonomy generation, scenario creation, test generation, and mission planning. 
  • Develop frameworks for trust, transparency, explainability, and human oversight within AI-assisted workflows. 
  • Help establish industry-leading design patterns for Physical AI development platforms and agent-driven software systems.

• 10+ years of experience in Product Design, UX Design, Human Factors, or related fields. 
  • Proven track record designing and shipping complex technical products, developer tools, platforms, infrastructure software, data-dense applications, or enterprise systems. 
  • Deep technical fluency and ability to effectively collaborate with senior engineering leaders on architecture, technical constraints, and software development workflows. 
  • Strong experience conducting user research and translating insights into product strategy and design solutions.

lists.content:
•Own daily operations and technical readiness for HIL and infrastructure laboratories, ensuring systems, workspaces, tools, documentation, and shared resources are available and ready for engineering use

•Build, install, configure, inspect, and maintain HIL racks, test benches, compute systems, network equipment, storage, power distribution, simulation hardware, flight hardware, and supporting lab infrastructure

•Own and maintain accurate asset control for lab and program equipment, including receiving, tagging, serial-number tracking, location, custody, configuration, calibration, maintenance, spares, and disposition records

•Manage lab schedules, equipment reservations, maintenance windows, integration priorities, and competing cross-program demands in coordination with software, hardware, systems, test, and program teams

•Perform wiring and fabrication tasks such as cable assembly, connector installation, crimping, soldering, continuity checks, cable routing, rack assembly, panel modification, bracket installation, and minor mechanical rework using approved procedures

•Read, apply, and update wiring diagrams, electrical schematics, rack elevations, mechanical and installation drawings, cable and port maps, bills of material, work instructions, and interface-control documentation

•Support software development by provisioning and restoring development and test environments, imaging computers, installing approved software, managing configurations, collecting logs, and assisting with automated lab workflows

•Diagnose and resolve lab issues across power, wiring, compute, networking, software, instrumentation, and mechanical interfaces using appropriate test equipment, logs, drawings, and structured troubleshooting methods

•Manage procurement coordination, incoming inspection, shipping and receiving, vendor repair activity, consumables, tool control, calibration, equipment staging, and capacity planning for lab growth and program execution

•Establish, maintain, and enforce lab standards for safety, access, cybersecurity, export control, electrostatic-discharge protection, foreign-object-debris prevention, cleanliness, labeling, and configuration management

•Own and maintain lab operating procedures, build records, maintenance logs, configuration baselines, status dashboards, issue trackers, and work instructions that provide traceability and support knowledge sharing

•Support customer integration events, demonstrations, operational exercises, and evaluations by preparing representative lab environments, reproducing field issues, and incorporating approved updates into HIL configurations and test infrastructure

•Typically requires 5+ years of hands-on experience supporting engineering laboratories, integration and test facilities, avionics, mission systems, electronics, IT infrastructure, industrial equipment, or comparable technical operations. A four-year engineering degree is not required. Relevant demonstrated experience, military service, vocational training, or technical certifications are acceptable pathways to qualification.

•Hands-on experience operating or supporting engineering laboratories, integration facilities, test environments, maintenance operations, or mission systems in the defense, aerospace, aviation, robotics, manufacturing, or another mission-critical industry

•Demonstrated experience assembling, installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting electro-mechanical equipment, test infrastructure, computing systems, electronics, or avionics hardware

•Experience maintaining accountable assets, serialized hardware, inventory, tools, calibration, spares, shipping and receiving, maintenance history, or configuration records

•Strong planning and organizational skills with demonstrated ability to own shared lab operations and coordinate schedules, equipment availability, maintenance activities, priorities, and dependencies across multiple teams or programs

•Ability to read and work from wiring diagrams, electrical schematics, mechanical and installation drawings, rack layouts, bills of material, work instructions, and technical manuals

•Competence with wiring, cable and connector work, fabrication, hand tools, digital multimeters, continuity testing, rack integration, and safe electro-mechanical troubleshooting

•Comfort working with Windows- and Linux-based computers, installing and configuring software, collecting logs, documenting technical work, and communicating clearly with software and hardware engineers

•Ability to obtain a SECRET clearance

•A degree in engineering technology; an associate degree in electronics technology, information technology, avionics, or a related technical discipline; equivalent military or vocational training; or relevant demonstrated experience

•Experience supporting HIL, SIL, VIL, avionics, flight-system, robotics, or systems-integration laboratories

•Familiarity with Python, Bash, PowerShell, or another scripting language for asset records, health checks, configuration, data collection, reporting, or routine lab workflows

•Experience supporting software-development or continuous-integration teams, including environment provisioning, software deployment, source control, build systems, automated testing, or test orchestration

•Experience with aircraft systems, autonomy software, embedded computing, real-time simulation, sensors, communications equipment, or uncrewed vehicle integration

•Familiarity with Ethernet networking, managed switches, IP addressing, serial communications, CAN, time synchronization, remote access, and basic network troubleshooting

•Experience with CAD viewers or tools used to review or update electrical drawings, mechanical drawings, rack layouts, cable drawings, or lab floor plans

As the Simulation Framework Lead, you will lead and mentor a team of simulation framework engineers responsible for building, extending, and maintaining the modeling and simulation (M&S) interface layers between core autonomy and various simulation backends (NGTS, AFSIM, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and HMSF). Integration teams own program-level software integration; your team partners with and supports them by providing the framework, plugins, interfaces, and technical troubleshooting needed to resolve simulation-software integration issues. You will drive the strategic simulation roadmap for Hivemind Solutions. While continuing to support programs reliant on HMSSimBlocks today, you will partner closely with Hivemind Platform (HMP) as they transition from SimBlocks to the new Hivemind Simulation Framework (HMSF). You will act as the key advocate for HMS program requirements, drive feature inputs into HMP's HMSF product roadmap, and lay out a clear, phased migration path from HMSSimBlocks to HMSF across all HMS portfolios.

As the Simulation Framework Lead, you will lead and mentor a team of simulation framework engineers responsible for building, extending, and maintaining the modeling and simulation (M&S) interface layers between core autonomy and various simulation backends (NGTS, AFSIM, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and HMSF). Integration teams own program-level software integration; your team partners with and supports them by providing the framework, plugins, interfaces, and technical troubleshooting needed to resolve simulation-software integration issues. You will drive the strategic simulation roadmap for Hivemind Solutions. While continuing to support programs reliant on HMSSimBlocks today, you will partner closely with Hivemind Platform (HMP) as they transition from SimBlocks to the new Hivemind Simulation Framework (HMSF). You will act as the key advocate for HMS program requirements, drive feature inputs into HMP's HMSF product roadmap, and lay out a clear, phased migration path from HMSSimBlocks to HMSF across all HMS portfolios.

lists.content:
• Lead, mentor, and grow a team of specialized C++ and Python simulation engineers. Set technical direction, conduct performance reviews, and foster high engineering rigor.
  • Collaborate directly with HMP engineering and product leadership to drive HMS program requirements into the Hivemind Simulation Framework (HMSF), ensuring HMSF accommodates complex DoD program needs, custom sensors, and multi-domain environments.
  • Architect and lay out the phased migration roadmap from HMSSimBlocks to HMSF, ensuring uninterrupted operational support for active programs using HMSSimBlocks while guiding teams toward HMSF adoption.
  • Oversee the design and maintenance of baseline simulation adapters, plugins, and interfaces for NGTS, AFSIM, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and HMSF.
  • Align simulation frameworks with defense interface standards (e.g., GRID/JSE, CIGI, CSF, DDS), ensuring seamless interoperability across DoD-recognized threat and visual simulators.
  • Partner cross-functionally with HMS program leads, integration teams, and autonomy teams to ensure simulation environments accurately support hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) and software-in-the-loop (SIL) testing needs.
  • Champion developer enablement by providing standardized simulation templates, documentation, and framework support to downstream engineering teams.

• Typically requires a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related technical discipline and 7+ years of related experience (or 5+ years with a Master’s, or equivalent practical experience), including experience in technical leadership, team lead, or engineering management.
  • Deep software engineering background in C++ and Python within Linux environments.
  • Practical experience with modeling and simulation frameworks (such as AFSIM, NGTS, SimBlocks/HMSF, or similar) and distributed simulation middleware (DDS, DIS/HLA).
  • Proven ability to partner with platform/product teams (e.g., HMP) to influence external product roadmaps and drive program requirements upstream.
  • Demonstrated experience managing software platform migrations while maintaining operational stability for legacy systems.
  • Familiarity with defense simulation interface standards (GRID/JSE, CIGI, CSF) and network protocols (UDP/TCP).
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an active U.S. SECRET security clearance (U.S. citizenship required).

As the Instructor & Customer Success Manager, you will lead a team responsible for developing and delivering classroom, simulator, flight, maintenance, and scenario-based training for Shield AI products. You will ensure customers in Ukraine have the knowledge, skills, and confidence required to safely operate, maintain, and effectively employ our technology. 

You will be responsible for instructor development, training quality, operational readiness, curriculum standards, and customer satisfaction. This is a hands-on leadership position that requires close collaboration with customers, engineering, product, flight operations, business development, and other internal teams. The ideal candidate is an experienced training leader, an effective communicator, and a credible UAS professional who is comfortable operating in dynamic domestic and international environments.

  • Deliver instruction and provide hands-on training support when mission or staffing needs require it.
  • Partner with engineering, product, design, and flight-operations teams to incorporate customer and instructor feedback into product and training improvements.
  • Support new-product validation, testing, field evaluations, and the development of training capabilities for new product releases.

lists.content:
• Lead, develop, and mentor a team of customer training professionals and UAV instructors.
  • Establish team priorities, performance expectations, staffing plans, and professional-development pathways.
  • Oversee the development and delivery of classroom, simulator, flight, maintenance, and scenario-based training for Shield AI products.
  • Ensure training programs prepare customers to safely operate, maintain, deploy, and effectively employ Shield AI systems.
  • Maintain high instructional standards through instructor qualification, observation, coaching, certification, and continuous evaluation.
  • Lead the development and standardization of curricula, lesson plans, lecture materials, simulator scenarios, practical exercises, assessments, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure student training records, instructor qualifications, course materials, and program metrics remain current and accurate.
  • Coordinate training schedules, aircraft, simulators, facilities, airspace, frequency management, personnel, and other operational resources.
  • Communicate directly with customers and partner-force leadership regarding training requirements, student progress, operational readiness, and program outcomes.
  • Build lasting customer relationships through continuous engagement, refresher training, and support for effective product utilization.
  • Adapt training for students with varying technical abilities, operational backgrounds, cultural contexts, and levels of experience.
  • Support domestic and international training events, including extended deployments when required. 
  • Deliver instruction and provide hands-on training support when mission or staffing needs require it.
  • Partner with engineering, product, design, and flight-operations teams to incorporate customer and instructor feedback into product and training improvements.
  • Support new-product validation, testing, field evaluations, and the development of training capabilities for new product releases.
  • Collaborate with business-development and sales teams to demonstrate Shield AI products to prospective customers. 
  • Establish and monitor training-program metrics, identify performance gaps, and implement improvements that increase safety, consistency, scalability, and customer success.
  • Ensure training activities comply with applicable company policies, safety requirements, security procedures, aviation regulations, and customer expectations.

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Five or more years of experience in technical, aviation, military, or UAS training.
  • Two or more years of experience leading instructors, training teams, or comparable operational teams.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and delivering classroom, simulator, flight, maintenance, or scenario-based instruction.
  • Working knowledge of UAS operations, flight and mission planning, aviation safety, and training operations.
  • Ability and willingness to travel internationally up to 50%, including for extended periods when required.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Fluent in Ukrainian
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical and operational information to audiences with varying levels of experience.
  • Experience managing multiple training events, resources, schedules, and customer requirements in a dynamic environment.
  • Effective, highly logical problem-solver who remains focused on safety, learning outcomes, and customer success.
  • Ability to work across organizational boundaries while maintaining a big-picture perspective and attention to operational details.

• Graduate degree in education, instructional design, aviation, engineering, business, or a related field.
  • Significant UAS experience as a pilot in command, instructor, maintainer, or mission operator.
  • More than 1,000 hours of UAS pilot-in-command experience.
  • Experience instructing or operating Group 1–3 UAS.
  • Former Ukrainian military service or comparable defense-sector experience.
  • Strong understanding of the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense, allied defense organizations, and international partner-force environments.
  • Tactical field experience and knowledge of small-unit tactics.
  • Prior overseas training or operational experience.
  • Experience managing training programs for international customers and working across cultural and language differences.
  • Experience with content-authoring and presentation tools such as PowerPoint, Prezi, http://Beautiful.ai , Camtasia, or comparable platforms. 
  • Experience with learning-management systems and online training-authoring or delivery tools.

lists.content:
Shield AI's Software Development Engineer Intern program spans engineers who design, build, and test the code that powers our autonomous systems — from user-facing applications and embedded flight software to machine learning models and the underlying systems platforms that tie it all together. Over 10–12 weeks, interns work alongside full-time engineers to analyze requirements, write and debug production-quality code, and ship a real feature or capability using our standard Agile development practices.

Example Intern Projects

  • Applications: Build a new feature or internal tool (web, mobile, or desktop) that streamlines a mission-planning or fleet-management workflow.

  • Firmware/Embedded: Develop and debug embedded C/C++ code for a flight controller or sensor module, including bring-up and hardware-in-the-loop testing.

  • Machine Learning: Train, evaluate, and integrate a perception or decision-making model (e.g., object detection, sensor fusion) into an autonomy pipeline.

  • Systems Development: Extend a platform tool, API, or data pipeline that supports autonomy software, simulation, or cloud infrastructure.

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field

  • Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., C, C++, Python, Java, or JavaScript)

  • Solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software design principles

  • Experience writing, testing, and debugging code, whether through coursework, personal projects, or prior internships

  • Familiarity with version control (e.g., Git) and collaborative development workflows

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous requirements into working code

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment

• Exposure to mobile or web application frameworks and full-stack development

  • Hands-on experience with embedded systems, microcontrollers, real-time operating systems, or assembly-level debugging

  • Coursework or projects involving machine learning, statistics, probability theory, or deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow)

  • Experience with cloud platforms, databases, networking, or distributed systems

  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies

  • Prior internship, research, or club/competition experience in robotics, autonomy, or aerospace applications

  • Interest in or exposure to the defense, aerospace, or autonomous systems industry

We are hiring a GTM Finance business partner to support Sales, Business Development, Marketing, and Customer Success. This is a hybrid role across finance, data engineering, and operational strategy — ideal for someone who moves confidently between modeling, systems, and decision-making.

lists.content:
Headcount & Spend Management
  • Build and maintain GTM headcount, spend forecasting, tracking, and capacity model
  • Provide full visibility into GTM Opex, identifying cost drivers and resource optimization opportunities
  • Monitor actuals vs. plan and forecast; drive accountability with cost center owners
  • Partner with Data Engineering and system owners to automate headcount reconciliations across HR, Finance, and GTM systems — including unit economics
    • Data Engineering & Analytics Infrastructure
  • Partner with Data Engineering and BI to define data architecture, KPIs, and source-of-truth models
  • Build automated reporting workflows and capacity models in partnership with Data Engineering or Anaplan teams
  • Write and maintain SQL for ETL workflows across the data lake / Databricks environment
  • Build and manage scalable, reliable data pipelines powering GTM finance reporting
  • Create semantic data models and curated reporting tables for consistent cross-team metrics
  • Build dashboards in Databricks, Power BI, or similar tools for real-time GTM visibility
    • Data Quality, Governance & SOPs
  • Establish and enforce data quality monitoring, validation rules, and anomaly detection
  • Write SOPs for key GTM finance processes: close, headcount reconciliation, budget loading, variance reporting
  • Drive consistent KPI and metric definitions across GTM, Finance, and Data
  • Implement data governance practices to protect reporting integrity
  • Identify data or process gaps and propose scalable solutions
    • Cross-Functional Collaboration & Process Improvement
  • Partner with Revenue Ops, HR, Recruiting, Accounting, and Data to ensure financial plans match operational reality
  • Collaborate with Revenue Operations on quotas, pipeline forecasting, and GTM capacity
  • Continuously streamline tools, reporting, and processes with an automation-first mindset
  • Lead special projects and strategic analyses for finance leadership

• Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, CS, or related field
  • Experience in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, robotics, automotive, or another heavy manufacturing or hardware-driven environment
  • 3–6 years of experience in FP&A, GTM Finance, Sales Finance, RevOps, or equivalent analytical roles
  • Proficiency with AI tools to improve analysis speed, accuracy, and productivity
  • Experience with cloud data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, Redshift, etc.) and ETL/pipeline concepts
  • Demonstrated ability to build headcount models and GTM or corporate OpEx budgets
  • Advanced financial modeling skills in Excel; strong driver-based forecasting experience
  • Excellent communication skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy
  • Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States

• Experience in defense tech, aerospace, or dual-use hardware/software
  • Exposure to U.S. government contracting or milestone-based revenue models
  • Proficiency with AI tools to improve analysis speed, accuracy, and productivity
  • Experience with Anaplan or similar planning tools; ERP/CRM experience (Oracle, NetSuite, Salesforce)
  • Strong SQL skills, including the ability to write, optimize, and troubleshoot queries on large datasets

• Growth mindset — you actively seek feedback, learn quickly, and continuously raise your own bar
  • First principles thinker — you dig into the “why” to design smarter, simpler, more scalable solutions
  • Data and AI first operator — you automate, streamline, and systematize every process you touch

About Shield AI
Shield AI develops AI-powered autonomy software and aircraft systems that protect service members and civilians by enabling intelligent operations in contested environments. As part of the X-BAT program, you will help develop and validate next-generation autonomous aircraft and mission-critical hardware that must perform reliably in demanding operational conditions.

Job Description:
Shield AI is seeking a Lead Mechanical Engineer, Hardware Test to lead the design and development of mechanical test infrastructure that enables rapid, rigorous validation of X-BAT hardware. This role will own the mechanical side of hardware testing, from concept through deployment, by building robust test stands, fixtures, and support equipment for engineering and production-level test activities. 


The ideal candidate is a strong technical leader who can manage a small team, establish sound engineering processes, and drive execution in a fast-paced hardware environment. Success in this role requires hands-on experience with mechanical design, fixture development, analysis, fabrication support, and cross-functional coordination in support of complex aerospace hardware test programs.

lists.content:
• Lead a team of mechanical engineers in designing, building, and maintaining X-BAT hardware test stands and fixtures that support subsystem, integration, and qualification testing.
  • Perform core people-lead responsibilities, including work planning, technical direction, regular 1:1s, coaching, feedback, and performance development for the team.  
  • Own requirements gathering, concept development, detailed design, and validation of multiple test stands used to evaluate X-BAT hardware and supporting subsystems.
  • Design fixtures, tooling, structural support hardware, and mechanical systems for engineering and production-level test applications. 
  • Perform mechanical analyses such as hand calculations and FEA-informed assessments for strength, stiffness, thermal behavior, durability, and safety.
  • Define and apply industry-standard mechanical engineering practices, including GD&T, tolerance analysis, DFM/DFA, design reviews, release documentation, and configuration discipline.
  • Partner with test, electrical, avionics, manufacturing, and technician teams to integrate test hardware that is safe, repeatable, maintainable, and efficient to operate.nyc+1
  • Support fabrication and build activities by working closely with internal shops and external vendors to release, procure, assemble, and iterate hardware quickly.
  • Drive troubleshooting and root-cause investigations when test hardware or units under test do not perform as expected and implement corrective design improvements.
  • Build team processes, documentation habits, and execution rhythms that improve quality, speed, and ownership across the hardware test function.

• B.S. in Mechanical Engineering or a related STEM discipline; advanced degree is a plus.  
  • Proven experience as a senior or lead mechanical engineer developing fixtures, tooling, or test stands for aerospace, defense, robotics, or other complex hardware systems.sf+1
  • Prior experience leading engineers and building high-performing teams, including mentoring, setting expectations, and driving accountability.  
  • Strong mechanical design fundamentals with the ability to take concepts through analysis, detailed design, fabrication, assembly, and checkout.
  • Proficiency with industry-standard CAD tools such as NX, SolidWorks, or CATIA, and experience releasing drawings for manufacture.
  • Familiarity with standard ME practices, including tolerance stack-up, materials selection, fastener design, load path evaluation, and safe machine/fixture design.
  • Hands-on experience in lab, prototype, or production environments, with the judgment to balance analytical rigor and practical execution.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work across disciplines to translate ambiguous test needs into robust mechanical solutions.  
  • Demonstrated ownership, strong work ethic, and a track record of improving processes, raising the bar, and delivering results under schedule pressure.

• Experience with propulsion or engine-related test equipment, high-load structural fixtures, or mechanically complex aerospace ground test systems.
  • Familiarity with environmental or qualification testing and the facility interfaces those systems require, such as mounting, cooling, plumbing, or instrumentation accommodations.
  • Experience using analysis tools such as ANSYS, Abaqus, or Nastran to support test hardware design decisions.
  • Comfort working directly with technicians, machine shops, and test operators to refine designs and improve ease of use in the lab.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving development program where priorities evolve and rapid iteration is expected.

The ideal candidate has strong experience in financial analysis, program finance, or FP&A; thrives in a fast-paced and evolving environment; and can translate complex financial data into clear, actionable insights. This individual will improve visibility into financial performance, strengthen forecasting discipline, support EAC and risk/opportunity processes, and help cross-functional teams make informed business decisions.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. The Lead Financial Analyst will be expected to build and maintain financial models, analyze performance against plan, improve reporting and financial cadences, and develop scalable processes that support Shield AI’s continued growth.

lists.content:
• Build, maintain, and scale financial models used for forecasting, budgeting, and long-term planning
  • Analyze data trends to develop business insights and deliver actionable recommendations to leadership
  • Partner closely with Program Management and Aircraft Ops teams to provide financial support on program health, spend trends, and headcount planning
  • Develop reporting cadences and dashboards to track KPIs and business performance using tools like Power BI and Excel
  • Participate in the month-end and quarter-end close process, including variance analysis and executive reporting
  • Assist with financial operational planning cycles, business reviews, and investment decision-making processes
  • Support data transformation initiatives and basic modeling efforts in collaboration with analytics or data engineering teams
  • Drive continuous process improvement by identifying automation and efficiency opportunities within financial reporting and analysis
  • Partner with inventory and supply chain teams to monitor material movement, usage, and cost trends
  • Collaborate with program managers to monitor actuals vs. plan, flag risks/opportunities, and support EAC (Estimate at Completion) updates
  • Ensure financial alignment of day-to-day operations with long-term strategic goals through regular operational reviews and ad hoc analysis

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in financial analysis, corporate finance, or FP&A
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel, financial modeling, and data analysis
  • Strong understanding of US GAAP, with practical experience applying accounting principles in a government contracting or manufacturing environment
  • Familiarity with cost accounting concepts and government contract structures (e.g., T&M, CPFF, FFP)
  • Strong working knowledge of Power BI and comfort with data visualization tools
  • Solid understanding of financial statements and business metrics
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaborate cross-functionally in a fast-moving environment
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to present complex financial data to non-financial stakeholders

• MBA or Master’s degree in a related discipline
  • Experience supporting operations or customer-facing teams in a manufacturing, aerospace, or tech environment
  • Exposure to Microsoft Fabric, Power Query, DAX, or other data transformation and modeling tools
  • Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g., Costpoint/Oracle) and planning tools (e.g., Vena/Anaplan)
  • Track record of being a high performer with a bias for action, intellectual curiosity, and attention to detail
  • Passion for using data to tell a story and drive strategic decisions

descriptionPlain:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


The primary function of this Proposal Specialist role is supporting US federal and international government and commercial Proposals and other related BD Ops deliverables (e.g., ROM pricing estimates, RFI responses, and white papers) for Shield AI’s Asia/Middel East (ASME) Go To Market (GTM) team. The Business Development Operations (BD Ops) team is looking for a candidate who thrives in a dynamic environment and is eager to join a rapidly scaling, nontraditional defense contractor. This ideal candidate will have strong oral and written communication skills (technical writing experience preferred), attention to detail, curiosity, and a proven ability to coordinate and work as a member of cross-functional teams.  
What we are looking for:  
Leadership skills: Lead ASME proposal efforts, align stakeholders, and communicate key customer, market, and BD strategy insights. 
Strong communicator: Strong oral and written communication skills. (Technical writing experience preferred.) Strong presentation skills. Ability to communicate seamlessly at all levels of Shield AI and customer organizations  
Attention to detail in a fast-paced environment: Be rigorous and go fast is one of Shield AI’s leadership traits and, possibly, the most relevant one for BD Ops. Our ideal candidate must always work with efficiency and a keen attention to detail. Both are critical to supporting on time, compliant Bids/Proposals and related deliverables.  
Organization and time management: Strong organizational and time management skills enabling the tracking and execution of multiple workstreams with stakeholders across Shield AI. 
Extreme ownership: BD Ops serves as the primary cross-functional lead for Bids/Proposals across product lines and geographic regions. We manage the proposal lifecycle from start to finish including kickoff, collaboration with stakeholders, color reviews, and management reviews with senior leaders/executives. We are ultimately responsible for everything that does or does not happen in the Bid/Proposal process. 
Team-first mentality: The ideal candidate will demonstrate the ability to be flexible, work hard, hold themself and others to high standards, embrace teammates, and act with kindness.

Job Description:
Help build the technology behind the next generation of autonomous aircraft. As a Lead, Electrical Engineer, you will serve as a player-coach: leading the architecture, design, integration, and delivery of advanced electrical systems while directly managing and developing a small team of electrical engineers.You will remain deeply hands-on technically while setting direction for your team, driving execution across disciplines, and building the leadership experience needed to grow into broader engineering management responsibilities, including eventually leading full avionics organizations.

Job Description:

Help build the technology behind the next generation of autonomous aircraft. As a Lead, Electrical Engineer, you will serve as a player-coach: leading the architecture, design, integration, and delivery of advanced electrical systems while directly managing and developing a small team of electrical engineers.You will remain deeply hands-on technically while setting direction for your team, driving execution across disciplines, and building the leadership experience needed to grow into broader engineering management responsibilities, including eventually leading full avionics organizations.

Growth Opportunity

This role is intended for an experienced technical leader who wants to expand their impact through both hands-on engineering leadership and people management. Successful performance can lead to broader responsibility for multiple teams, larger avionics portfolio.

lists.content:
• Lead the architecture, design, integration, and production release of electrical systems and subsystems for autonomous aircraft and support equipment.
  • Own technical decisions across complex architectures involving FPGAs, power management, analog and digital circuitry, servos, microcontrollers, sensors, radios, and embedded systems.
  • Remain hands-on with part selection, schematic capture, simulation, analysis, verification, debugging, design reviews, and production support.
  • Lead and develop a team of electrical engineers through technical mentorship, coaching, performance feedback, and effective delegation.
  • Establish technical direction, priorities, and development plans for your team in alignment with program and aircraft objectives.
  • Partner closely with firmware, software, mechanical, manufacturing, supply chain, test, and systems engineering teams to deliver integrated products.
  • Support the design and integration of embedded systems and sensors that enable aircraft autonomy and AI capabilities.
  • Define technical requirements, product features, interfaces, and verification strategies.
  • Own project execution for your team, including schedules, risks, dependencies, deliverables, and cross-functional communication.
  • Lead and participate in architecture, design, integration, and production readiness reviews.
  • Help develop automated test solutions and improve hardware development, verification, and production processes.
  • Identify and implement improvements that increase engineering efficiency, product quality, aircraft reliability, and team effectiveness.
  • Build the technical and organizational foundation required to scale the avionics engineering team over time.

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of industry experience in electrical engineering, including multiple product development cycles.
  • Experience leading technically complex electrical or avionics designs from concept through production.
  • Strong fundamentals in circuit design, embedded systems, hardware architecture, analysis, verification, and debugging.
  • Experience delivering products across EE, ME, firmware, software, manufacturing, and systems engineering disciplines.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, and develop engineers while maintaining hands-on technical ownership.
  • Proven track record of shipping high-quality products, navigating ambiguity, resolving obstacles, and delivering against challenging schedules.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, prioritization, and cross-functional leadership skills.
  • Demonstrated ownership, initiative, sound technical judgment, and commitment to engineering excellence.
  • Ability to obtain a Secret/SAR-level security clearance desired.

Job Description:
The Autonomous Pilot Integration team for launched effects builds autonomy solutions for small, often air- or ground-launched platforms that operate in multi-agent fleets and frequently in disconnected or air-gapped environments. We combine capabilities from the Autonomy Capabilities team (motion planning, tactics), the Perception team (e.g., track fusion), and the HivemindSDK to develop the autonomy software that runs on launched effects platforms, then integrate, validate, and field it on the real hardware — for U.S. and international defense customers. Our engineers write new autonomy code — such as mission behaviors, platform-specific control, multi-agent coordination, contingencies, and executive autonomy — and own it end-to-end from software-in-the-loop, to hardware-in-the-loop, to vehicle-in-the-loop, to live test exercise.
In this role, you'll lead a team of autonomy engineers working on launched effects programs — owning their delivery, their growth, and the technical health of your area. A core part of the job is growing the team: hiring strong engineers, mentoring them through hard technical work, and shaping their career development. You'll stay technically active — close enough to the code and the integration work to make sound technical decisions, to be credible to your team, and to lead them through the design, development, and delivery of a major capability or program. You'll partner closely with the Autonomy Capabilities and Perception teams, feature crews, autopilot vendors (e.g., PX4, ArduPilot), C2 providers, and customer/contractor partners that staff and operate alongside our team. This portfolio runs at a fast cadence — frequent Capability Release milestones, multi-agent fleet operations, air-gapped deployments at scale, and demanding live exercises — and you'll set the pace for your team accordingly.
Shield AI is committed to developing cutting-edge autonomy for unmanned platforms across every operating domain — air, maritime, space, and effects/expendables — in service of the U.S. Department of Defense and our international defense customers. Our Autonomous Pilot Integration engineers bridge the gap between R&D and deployment, ensuring autonomous systems function reliably and effectively wherever and whenever they're needed most.

lists.content:
• Lead the Team — Manage a small-to-mid-sized engineering team (typically 3–8 engineers); own performance, growth, leveling, and delivery; run 1:1s, performance reviews, and team rituals.
  • Grow the Team via Hiring — Drive hiring for your area: identify the skills you need, partner with recruiting, run interviews, set the bar, and personally close strong candidates.
  • Grow Engineers Technically — Mentor engineers through hard problems; create stretch opportunities; give direct, actionable technical feedback; help engineers level up in both skill and impact.
  • Develop & Field Autonomy — Develop & integrate autonomy software solutions onto launched effects platforms, including payload computer bring-up, autopilot integration (e.g., PX4, ArduPilot), multi-agent coordination, and fleet-scale deployment to disconnected or air-gapped environments — and lead a small team through the design, development, and delivery of a major capability or program.
  • Technical Leadership — Lead a small feature crew or sub-program; set technical direction, break down work, unblock the team, and report progress to leadership and stakeholders.
  • Collaboration Across Teams & Partners — Act as a primary technical interface with the Autonomy Capabilities team (motion planning, tactics), the Perception team, feature crews, autopilot vendors (e.g., PX4, ArduPilot), C2 providers, and customer/contractor partners (including embedded contractor engineers and U.S. or international government program offices); author and negotiate ICDs and interface contracts rather than just consume them.
  • Design & Documentation — Drive design reviews, ICDs, and post-mortems for your area; push the team toward higher rigor and close process gaps that span teams.
  • Pre-deployment Preparation — Own the build, configuration, and validation process for mission-ready systems and fleet-scale deployments (often 50–150+ units in disconnected environments); coordinate hardware/software compatibility, mission readiness, and Capability Release (CR) cadence with capability and feature teams.
  • On-site Test & Mission Support — Travel to test sites and customer exercises to support live mission operations (flight tests, range exercises, multi-agent live events, customer demonstrations), including safety checks, system bring-up, and troubleshooting under time-critical constraints.
  • Hardware/Software Debugging — Diagnose and resolve integration issues across complex autonomy stacks, payload computers, and embedded systems in lab and field environments — including memory, CPU, and timing profiling under operationally-representative loads.
  • Mission Data & Debrief Support — Capture mission and test data, reproduce issues in simulation, and partner with autonomy capability owners to drive fixes back into the next build.
  • Continuous Improvement — Build tools and processes to improve integration timelines, test/mission reliability, and team efficiency across deployment cycles.
  • C2 Interoperability & Standards — Own the interface contracts with C2 providers and drive compliance against common message and open-systems standards (e.g., UCI, OMS, MOSA, WOSA, TAK/CoT).
  • Travel Requirement – Members of this team typically travel around 20-30% of the year (to different office locations, customer sites, range exercises, and integration events).

• BS/MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, and/or similar degree, or equivalent practical experience
  • Typically requires a minimum of 7 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 5 years and a Master's degree; or 4 years with a PhD; or equivalent work experience.
  • 2+ years of direct people-management experience (running 1:1s, performance reviews, hiring decisions, growth planning).
  • Demonstrated experience building or growing an engineering team — including interviewing, hiring, and onboarding new engineers.
  • Track record of mentoring engineers and growing their technical skill and career trajectory.
  • Demonstrated experience leading a small technical team or owning a major capability from design through field delivery.
  • Experience authoring or negotiating interface contracts / ICDs with internal or external stakeholders.
  • Direct experience with launched effects, loitering munitions, expendable autonomous systems, or comparable small unmanned platforms.
  • Experience with multi-agent, swarm, or fleet-scale autonomy.
  • Strong proficiency in C++, with experience developing or integrating real-time or latency-sensitive systems.
  • Proficiency in Linux-based development and experience working with embedded systems, shell scripting, and system diagnostics.
  • Familiarity with middleware, pub-sub, or IPC frameworks used in autonomy or robotics systems (e.g., DDS, message buses).
  • Hands-on experience supporting live exercises, customer demonstrations, or operational test events for launched effects or similar small unmanned systems.
  • Experience with autonomy simulation environments for testing and validation.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot and optimize system performance across the full stack.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work effectively in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment.
  • Ability to obtain a SECRET clearance.

• Direct experience with PX4 and/or ArduPilot at the platform integration level.
  • Experience using and developing on QGroundControl (QGC) or other Qt-based ground control stations.
  • Proficiency in Python for scripting, automation, and analysis.
  • Experience leading a feature crew, sub-program, or small team in an unmanned systems context.
  • Experience growing engineers from mid-level into senior IC, or supporting promotion decisions through a leveling framework.
  • Experience with air-gapped, disconnected, or otherwise constrained deployment of autonomous systems at fleet scale.
  • Familiarity with tactical edge C2 (e.g., TAK, CoT) and ground operator workflows.
  • Experience working with embedded contractor engineers, FFRDC partners, or customer-funded staff augmentation models.
  • Experience supporting international defense customer programs (FMS or direct commercial sales).
  • Experience owning customer- or partner-facing technical relationships (e.g., autopilot vendors, C2 providers, government program offices).
  • Track record of cross-team improvements (process, rigor, documentation, or developer experience).
  • Familiarity with autonomy stacks, motion planning, or vehicle-control integration.
  • Competence in avionics bring-up, payload computer integration, or hardware-in-the-loop debugging.
  • Experience with container orchestration (e.g., k3s, k3d, Docker) on embedded or payload compute.
  • Proficiency in developing automation tools for system testing, logging, and data parsing.
  • Build-system experience (e.g., Conan, CMake) and CI/CD pipeline familiarity.
  • Comfortable interfacing with DoD stakeholders during field events or technical reviews.
  • Experience with common message and open-systems standards such as UCI, OMS, MOSA, or WOSA.

descriptionPlain:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


The Autonomy Capabilities team develops the core functionality used to drive autonomous decision making for single- and multi-agent teams of platforms in pursuit of mission objectives. The team serves as a central technical discipline within Shield AI, driving consistent approaches across business portfolios while operating at every level of the command-and-control hierarchy, from advanced control laws and motion planning to tactical behaviors and multi-agent coordination. Our work spans a wide range of mission sets, platform types, and operational domains, including air, sea, and space. 
The team combines strong technical fundamentals, including vehicle kinematics and dynamics, trajectory design, optimization, information fusion, and efficient algorithms, with the software engineering and integration rigor required to field these capabilities on real-world systems. We build autonomy that operates reliably within complex integration environments and delivers differentiated mission capabilities to U.S. and international defense customers. 
Your team will build autonomy solutions for small, often air- or ground-launched platforms that operate individually or as part of collaborative multi-agent fleets, frequently in disconnected or air-gapped environments. The capabilities your team develops will span motion planning, tactical behaviors, track fusion, weapons-target assignment, and perception-aware decision-making. 
You will own the team’s technical delivery, organizational health, and growth. A core part of the role is building and developing the team by hiring strong engineers, mentoring them through complex technical challenges, and creating opportunities for continued growth. You will remain technically engaged, helping define system architecture, guiding key design decisions, contributing directly where it best serves the team, and ensuring solutions are delivered from rapid prototyping through software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and live test exercises. Success in this role requires a leader who can balance technical depth with people leadership, navigate ambiguity across multiple programs, and translate evolving customer needs into autonomy capabilities that can be integrated, validated, and fielded.
