Job Description:

The Reliability and Maintainability Engineer is a senior-level individual contributor responsible for driving investigation, root cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement for V-BAT field failures, repeat defects, and complex technical issues requiring deeper engineering analysis.This role owns the technical investigation path for fielded V-BAT issues by using logs, returned hardware, test data, maintenance records, operational context, configuration data, and fleet trends to determine failure modes, root causes, contributing factors, and corrective actions. The Reliability and Maintainability Engineer partners closely with Fleet Support Engineering, Product Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Reliability Data Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations to ensure field failures are understood, contained, corrected, and prevented from recurring.This role is accountable for translating field issues into structured technical investigations, verified corrective actions, reliability improvements, maintainability improvements, and clear product health insights that improve fleet readiness, customer support, and long-term system performance.

lists.content:
• Lead engineering investigations for V-BAT field failures, repeat defects, reliability issues, maintainability issues, and complex technical escalations.
  • Drive Root Cause and Corrective Action investigations for fielded V-BAT issues, including containment, root cause identification, corrective action planning, verification, and closure.
  • Reproduce and analyze field issues using logs, returned hardware, test data, maintenance records, operational context, configuration data, environmental conditions, and customer-reported symptoms.
  • Partner with Fleet Support Engineers, Product Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Reliability Data Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations to investigate and resolve fielded system issues.
  • Determine whether issues are caused by design, manufacturing, supplier quality, configuration, software, operator use, environmental exposure, maintenance practices, documentation gaps, or system integration effects.
  • Lead and support returned material analysis, teardown reviews, bench testing, inspection planning, fault isolation, and failure replication activities.
  • Document failure modes, root cause, contributing factors, containment actions, corrective actions, verification plans, and recurrence-prevention measures.
  • Drive corrective actions through closure by ensuring actions have owners, due dates, verification methods, and measurable field-improvement outcomes.
  • Identify reliability and maintainability trends from field failures, repeat defects, maintenance data, test results, and product health indicators.
  • Recommend new tests, inspections, diagnostics, design changes, process changes, maintenance updates, or supplier quality actions to prevent recurrence.
  • Provide technical input to product health reviews, reliability readouts, sustainment reviews, fleet readiness assessments, and leadership updates.
  • Support development and improvement of R&M processes, including field failure review, FRACAS, RCCA, reliability growth tracking, maintainability feedback loops, and corrective action management.
  • Work with Product Engineering to ensure field-failure findings are translated into design improvements, retrofit plans, software updates, service actions, or configuration changes where appropriate.
  • Work with Quality and Manufacturing to determine whether failures are linked to process escapes, inspection gaps, workmanship issues, supplier defects, or production variation.
  • Work with Fleet Support and Operations to understand operational impact, maintenance burden, customer effects, and urgency of fielded system issues.
  • Provide clear technical recommendations on containment, inspection, repair, replacement, retrofit, service guidance, or fleet-level mitigation.
  • Communicate investigation findings, risks, corrective actions, and verification status clearly to technical teams, sustainment leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Support X-BAT lessons learned where V-BAT reliability, maintainability, and field-failure experience can inform future design, sustainment, diagnostics, repairability, and lifecycle planning.

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Reliability Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 4+ years of experience in reliability engineering, maintainability engineering, failure analysis, systems engineering, quality engineering, aviation sustainment, product support, manufacturing engineering, or complex hardware sustainment.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting technical investigations for field failures, repeat defects, hardware issues, system-level issues, or complex product performance problems.
  • Experience driving Root Cause and Corrective Action investigations from initial problem statement through containment, root cause, corrective action, verification, and closure.
  • Strong ability to analyze hardware, software behavior, logs, test data, returned material, field reports, configuration history, maintenance records, and operational context.
  • Familiarity with structured problem-solving and failure-analysis methods such as 5 Whys, fault tree analysis, fishbone diagrams, 8D, FMEA/FMECA, FRACAS, fault isolation, or similar methods.
  • Ability to distinguish between design, manufacturing, supplier quality, configuration, software, operator, environmental, maintenance, and documentation-related contributors.
  • Experience working across Product Engineering, Fleet Support, Quality, Manufacturing, Reliability Data Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations to resolve technical issues.
  • Strong technical judgment and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate ambiguous field reports, identify likely failure modes, and define practical next steps.
  • Ability to convert technical findings into clear corrective actions, verification plans, risk assessments, and product or process improvement recommendations.

We are seeking a new-graduate RF Hardware Test Engineer to help verify RF modules, assemblies, and interfaces used in airborne and ground systems. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will build practical expertise in RF measurements, instrument automation, data analysis, troubleshooting, and qualification support. This role is centered on disciplined test execution and objective evidence rather than top-level RF system architecture.

This is an Engineer I (L1) position intended for candidates completing an undergraduate or graduate degree or beginning their professional career. Coursework, research, internships, student teams, and personal projects are all relevant ways to demonstrate readiness.

lists.content:
• Execute documented RF test plans and procedures with mentorship, record test configurations, and produce clear, traceable results.
  • Characterize RF modules and assemblies for S-parameters, gain and loss, output power, compression, harmonics and spurious emissions, isolation, rejection, noise figure, and receiver sensitivity as applicable.
  • Set up and operate vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, power meters, oscilloscopes, noise-figure equipment, programmable power supplies, and related laboratory instruments.
  • Calibrate measurement setups and characterize cables, adapters, attenuators, fixtures, and other sources of measurement error.
  • Develop simple test fixtures, harnesses, interface adapters, and monitoring circuits; perform basic soldering and hardware rework when appropriate.
  • Automate instrument control, data collection, analysis, and plotting using Python, MATLAB, or comparable tools.
  • Compare measured performance with requirements, identify unexpected behavior, and summarize conclusions in engineering reports and reviews.
  • Troubleshoot test anomalies with senior engineers and learn to distinguish device behavior from setup, calibration, software, or environmental artifacts.
  • Support EMI/EMC pre-compliance and MIL-STD-461 qualification testing, environmental testing, hardware integration, and ground or flight test activities as needed.
  • Maintain safe, organized laboratory practices and follow equipment calibration, configuration-control, and data-management processes.
  • Collaborate with RF, electrical, mechanical, systems, software, manufacturing, and supplier teams.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

• Bachelor's or master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical field, completed or expected within 12 months of the anticipated start date.
  • Coursework, research, project, or internship experience in RF or microwave engineering, communications, electromagnetics, analog circuits, or electronic hardware testing.
  • Fundamental understanding of S-parameters, impedance, transmission lines, gain and loss, noise, power, spectral content, and frequency response.
  • Hands-on laboratory experience gained through coursework, research, an internship, a student organization, or a personal project.
  • Basic programming and data-analysis skills in Python, MATLAB, or a similar environment.
  • Ability to follow test procedures, document setups and results accurately, recognize uncertainty, and ask for guidance when needed.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work constructively in a multidisciplinary team.
  • Ability to work on-site in a laboratory and hardware-development environment.

• Experience using a vector network analyzer, spectrum analyzer, signal generator, power meter, oscilloscope, noise-figure analyzer, or programmable test equipment.
  • Experience automating laboratory instruments or analyzing measurement data using Python, MATLAB, SCPI, or a comparable approach.
  • Familiarity with RF simulation or design tools such as ADS, AWR, HFSS, or CST.
  • Experience with PCB bring-up, soldering, RF connectors and cables, test fixtures, harnesses, or basic hardware rework.
  • Exposure to EMI/EMC testing or MIL-STD-461 through coursework, research, an internship, or laboratory work.
  • Exposure to environmental, qualification, reliability, or acceptance testing of electronic hardware.
  • Experience on a university design team, research laboratory, internship, co-op, or project involving aerospace, defense, robotics, communications, or other high-reliability hardware.
  • Ability to obtain an S//SAR level security clearance, if required by the program.

Job Description:

Shield AI develops intelligent autonomous systems that protect service members and civilians. The X-BAT Engineering team is building a next-generation autonomous aircraft for demanding and contested environments.

We are seeking an RF and Microwave Hardware Design Engineer to design and deliver compact, high-performance RF modules for airborne and ground systems. You will design and mature active and passive RF circuits, PCB assemblies, packaging interfaces, laboratory verification, and transition to production. The center of gravity of this position is hands-on module design rather than top-level communications architecture, waveform development, or link-budget ownership.

This position may be filled at the Engineer II (L2) or Senior Engineer (L3) level. The selected level will reflect the candidate's demonstrated technical depth, independence, scope, and impact.

lists.content:
• Design RF and microwave modules from requirements and architecture through schematic capture, component selection, layout, bring-up, verification, qualification, and production release, with scope and independence appropriate to level.
  • Design active and passive RF circuits such as low-noise amplifiers, power amplifiers, filters and multiplexers, RF switches, limiters, couplers, attenuators, power detectors, and frequency-conversion stages.
  • Develop RF front-end assemblies that meet gain, noise figure, output power, linearity, compression, efficiency, harmonic and spurious-emission, stability, isolation, and out-of-band rejection requirements.
  • Perform circuit and electromagnetic analysis using tools such as Keysight ADS, Cadence AWR, HFSS, or CST, and correlate models with measured hardware performance.
  • Create and review RF and mixed-signal PCB designs, including controlled-impedance routing, grounding, shielding, stack-up definition, power distribution, and placement of sensitive or high-power components.
  • Plan and execute laboratory characterization using network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, noise-figure analyzers, power meters, oscilloscopes, and automated test equipment.
  • Diagnose difficult hardware issues involving instability, oscillation, intermodulation, self-interference, desense, thermal drift, mismatch, leakage, and electromagnetic coupling.
  • Work closely with mechanical, thermal, avionics, communications, antenna, manufacturing, and test engineers to integrate RF hardware into size-, weight-, power-, cooling-, and environmental constraints.
  • Develop verification methods, production test strategies, calibration approaches, and clear technical documentation that make designs repeatable and manufacturable.
  • Support environmental and electromagnetic qualification, supplier engagements, hardware integration, ground test, and flight test as needed.
  • Contribute to design reviews, share technical knowledge, and support the growth of interns and less-experienced engineers at a level appropriate to the position.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Typically 1 or more years of relevant post-undergraduate experience for L2, or 2 or more years for L3. Applicable graduate study and research may count toward experience. Demonstrated capability and scope are more important than years alone.
  • Hands-on experience designing, building, or debugging an RF or microwave circuit, module, or PCB assembly through measured verification.
  • Solid understanding of S-parameters, impedance matching, transmission lines, stability, gain and noise figure, linearity and compression, nonlinear products, isolation, and cascaded RF performance.
  • Experience creating or reviewing RF PCB layouts with controlled impedance, grounding, shielding, component placement, and signal-integrity considerations.
  • Proficiency with common RF laboratory instruments and calibration methods, with the ability to distinguish hardware behavior from measurement artifacts.
  • Ability to use simulation and measured data to make sound design decisions, document tradeoffs, and close requirements with objective evidence.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with cross-functional engineering and manufacturing teams.
  • Ability to work on-site in a laboratory and hardware-development environment.

• Experience with RF front ends for airborne, defense, space, robotics, or other high-reliability systems.
  • Experience integrating GaN or GaAs power amplifiers, MMICs, LNAs, switches, limiters, frequency converters, or high-selectivity filter technologies.
  • Experience designing for simultaneous transmit and receive operation, high-power RF, intermodulation control, adjacent-band rejection, or co-site interference and desense.
  • Experience with Altium Designer and one or more RF or electromagnetic simulation environments such as ADS, AWR, HFSS, or CST.
  • Working knowledge of thermal design, RF packaging, connector and cable interfaces, tolerance analysis, and design for manufacturability and test.
  • Experience with EMI and EMC design and qualification for military or aerospace hardware.
  • Experience developing automated characterization or data-analysis tools in Python, MATLAB, or a similar environment.
  • Experience transitioning RF hardware from prototype through qualification and low-rate production.
  • Ability to obtain an S//SAR level security clearance, if required by the program.

We are seeking a Senior Accountant to play a critical role in scaling our accounting function as the business grows. This role goes beyond the close, you will influence how financial data is produced, trusted, and used by leadership to make decisions. You’ll own meaningful areas of the balance sheet and P&L, improve how we operate, and help build a best-in-class accounting function.

What you'll do:
* Own close for assigned areas: prepare journals, account reconciliations, and flux analysis; ensure GL-to-subledger integrity.

* Uplift controls and audit readiness: Identify risks, control gaps, or inefficiencies and drive solutions with minimal direction. 
* Improve processes and tools: standardize templates, automate reconciliations, streamline the close calendar.

Required qualifications:
* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field. 
* CPA or CPA eligible. 
* 4+ years of progressive accounting experience in public accounting (Big 4 or national firm) and/or a high-growth operating environment. Public company experience a plus
* Proficiency with GLs/subledgers and reconciliation tools (e.g., FloQast) and strong Excel/Sheets skills 
* Solid working knowledge of US GAAP and internal controls 
* Clear communicator with an ownership mindset and the ability to collaborate to deadlines. 
* Strong attention to detail and problem-solving mindset.

Job Description:
The Senior Analyst, U.S. Market Intelligence & Price-to-Win develops and sustains Shield AI's integrated understanding of U.S. defense funding, competition, and pricing for the X-BAT Family of Systems. The role turns primary-source budget data, competitor intelligence, program history, and market evidence into decision-ready inputs for strategy, capture, pricing, and go-to-market leaders. 
This is a cumulative knowledge role, not a series of one-off studies. The analyst maintains an authoritative U.S. budget, competitive, and PTW knowledge base and keeps it current across the full budget and acquisition cycle, from President's Budget release through congressional marks, enactment, execution, competitions, and awards. 
U.S. X-BAT FoS GTM leads own their customers, captures, and final pricing posture. This role owns the analytic layer beneath those decisions: the integrated view of available funding, competitors, likely bid strategies, and defensible Price-to-Win positions. It is a pre-award enablement role and is not the primary customer or congressional interface.

Job Description:

The Senior Analyst, U.S. Market Intelligence & Price-to-Win develops and sustains Shield AI's integrated understanding of U.S. defense funding, competition, and pricing for the X-BAT Family of Systems. The role turns primary-source budget data, competitor intelligence, program history, and market evidence into decision-ready inputs for strategy, capture, pricing, and go-to-market leaders. 

This is a cumulative knowledge role, not a series of one-off studies. The analyst maintains an authoritative U.S. budget, competitive, and PTW knowledge base and keeps it current across the full budget and acquisition cycle, from President's Budget release through congressional marks, enactment, execution, competitions, and awards. 

U.S. X-BAT FoS GTM leads own their customers, captures, and final pricing posture. This role owns the analytic layer beneath those decisions: the integrated view of available funding, competitors, likely bid strategies, and defensible Price-to-Win positions. It is a pre-award enablement role and is not the primary customer or congressional interface.

lists.content:
• Own the integrated U.S. market picture. Maintain one product-line-aligned view of DoW funding, competitors, programs, acquisitions, awards, and pricing signals relevant to the X-BAT Family of Systems. 
  • Lead U.S. budget intelligence. Track requested, marked, appropriated, and executed resources across the PPBE and congressional cycle, including budget releases, marks, enactment, execution, reprogrammings, and budget line item adjustments. 
  • Work from primary budget sources. Extract and interpret data from J-books, P-1/R-1/O-1 exhibits, committee reports and marks, appropriations acts, reprogramming actions, and OMB and Treasury reporting. 
  • Lead competitive intelligence. Develop and maintain competitor profiles, product-line baselines, differentiation analyses, competitor courses of action, teaming maps, and market assessments for the U.S. defense market. 
  • Lead Price-to-Win analysis. Build and defend PTW positions for priority pursuits, including competitor cost structures, likely bid strategies, most-probable price ranges, and pricing sensitivities, and translate them into recommendations on scope, teaming, and pricing posture. 
  • Deliver integrated assessments. Combine budget, competitive, program, and company financial data into coherent judgments for pursuit shaping, capture reviews, proposal color teams, gate reviews, and executive decisions. 
  • Curate the knowledge base. Design and maintain a cumulative, structured, queryable repository of U.S. budget, competitive, market, and PTW content using AI-enabled tools for ingestion, organization, and upkeep. 
  • Publish on cadence and on demand. Deliver recurring cycle-event and market updates, while responding to fast-turn requests for funding, competitive, and PTW analysis. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

This role is accountable for the integrated U.S. budget and competitive picture for the X-BAT Family of Systems; PTW positions and pricing recommendations on assigned U.S. pursuits; recurring intelligence products; the curated knowledge base; and rapid-turn analysis supporting pursuit and executive decisions. 

U.S. GTM leads are accountable for customer relationships and engagement strategy, win strategy, proposal content, the bid/no-bid recommendation, and final pricing posture for their pursuits. 

Government Relations is accountable for the comprehensive DoW budget picture and engagement with congressional staff, OSD, and the Services; this role provides product-line analysis and does not lead those engagements. 

Finance and Contracts are accountable for internal pricing policy, cost buildup, financial planning, and contracting terms; this role provides the external funding, competitive, and pricing baseline that informs those decisions. 

The International Market Intelligence Analyst is accountable for maintaining allied and partner-nation budget and competitive data; this role coordinates methods and integrates relevant context when required. 

Engineering and Product are accountable for technical solution definition and performance commitments that shape the competitive comparison. 

External customer and congressional engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead or Government Relations owner.

• 6–10 years of experience spanning competitive intelligence, defense budget analysis, capture strategy, market assessment, Price-to-Win, or closely related work in defense or aerospace. 
  •  Demonstrated prior experience conducting Price-to-Win analysis on active captures, including competitor cost modeling, bid strategy analysis, and most-probable-price recommendations used by capture and pricing leadership. 
  •  Deep working familiarity with the U.S. defense budget process, including PPBE and the congressional authorization and appropriations cycle, and experience analyzing primary budget documents. 
  •  Demonstrated experience in competitive intelligence, market assessment, and product differentiation analysis in aerospace, unmanned, or autonomous systems. 
  •  Familiarity with parametric cost estimating, should-cost analysis, or related cost-analytic methods. 
  •  Strong data-handling, analytic writing, and briefing skills, with the ability to turn incomplete evidence into defensible recommendations for senior audiences. 
  •  Demonstrated experience using AI tools to build and sustain structured, reusable knowledge resources. 
  •  Bachelor's degree in economics, finance, public policy, political science, business, engineering, security studies, or a related field. 
  •  Demonstrated alignment with Shield AI core values: Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, Pursue Excellence. 
  •  Ability to travel domestically as required and to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

• Prior PTW experience across multiple pursuit types, including production, sustainment, and services, in the U.S. Government context. 
  • Experience in congressional appropriations, DoW/OSD resource management, service headquarters programming, or defense-industry budget analysis. 
  • Familiarity with Home | SAM.gov , USAspending, FPDS, and other programmatic data sources that complement budget and competitive analysis. 
  • Experience supporting business development, capture, strategy, or executive decision-making in the defense industry. 
  • Advanced degree in a relevant field; PMP or comparable certification.

• U.S. GTM, capture, and pricing leaders work from one current, defensible picture of funding, competition, and likely pricing for the X-BAT Family of Systems. 
  • Budget-cycle events and competitive developments are anticipated and covered on cadence, with implications delivered early enough to shape pursuit, solution, teaming, and pricing decisions. 
  • Capture and pricing leadership use the role's PTW positions as a reference point and can trace recommendations to defensible evidence. 
  • The integrated knowledge base grows in coverage and quality quarter over quarter, and rapid-turn questions take less time to answer. 
  • Budget, competitive, and PTW judgments are consistent across U.S. pursuits, and discrepancies are visible and reconciled.

Job Description:
Our Applications Engineers are highly technical, customer-facing problem solvers who play a critical role in deploying Shield AI’s Hivemind software in real-world environments. This role focuses on maritime autonomy, helping customers integrate and deploy Hivemind on maritime platforms. It involves frequent travel, including international and multi-week engagements, to work directly alongside customers on-site.

lists.content:

  • You’re passionate about autonomy, robotics, and applying these technologies to maritime operations.

• You prefer minimal travel or want to work primarily from a single location.
  • You want to do 100% R&D and don’t enjoy customer interactions.
  • You’ve never programmed in C, C++, or Rust.

• Deploy with customers on-site globally (up to 50% travel) to support software integration, development, and on-water testing.
  • Become an expert user of the Hivemind enterprise software stack and its various autonomy modules.

  • Develop AI and autonomy applications using the Shield AI enterprise software development kit, with a focus on maritime missions and platforms.
  • Assist the sales team in pre-sales activities, including demonstrations, conferences, and immersions.
  • Assist in post-sales deployment and integration of Shield AI enterprise software products with maritime platform controls, sensors, navigation systems, and communications.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation and training materials.
  • Help customers debug software and API integration issues.
  • Collaborate with the product engineering team to address customer feedback and improve products.

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of industry experience.
  • 2+ years of experience in an integration or applications engineering role.
  • 2+ years of experience working in a startup environment.
  • Strong technical background in software engineering.
  • Strong proficiency in modern C++.
  • Intermediate proficiency in Python.
  • Experience developing or integrating software for maritime platforms, marine robotics, or autonomous vessel systems.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

• Experience in the defense maritime or marine robotics industry.
  • Familiarity with maritime navigation, vessel control, collision avoidance, or maritime sensors such as radar, AIS, and sonar.
  • Experience supporting autonomous vessel demonstrations or sea trials.
  • Experience building and running a small enterprise software applications or solutions engineering team.
  • Advanced technical degree, especially in robotics or autonomy-related fields.

description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

This position is ideal for an individual who thrives on solving complex integration challenges that span hardware, software, and systems engineering. A successful candidate will be skilled at deploying autonomy solutions onto unmanned platforms, preparing systems for flight, and troubleshooting mission-critical issues in both lab and field environments.
 
The role is highly dynamic, requiring hands-on experience, strong systems thinking, and the ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, real-world test conditions. Our Flight Integration Engineers are essential to bridging the gap between R&D and deployment, ensuring that autonomous systems function reliably and effectively when and where they are needed most.

lists.content:
• System Integration & Deployment — Integrate autonomy software onto unmanned aircraft systems, ensuring seamless operation across onboard compute, sensors, and control interfaces.
  • Pre-flight Preparation — Own the build, configuration, and validation process for flight-ready systems; coordinate hardware/software compatibility and mission readiness.
  • On-site Flight Test Support — Travel to test sites and support live flight operations, including safety checks, system bring-up, and troubleshooting under time-critical constraints.
  • Hardware/Software Debugging — Diagnose and resolve integration issues across complex autonomy software stacks and embedded systems in lab and field environments.
  • Flight Data Capture & Analysis — Manage data collection during missions and post-test analysis, working with autonomy engineers to refine behaviors and identify improvements.
  • Collaboration Across Teams — Work closely with autonomy, GNC, systems, and test teams to ensure mission-critical functionality is delivered on time and validated thoroughly.
  • Continuous Improvement — Build tools and processes to improve integration timelines, flight test reliability, and team efficiency across deployment cycles.
  • Support Certification and Compliance — Assist with documentation and system-level validation required for certification, airworthiness, and compliance in defense-relevant environments. 
  • Travel Requirement – Members of this team typically travel around 30-40% of the year (to different office locations, customer sites, and flight integration events).

• BS/MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, and/or similar degree, or equivalent practical experience. 
  • Typically requires a minimum of 7 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 5 years and a Master’s degree; or 4 years with a PhD; or equivalent work experience. 
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as C++ and Python, and familiarity with real-time operating systems (RTOS).
  • Proficiency in Linux-based development and experience working with embedded systems, shell scripting, and system diagnostics. 
  • Knowledge of sensor integration, sensor fusion, and middleware frameworks (e.g., ROS, DDS).
  • Hands-on experience supporting flight demos or live exercises. 
  • Experience with simulation tools and environments for testing and validation.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot and optimize system performance.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work effectively in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment.

• Direct experience supporting unmanned aerial systems or similar flight test campaigns.
  • Familiarity with autonomy stacks, flight control systems, or GNC pipelines.
  • Competence in sensor integration, electronics debugging, or avionics bring-up.
  • Proficiency in developing automation tools for system testing, logging, and data parsing.
  • Comfortable interfacing with DoD stakeholders during field events or technical reviews.
  • Experience with UCI and OMS Standards.

Job Description:
Shield AI is seeking a high-performing Business Development / Account Executive to drive growth for Hivemind Autonomy across the Netherlands, with a primary focus on defense and government customers. 
This role is responsible for identifying, shaping, and closing complex opportunities while building enduring customer relationships and executing disciplined capture strategies. You will partner closely with Sales Leadership, Product, Engineering, and Strategic Engagement teams to align customer needs with Hivemind’s autonomy capabilities and deliver mission-critical outcomes. 
The ideal candidate is a customer-first, technically credible seller with strong capture instincts, experience navigating defence acquisition processes, and a proven track record of winning and expanding strategic accounts.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a high-performing Business Development / Account Executive to drive growth for Hivemind Autonomy across the Netherlands, with a primary focus on defense and government customers. 

This role is responsible for identifying, shaping, and closing complex opportunities while building enduring customer relationships and executing disciplined capture strategies. You will partner closely with Sales Leadership, Product, Engineering, and Strategic Engagement teams to align customer needs with Hivemind’s autonomy capabilities and deliver mission-critical outcomes. 

The ideal candidate is a customer-first, technically credible seller with strong capture instincts, experience navigating defence acquisition processes, and a proven track record of winning and expanding strategic accounts.

lists.content:
• Own and drive the full sales lifecycle for Hivemind opportunities across assigned accounts/territories (pipeline generation through close) 
  • Develop and execute territory and capture strategies for priority pursuits, aligning with Shield AI’s long-term strategic plan 
  • Identify, qualify, and shape new business opportunities through deep understanding of customer missions, budgets, and acquisition pathways 
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key decision-makers, program offices, and influencers across defense and government customers 
  • Lead proposal development in partnership with BD Operations and cross-functional teams, ensuring alignment with customer requirements and value propositions 
  • Conduct competitive analysis and position Hivemind effectively in complex, multi-stakeholder environments 
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Solutions teams to translate customer needs into compelling technical and operational solutions 
  • Manage deal progression with rigour (qualification, deal strategy, forecasting accuracy, CRM hygiene) 
  • Represent Shield AI at industry events, conferences, and customer engagements to expand market presence and pipeline 
  • Communicate clearly with internal stakeholders and leadership on pipeline status, risks, and key milestones

• Strong pipeline generation and progression within assigned accounts and territories 
  • Successful execution of capture strategies resulting in qualified opportunities and wins 
  • Improved deal velocity and win rates through disciplined qualification and positioning 
  • Establishment of trusted relationships with key customer stakeholders and partners 
  • Consistent, accurate forecasting and high-quality CRM and pipeline hygiene 
  • Meaningful contribution to revenue growth across the Hivemind business

• 10–15+ years of experience in business development, sales, or capture roles in technically complex domains (AI/ML, autonomy, SaaS, aerospace/defence, or similar) 
  • Proven track record of owning and closing deals, particularly within European government or defence markets 
  • Deep understanding of defence acquisition processes and government procurement lifecycle 
  • Strong experience developing and executing capture strategies for complex opportunities 
  • Technical aptitude and ability to engage credibly with Engineering, Product, and Operational stakeholders 
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills 
  • Self-motivated, results-oriented, and capable of operating in a fast-paced environment 
  • Bachelor’s degree required

• Experience selling autonomy, AI/ML, or unmanned systems (UAS) solutions  
  • Prior military experience a plus 
  • Established relationships within defense, government, or aerospace customer sets 
  • Experience working with Large Systems Integrators (LSIs) and strategic partners 
  • Ability to travel as needed for customer engagements and industry events 
  • Active or eligibility for security clearance 
  • MBA or equivalent graduate degree

Job Description:
Shield AI is seeking a high-performing Business Development Lead to drive defence market growth, customer engagement, and business expansion across assigned markets in Italy. As Shield AI’s territory leader, this individual will represent Shield AI’s autonomy and aircraft portfolio, including V-BAT, X-BAT, ViDAR-enabled ISR capabilities, and Hivemind autonomy software across customer engagements, operational demonstrations, strategic partnerships, opportunity development, and business growth initiatives.
The Business Development Lead owns territory strategy, pipeline development, account growth, and opportunity execution across Italy, driving opportunities from early shaping through award and expansion. This role combines strategic business development, account leadership, and revenue generation in a fast-paced international defence environment. Additionally, this person will carry a sales quota for their assigned territory.
The ideal candidate is a customer-focused and technically credible leader with strong commercial instincts, experience navigating defence acquisition environments, and a proven track record of growing strategic accounts and delivering mission-critical outcomes.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a high-performing Business Development Lead to drive defence market growth, customer engagement, and business expansion across assigned markets in Italy. As Shield AI’s territory leader, this individual will represent Shield AI’s autonomy and aircraft portfolio, including V-BAT, X-BAT, ViDAR-enabled ISR capabilities, and Hivemind autonomy software across customer engagements, operational demonstrations, strategic partnerships, opportunity development, and business growth initiatives.

The Business Development Lead owns territory strategy, pipeline development, account growth, and opportunity execution across Italy, driving opportunities from early shaping through award and expansion. This role combines strategic business development, account leadership, and revenue generation in a fast-paced international defence environment. Additionally, this person will carry a sales quota for their assigned territory.

The ideal candidate is a customer-focused and technically credible leader with strong commercial instincts, experience navigating defence acquisition environments, and a proven track record of growing strategic accounts and delivering mission-critical outcomes.

lists.content:
• Own and execute Shield AI’s go-to-market strategy across assigned markets, aligning territory activities with strategic growth priorities and customer mission requirements.  
  • Build and grow a disciplined pipeline across autonomy, aircraft, ISR, and mission-system opportunities aligned with regional defence priorities.  
  • Lead end-to-end deal closure, including account planning, customer shaping, competitive positioning, proposal leadership, negotiation, and contract close to meet or exceed carried sales quota. 
  • Engage directly with senior military leaders, Ministries of Defence, procurement authorities, sovereign stakeholders, and strategic industry partners across the territory.  
  • Represent and differentiate Shield AI’s autonomy and aircraft portfolio by clearly articulating mission outcomes, operational advantages, and integration pathways.  
  • Develop and manage regional partnerships, consultants, industrial participation structures, and offset-aligned strategies that expand market access and accelerate execution.  
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams across Business Development, Product, Engineering, Government Relations, Legal, Contracts, Export Compliance, Operations, and Customer teams to support successful capture and delivery.  
  • Maintain disciplined forecasting, pipeline management, opportunity tracking, and campaign reporting across the territory.  
  • Provide regional market intelligence on competitor dynamics, customer demand, and political or operational risks.  
  • Support executive customer engagement after award to support customer success, follow-on growth, and long-term account expansion.

• Typically requires 6+ years of experience in business development, capture, sales, strategic engagement, account management, or related customer-facing roles within defence, aerospace, national security, or advanced technology environments.  
  • Demonstrated success identifying, shaping, and advancing complex opportunities involving long sales cycles, senior stakeholders, and technically differentiated solutions.  
  • Strong executive presence and ability to build credibility with military, government, industry, and strategic partner stakeholders.  
  • Strong communication, negotiation, stakeholder management, and cross-functional collaboration skills.  
  • Fluency in English and regional languages relevant to the assigned market.  
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional, military, or operational experience preferred.

• Previous experience working in a consultancy environment is highly desirable, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders, navigate complex client requirements, and deliver solutions in a fast-paced, project-driven setting.
  • Experience with UAS, autonomy, ISR, mission systems, aerospace, or AI-enabled operational capabilities.  
  • Existing relationships across defence ministries, military organizations, procurement authorities, or strategic industry partners within the assigned territory.  
  • Experience supporting direct commercial sales, Foreign Military Sales (FMS), or international government procurement programs.  
  • Prior military, operational defence, government, or national security experience.

• Help build the defining defence technology company of this century.  
  • Work at the forefront of AI, autonomy, and next-generation defence systems.  
  • Operate in a highly entrepreneurial and mission-driven environment.  
  • Make a direct impact on international growth and strategic defence partnerships.  
  • Collaborate with exceptional teams solving some of the world’s most complex operational challenges.

lists.content:

  • Engage directly with senior military leaders, Ministries of Defence, procurement authorities, sovereign stakeholders, and strategic industry partners across the territory.  
  • Represent and differentiate Shield AI’s autonomy and aircraft portfolio by clearly articulating mission outcomes, operational advantages, and integration pathways.

  • Maintain disciplined forecasting, pipeline management, opportunity tracking, and campaign reporting across the territory.

• Typically requires 6+ years of experience in business development, capture, sales, strategic engagement, account management, or related customer-facing roles within defence, aerospace, national security, or advanced technology environments.

Job Description:
Shield AI is seeking a Senior Engineer to help design and develop the middleware framework upon which Shield AI autonomy is developed. As part of the Hivemind Foundations team, you’ll focus on building the high-performant, reliable, and robust foundational layer of the Hivemind SDK, EdgeOS. The Hivemind Foundations team ensures that autonomous systems have the functionality required to deploy to platforms operating in some of the most restrictive and demanding environments around the world. They also create the tools that enable autonomy engineers develop, understand, debug, and rapidly iterate on complex autonomous systems.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Senior Engineer to help design and develop the middleware framework upon which Shield AI autonomy is developed. As part of the Hivemind Foundations team, you’ll focus on building the high-performant, reliable, and robust foundational layer of the Hivemind SDK, EdgeOS. The Hivemind Foundations team ensures that autonomous systems have the functionality required to deploy to platforms operating in some of the most restrictive and demanding environments around the world. They also create the tools that enable autonomy engineers develop, understand, debug, and rapidly iterate on complex autonomous systems.

lists.content:
• Own the architecture and implementation of features critical to EdgeOS and EdgeOS RT middleware. 
  • Develop runtime services and abstractions that operate across Linux, real-time operating system, and resource-constrained computing platforms. 
  • Design and develop the tooling used to evaluate, observe, and debug autonomous systems. 
  • Contribute to and extend EdgeOS Language, Hivemind’s interface definition language, which defines how data is represented within autonomous systems, between agents, and with third-party systems. 
  • Collaborate closely with autonomy, systems, simulation, and test engineers to deliver capabilities from initial design to integration. 
  • Raise the engineering bar though design and code reviews, technical guidance, documentation, and mentorship.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
  • Typically requires a minimum of 7 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 6 years with a Master’s; or 4 years with a PhD; or equivalent work experience. 
  • Strong proficiency in C++11 or newer in a production environment. 
  • Experience designing, developing, and debugging multithreaded systems. 
  • Experience developing software for real time operating systems and embedded platforms. 
  • Strong understanding of systems programming concepts, including concurrency, memory management, resource constraints, and performance optimization. 
  • Experience writing automated tests and clear technical documentation.

• Experience with C++17 or newer standards. 
  • Experience writing MISRA C++ or comparable coding standards for safety-critical or airborne systems. 
  • Experience with systems engineering design principles and requirements. 
  • Experience software assurance frameworks such as DO-178C. 
  • Familiarity with ROS2 or similar robotics frameworks. 
  • Experience with interface definition languages, serialization systems, or code-generation tooling. 
  • Knowledge of CMake and Nix build systems. 
  • Experience profiling and debugging complex software across multiple hardware and operating-system environments.

Job Description:

Come join a fast-growing team in a strategically important market to shape stories around the cutting-edge technologies that underpin Shield AI's mission: protecting service members and civilians through intelligent systems and sovereign autonomy. In this role, you will lead media relations and communications initiatives for Shield AI in Australia, building the company's reputation as a trusted, locally capable and long-term defence technology partner.

Australia is home to Shield AI Australia and its Melbourne-based engineering capability. You will help translate the substance of that local presence—including Australian engineering expertise, sensing and situational-awareness technologies, autonomy software, and collaboration with Australian defence and industry stakeholders—into credible, sustained external communications.

Working closely with the Regional Communications Lead for Asia and the Middle East, Global Communications, Australia business development, government relations, engineering, and cross-functional teams, you will support strategic business priorities and shape narratives around consequential technologies changing the defence landscape. You will serve as the in-country communications owner for Australia while connecting local proof points to Shield AI's global mission and regional growth strategy.

lists.content:
Earned media and press strategy
  • Own and grow Shield AI's earned-media footprint in Australia, building trusted relationships with defence, aerospace, national-security, technology, business and policy journalists.
  • Develop and execute proactive media strategies tied to product and technology milestones, customer and partner activity, local engineering and workforce developments, and major defence exhibitions and events.
  • Identify and create high-quality opportunities for Shield AI executives, technical leaders and subject-matter experts to participate in interviews, briefings, contributed articles and other earned speaking engagements.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for Australian media inquiries, coordinating sensitive, reactive and issues communications with regional and global teams.
  • Prepare spokespeople for interviews, media briefings and public engagements; manage press logistics and on-site media operations.
  • Monitor news, defence-policy developments, industry trends and competitor activity to identify opportunities, risks and emerging narratives relevant to Shield AI.
    • Content development and storytelling
  • Develop and edit Australia-focused communications materials, including press releases, bylines, executive talking points, speeches, briefing documents, media pitches, customer-safe case studies and internal communications.
  • Build a repeatable local storytelling pipeline around Australian engineering, mission autonomy, AI-enabled sensing, resilient ISR, trusted local capability and allied interoperability.
  • Translate complex technical concepts into concise, accurate and compelling narratives for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Localise global Shield AI messaging for Australian stakeholder priorities and public-policy context while maintaining consistency with the core brand and mission.
  • Work with technical, programme, business-development and government-relations colleagues to validate claims, capture proof points and ensure disciplined external messaging.
    • Narrative, reputation and stakeholder positioning
  • Shape and protect Shield AI's reputation as a credible, consistent and long-term contributor to Australia's defence and national-security ecosystem.
  • Build a sustained drumbeat of earned visibility that demonstrates Shield AI's commitment to Australia through local talent, engineering, technology development and collaboration with Australian industry and defence stakeholders.
  • Help differentiate Shield AI's local capability and technology leadership in a competitive discussion around sovereign autonomy, AI, sensing and future warfare.
  • Anticipate and help manage narrative risk, including questions related to foreign ownership, sovereign capability, defence procurement, AI assurance and geopolitical sensitivities.
  • Partner closely with Australia business development and government relations teams to ensure communications activity supports stakeholder engagement while maintaining appropriate independence and credibility with media.
    • Events and regional coordination
  • Lead communications planning and execution for priority Australian events, including Land Forces, Avalon Airshow and other relevant defence, aerospace, technology and policy engagements.
  • Develop integrated event communications plans covering narrative development, media targets, executive programmes, press materials, interview scheduling, on-site management and post-event follow-up.
  • Coordinate with the Asia and Middle East regional team on overlapping executive visits, partner announcements and major communications moments.
  • Manage external agencies, freelancers and suppliers where appropriate, setting clear scopes, standards, reporting and performance expectations.
  • Travel within Australia and periodically across the Asia-Pacific region as business needs require.

• 8+ years of communications experience, including meaningful experience in defence, aerospace, national security, government, technology or other complex B2G sectors. A mix of in-house and agency experience is welcome.
  • Bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, public relations, political science, international relations, marketing or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong track record of securing high-quality earned media coverage in Australia, with established relationships across relevant defence, aerospace, business, technology and/or policy media.
  • Demonstrated experience developing communications strategies and executing programmes around major announcements, partnerships, events and executive visibility.·       Exceptional written and verbal storytelling skills, sound editorial judgement and close attention to detail.
  • Experience drafting and editing press releases, media materials, executive briefing documents, speeches, talking points and thought-leadership content.
  • Familiarity with Australian defence-industry dynamics, government and stakeholder sensitivities, and public discussions around sovereign capability, advanced technology and national security.
  • Ability to simplify complex technical concepts accurately for non-technical and technical audiences alike.
  • Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to identify opportunities for brand enhancement while assessing potential reputational and issues risks.
  • Experience working across cross-functional and cross-cultural teams, including technical leaders, business development, government relations, external partners and senior executives.
  • Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy and manage multiple projects, deadlines and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
  • Interest in AI, autonomy, uncrewed systems, sensing and defence technology.
    • Note: This role is based in Melbourne, Australia, with regular domestic travel and periodic regional travel.

• Establish Shield AI as a recognized and trusted defence-technology voice in Australia—consistently featured, quoted and referenced in relevant media conversations on mission autonomy, AI-enabled sensing, resilient ISR and future defence capability.
  • Position Australia-based and visiting Shield AI leaders as credible, informed voices in earned media, industry and policy conversations.
  • Build a sustained, proactive earned-media programme that demonstrates Shield AI's long-term commitment and local contribution, rather than relying solely on news-driven announcements.
  • Develop a repeatable Australia storytelling engine that turns local engineering, technology, workforce, customer-safe programme and partnership proof points into high-quality external content.
  • Deliver disciplined, effective communications programmes around Land Forces, Avalon Airshow and other priority Australian engagements.
  • Strengthen relationships with priority Australian journalists, editors, analysts and industry influencers so Shield AI can earn informed, accurate and high-quality coverage over time.
  • Reduce reliance on regional leadership for day-to-day Australian communications execution while maintaining close alignment with regional strategy, global messaging and senior stakeholder priorities.

As one of the first Component Engineers at Shield AI, you'll be a foundational hire building the function from the ground up — defining process, tooling, and standards, not just executing an existing playbook. lists.content:
• Establish and scale Component Engineering processes, tools, and standards as one of the function's first dedicated hires
  • Define baseline quality and certification requirements for EEE components across the XBAT aircraft
  • Qualify and up-screen EEE components for use in aerospace applications, driving environmental and bench-top testing.
  • Own component data and governance in PLM and the ECAD part library, including lifecycle status and approved vendor list
  • Contribute to component failure analysis and root cause efforts
  • Monitor and assess PCNs and lifecycle changes (NRND/EOL), and drive mitigation actions
  • Support supply chain with alternate part evaluations and second-sourcing strategies
  • Engage directly with suppliers to resolve technical questions

• B.S. in an engineering, physics or materials science
  • 5+ years of relevant experience
  • Deep knowledge of EEE components
  • Understanding of Product Lifecycle Management, ECAD tools and structured component libraries
  • Strong judgment in balancing performance, cost and supply chain risk
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical discussions and influence design decisions across engineering, supply chain, and program teams — including in ambiguous, fast-moving environments without an established playbook

• Experience building or scaling a component engineering function in a startup or fast-growth environment
  • Familiar with industry-standard component qualification process (AEC-Q, NASA, JEDEC, MIL, etc)
  • Knowledge of electrical component manufacturing processes and common failure modes
  • Experience writing specifications/standards for internal company distribution

descriptionPlain:
The DevSecOps Engineer at Shield AI is responsible for designing, building, securing, and operating the software delivery infrastructure required to develop and deploy advanced autonomous systems for defence applications.

This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, platform engineering, cyber security, and defence systems engineering. The DevSecOps Engineer works alongside autonomy, software, systems, integration, and test engineers to create secure and reliable development environments and delivery pipelines that enable teams to rapidly develop, integrate, test, and deploy mission critical software.

The ideal candidate has a strong software and platform engineering background combined with significant experience operating within UK defence environments. They have a strong understanding of the UK Ministry of Defence/NATO approach to DevSecOps, Secure by Design, cyber risk management, security assurance, and the delivery of software into classified and operational environments.
description:
The DevSecOps Engineer at Shield AI is responsible for designing, building, securing, and operating the software delivery infrastructure required to develop and deploy advanced autonomous systems for defence applications.

This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, platform engineering, cyber security, and defence systems engineering. The DevSecOps Engineer works alongside autonomy, software, systems, integration, and test engineers to create secure and reliable development environments and delivery pipelines that enable teams to rapidly develop, integrate, test, and deploy mission critical software.

The ideal candidate has a strong software and platform engineering background combined with significant experience operating within UK defence environments. They have a strong understanding of the UK Ministry of Defence/NATO approach to DevSecOps, Secure by Design, cyber risk management, security assurance, and the delivery of software into classified and operational environments.

lists.content:
• Design, build, and operate secure development and deployment infrastructure for Shield AI autonomy and defence programmes.
  • Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines that enable rapid, repeatable, and secure delivery of autonomy and mission software.
  • Embed security throughout the software development lifecycle, ensuring security controls, testing, evidence, and assurance are integrated into engineering workflows rather than treated as separate activities.
  • Apply UK MOD Secure by Design principles throughout the development lifecycle and help engineering teams understand and meet their responsibilities for cyber security and technical assurance.
  • Work closely with software, autonomy, systems, cyber security, integration, and test engineers to establish development environments that support rapid engineering while meeting defence security requirements.
  • Design and maintain development and deployment environments spanning cloud, on premises infrastructure, laboratory environments, simulation, hardware in the loop, and operational platforms.
  • Enable secure software development and deployment across different security classifications and appropriately segmented development environments.
  • Implement automated security controls within CI/CD pipelines, including static analysis, dependency scanning, container scanning, secrets detection, software composition analysis, vulnerability management, and policy enforcement.
  • Champion a DevSecOps culture where software engineers take ownership of the security, reliability, deployability, and operational performance of the systems they develop.

• BS or MS in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Cyber Security, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in DevOps, DevSecOps, platform engineering, site reliability engineering, software engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Significant experience delivering software or digital capabilities within UK defence or another highly regulated national security environment.
  • Strong understanding of the UK Ministry of Defence/NATO approach to DevSecOps and Secure by Design, including the integration of cyber security and risk management throughout the capability lifecycle.
  • Experience applying MOD security policies, security assurance processes, and technical security requirements to software intensive defence programmes.
  • Experience developing and operating CI/CD pipelines using modern source control, build, test, artefact management, and deployment technologies.
  • Strong understanding of Infrastructure as Code, configuration management, containerisation, and infrastructure automation
  • Experience with technologies such as Git, GitLab or GitHub, or equivalent tooling.

• Experience supporting DevSecOps, software delivery, or digital engineering activities across NATO nations or multinational defence programmes.
  • Understanding of DevSecOps approaches, security frameworks, and software assurance practices used by other NATO nations, particularly the United States and European NATO partners.

Job Description:
Shield AI’s International Business & Strategy team is hiring a Senior Director Business Development to accelerate growth and support the adoption of its autonomy ecosystem: X-BAT, V-BAT, ViDAR, and Hivemind across Japan, South Korea and Taiwan
The Senior Director of Business Development will lead Shield AI’s regional growth strategy, building out a team that is responsible for significant annual orders targets. The leader must have deep defense, national security, or aerospace experience in the country / region (Japanese language fluency preferable), established government relationships, and a track record of closing complex defense programs (ideally across both hardware and software).  
You will operate with significant autonomy and ownership, shaping country strategy, leading major pursuits, and building long-term defense partnerships. You will report to the Vice President of International Business & Strategy (Middle East & Asia Pacific) and work closely with international business development colleagues around the globe, as well as product, engineering, and operations teams, to deliver mission-relevant autonomy capabilities at scale.

lists.content:
• Own and execute regional (Japan/South Korea/Taiwan) go-to-market strategy for Shield AI’s product portfolio, including X-BAT, V-BAT, ViDAR, and Hivemind.  
  • Maintain direct responsibility for annual order targets, multi-year pipeline development, and order growth.  
  • Lead end-to-end capture and sales efforts from early engagement through contract award and follow-on growth.  
  • Engage directly with senior military, government, and defense industry stakeholders across the region.  
  • Differentiate Shield AI in competitive and regulated defense procurements.  
  • Provide actionable market and customer intelligence to influence product roadmap and broader international strategy.  
  • Work cross-functionally with product, legal, export compliance, and operations.  
  • Lead proposal/program development and complex product demonstrations.  
  • Structure and manage local partnerships, primes, and industrial participation or offset strategies.  
  • Represent Shield AI at senior-level engagements, exhibitions, and industry forums.

• 10+ years business development experience in the country or broader region within defense, aerospace, or national security.  
  • Specific prior defense or government-facing experience in Japan/South Korea/Taiwan with a deep understanding of procurement processes, offset requirements, export sensitivities, local defense primes, and indigenization requirements.  
  • Fluency in English & Japanese preferable (written and spoken).  
  • Demonstrated success closing complex defense or government programs - ideally across both hardware (aircraft/UAS) and software (autonomy/ai).  
  • Technical experience with autonomy, UAVs, ISR, and advanced sensing technologies.  
  • Strong negotiation, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills.  
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent pursuits, involving technical products, in ambiguous environments.  
  • Proven cross-functional leadership across operations, product, and BD teams.  
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills.  
  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently in country/region and internationally   
  • Willingness and ability to work across multiple time zones  
  • Based today in Tokyo, Japan. 
  • Mastery of critical business tools (Microsoft Suite – PPT, Excel, Word, LLMs, etc.)  
  • Experience forecasting, tracking, and managing deal cycles using Salesforce.

• Existing U.S. or allied security clearance.  
  • Prior military service or operational leadership experience in Japan 
    (++ if directly related to UAS, autonomy, or fighter jet aircraft).  
  • Prior experience supporting foreign military sales (via DSCA), engaging with SAF/IA, or working directly with foreign air forces.  
  • Direct experience with UAV operations, mission autonomy, AI-enabled C2 systems.

Job Description:

The Head of Deal Strategy and Execution (DSE) owns the operating model that turns Shield AI’s most complex, highest-value domestic and international opportunities into repeatable, executable transactions. This is not a traditional deal desk. It is a strategic deal architecture and execution function: a force multiplier for the field that helps teams build winning deal structures, terms, and negotiation approaches faster, accelerate cross-functional decisions, protect margin and risk posture, and convert successful one-off transactions into reusable plays. 

The role exists because Shield AI’s opportunity set is increasingly defined by complex government and international transactions where a product sale alone is insufficient. Customers require combinations of autonomous platforms, software subscriptions, payloads, training, field services, integration, sustainment, and partner-led delivery. Each transaction introduces unique constraints around product maturity, delivery capacity, exportability, contracting pathway, pricing, and risk, and the company needs a single operating mechanism that translates all of it into viable, approvable, and scalable transactions. 

This is a leadership role. The Head of DSE builds and directs three functions: Regional Deal Strategists embedded with BD teams, a central Business Proposals function, and an Architecture and Packaging capability. The constant is the operating principle: standardize what can be standardized, and elevate and deliberately govern what must be bespoke.

lists.content:
• Team charter and operating model. Set engagement criteria, service levels, decision rights, approval thresholds, and the escalation framework. Define when DSE engages: a priority or non-standard opportunity involving complex configuration, international scope, a partner-led construct, a packaged offering, or an exception request. 
  • Cross-functional deal governance. Chair cross-functional deal reviews and ensure executives receive clear decisions, trade-offs, and recommendations. Convene BD Ops, Sales, Product, Finance, Legal, Contracts, Delivery, and Partnerships around a structured process rather than disconnected approval gates. 
  • Strategic deal architecture. Own the quality of deal strategy on priority pursuits: customer value hypothesis, solution configuration, commercial construct, pricing posture, terms, partner path, negotiation approach, and close plan. Challenge weak qualification and help account teams exit or reframe low-probability pursuits. 
  • Modular deal catalog and packaging. Direct the build and maintenance of the authoritative capability catalog: approved configurations, modular bundles, eligibility criteria, deployment assumptions, exclusions, dependencies, pricing guardrails, discount and volume logic, and delivery handoffs across hardware, software, subscriptions, services, training, sustainment, and integration. 
  • Deal plays and repeatability. Establish the deal-play roadmap aligned to GTM priorities, product maturity, and international growth. Turn wins, losses, and delivery outcomes into qualification tools, discovery guides, value narratives, proposal modules, negotiation guidance, and win-wire content the field can reuse in the flow of work. 
  • Exception governance. Govern pricing, terms, and delivery exceptions through clear thresholds and fast escalation, not bureaucracy. Serve as the escalation point for deal strategy conflict, cross-functional ambiguity, and strategic exceptions. 
  • Measurement and continuous improvement. Measure business impact: cycle time, deal velocity, win rate on strategic pursuits, gross-margin protection, exception volume, reuse rate, and delivery outcomes. Lead postmortems on won and lost strategic business and feed the lessons back into the pre-sales motion. 
  • Team leadership and role boundaries. Build and lead Regional Deal Strategists, the Business Proposals team, and the Architecture and Packaging function. Hold the line on the boundary that matters most: the Regional Deal Strategist owns the deal, and the Proposal Manager owns the submission. 
  • Enablement and incentives. Partner with the GTM Enablement Lead on trainings and enablement, and work with Rev Ops and Business Ops on buying-program and product and deal-structure related SPIFFs.

• The agenda below reflects the founding priorities. Expect it to evolve as the organization matures. 
  • Stand up the organization. Charter, engagement criteria, decision rights, escalation paths, and service levels, published so the field knows when and how to engage DSE. 
  • Deal intake and triage. A structured intake that captures customer mission, use case, configuration, value, funding, timeline, procurement path, geography, export considerations, partners, delivery needs, and requested exceptions early, before heavy internal resources are committed. 
  • Modular capability catalog. Standard configurations and modular bundles across products, subscriptions, hardware, services, training, sustainment, integration, and partner components, with eligibility criteria, deployment assumptions, exclusions, and handoff requirements. 
  • Deal plays for priority segments. Repeatable plays for priority customer segments, use cases, geographies, routes to market, and partner motions, with approved pricing guidance and negotiation positions. 
  • Pre-sales inspection. Premortem discipline in the form of Opportunity Reviews and Management Reviews, with DSE review and approval prior to formal MRs. 
  • Post-deal learning. Postmortems on wins, losses, and delivery outcomes that feed back into product packaging, pricing, playbooks, training, and governance.

• Advisory, not administrative. The team shapes stronger deals; it does not merely route requests for signatures. A desk that only passes work to executives fails to create speed or leverage. 
  • Clear guardrails. Publish price floors, discount bands, authority limits, eligibility rules, standard terms, and escalation triggers. Decisions within established guardrails are delegated; true strategic exceptions are escalated with a concise recommendation, alternatives, and quantified trade-offs. 
  • Speed by design. Service-level expectations with most standard reviews resolved same day or next business day. Urgency is governed by intake quality, not informal escalation. 
  • One source of truth. Centralize product and package definitions, deal-structure precedents, templates, approval outcomes, and lessons learned in a searchable repository, usable in the flow of work: inside CRM, opportunity reviews, proposal workflows, and account planning. 
  • Cross-functional accountability. Functional experts retain their authorities. DSE owns orchestration, deal-strategy coherence, pace, and knowledge capture. 
  • Decision rights. The role owns the recommendation and the orchestration. The CRO owns the strategic decision. Account teams own the customer relationship and the close. 
  • Measurement. The organization is evaluated on velocity, economics, execution quality, and reuse, not merely the number of tickets processed.

  • 10+ years in revenue, commercial, or deal or sales leadership roles in B2B technology, with material time structuring complex, mixed software and hardware transactions. 
  • Demonstrated experience building or leading a deal desk, deal strategy, or commercial structuring function, and elevating it from an approval queue into a strategic capability. 
  • Deep familiarity with international government contracting, international sales, and partner-led motions. Comfort with export considerations, contracting pathways, long cycles, complex stakeholders, and program-driven buyers is required.

  • Deal architect. Thinks in commercial constructs, pricing logic, and negotiation posture, and translates technical capability into viable, approvable transactions. 
  • Cross-functional orchestrator. Aligns sales, finance, legal, product, and delivery around decisions without claiming their authority. 
  • Negotiation craft. Has personally shaped and negotiated high-value, non-standard transactions to close. 
  • Writes well. Produces executive-ready deal briefs, decision memos, and value narratives that compress complexity without losing it. 
  • Standardizer by instinct. Converts one-off wins into reusable plays, templates, and guardrails. 
  • Calibrated on the line between governing exceptions and adding bureaucracy. Stays on the governance side.
